“Sangat sulit,” kata pria yang duduk di hadapanku. “Kami sudah menikah hampir lima puluh tahun, tetapi aku tidak pernah mengira akan seperti ini.”

“Apa yang sedang terjadi?” aku bertanya kepada Al dengan penuh empati.

“Ini tentang Lisa,” katanya. “Kau tahu ingatannya sudah menurun sejak beberapa waktu. Nah, kami pergi ke neurolog seperti yang kau sarankan, dan mereka memerintahkan serangkaian tes dan semacam pemindaian otak. Lalu, mereka memberi tahu dia bahwa dia menderita demensia.”

“Kupikir itulah yang sedang terjadi,” jawabku.

“Aku tahu kau sudah memberi tahu kami itu,” kata Al. “Nah, ada saat-saat dia tidak mengenaliku. Dia menatapku hampa seolah-olah bertanya siapa orang asing gila yang masuk ke rumahnya.”

“Itu pasti sangat berat,” kataku.

“Satu-satunya hal yang membuatnya kembali seperti dirinya adalah pergi ke luar dan meneleponnya dengan ponsel. Kukatakan padanya keluar ke garasi, aku punya sesuatu untuk ditunjukkan. Entah bagaimana ketika aku melakukan itu, itu membawanya kembali ke masa sekarang dan membuatnya tahu siapa aku – setidaknya untuk sedikit waktu.”

Kami melanjutkan pembicaraan tentang hal-hal lain, tetapi aku bisa melihat bahwa hati Al sedang hancur. Istrinya yang sudah 48 tahun terlihat sama seperti biasa di luar, namun di dalam dia adalah orang yang benar-benar berbeda.

Aku ingin membahas beberapa tantangan dalam menghadapi demensia.

Demensia dalam Alkitab

Pengkhotbah 12:1-7 memberi gambaran yang agak suram tentang proses penuaan. “Remember now thy Creator in the days of thy youth, while the evil days come not, nor the years draw nigh, when thou shalt say, I have no pleasure in them; While the sun, or the light, or the moon, or the stars, be not darkened, nor the clouds return after the rain: In the day when the keepers of the house shall tremble, and the strong men shall bow themselves, and the grinders cease because they are few, and those that look out of the windows be darkened, And the doors shall be shut in the streets, when the sound of the grinding is low, and he shall rise up at the voice of the bird, and all the daughters of musick shall be brought low; Also when they shall be afraid of that which is high, and fears shall be in the way, and the almond tree shall flourish, and the grasshopper shall be a burden, and desire shall fail: because man goeth to his long home, and the mourners go about the streets: Or ever the silver cord be loosed, or the golden bowl be broken, or the pitcher be broken at the fountain, or the wheel broken at the cistern. Then shall the dust return to the earth as it was: and the spirit shall return unto God who gave it.”

Dalam bagian ini, gambaran puitis tampaknya berbicara tentang kehilangan gigi, hilangnya pendengaran, langkah yang tidak stabil, dan kelemahan umum. Sulit untuk mengatakan apakah gambaran-gambaran ini berbicara tentang kehilangan ingatan. Yang pasti adalah bahwa bagian ini dimulai dengan suatu perintah: “Remember!”

Ini bukan satu-satunya tempat dalam Kitab Suci di mana manusia diperintahkan untuk mengingat. Berulang kali, kita diberi tahu untuk mengingat Allah. Kita harus memastikan bahwa kita mengajarkan anak-anak kita tentang Dia. “And thou shalt teach them diligently unto thy children, and shalt talk of them when thou sittest in thine house, and when thou walkest by the way, and when thou liest down, and when thou risest up” (Deuteronomy 6:7).

Mungkin akan datang masa ketika kita tidak mampu lagi mengingat. Hal yang paling penting – bahkan saat kita memikirkan topik demensia – adalah agar kita mengingat Dia yang menjadikan kita dan mengikuti-Nya dengan segenap hati.

Apa itu Demensia

Demensia adalah setiap penyakit yang menyebabkan kehilangan ingatan, kemampuan bernalar, dan fungsi sosial. Kebanyakan orang berpikir terutama tentang kehilangan ingatan. Kurasa ini karena pada tahap awal penyakit orang lain memperhatikan hal-hal seperti kesulitan mencari kata-kata dan sering mengulang cerita.

Fungsi sosial seringkali tetap terjaga sampai tahap akhir penyakit. Jika Anda menanyakan kepada seseorang dengan demensia ringan apakah mereka tahu tanggal hari ini, kemungkinan besar mereka akan menjawab, “Oh, kau tahu, aku berhenti memperhatikan hal-hal seperti itu ketika aku pensiun.”

Penyebab paling umum demensia adalah demensia Alzheimer – setidaknya 70 persen orang yang mengalami kehilangan ingatan progresif menderita demensia Alzheimer. Alzheimer tampaknya terkait dengan protein yang disebut amiloid, yang terdeposit di otak dan mencegah sel saraf berkomunikasi satu sama lain.

Penyebab lain adalah demensia vaskular, di mana sumbatan di pembuluh darah otak menyebabkan kematian sel saraf. Demensia Lewy Body adalah semacam kehilangan ingatan yang terkait dengan Penyakit Parkinson. Sekitar delapan puluh persen orang dengan Penyakit Parkinson akhirnya akan mengembangkan demensia.

Mendiagnosis Demensia

Jika anggota keluarga curiga seseorang sedang mengembangkan kehilangan ingatan, hal terbaik adalah membawa mereka ke penyedia perawatan primer untuk evaluasi. Selain melakukan pemeriksaan fisik, dokter biasanya akan meminta pasien menggambar sebuah jam dan melakukan pemeriksaan status mental mini, yang meminta pasien menjawab banyak pertanyaan sederhana dan melakukan beberapa pengingatan jangka pendek terhadap item.

Tes darah termasuk kadar tiroid dan Vitamin B12 akan dilakukan. Pemindaian otak atau ultrasonografi pembuluh leher mungkin juga dilakukan.

Tujuannya adalah mengidentifikasi hal-hal yang dapat diobati dan menangani itu.

Hentikan Penggunaan Obat-obatan

Banyak obat meningkatkan risiko masalah ingatan. Seiring bertambahnya usia, berusaha menghindari obat-obatan ini membantu mencegah berkembangnya demensia.

Obat antikolinergik mungkin merupakan penyebab terbesar yang aku temui. Yang paling umum dari obat-obat ini adalah antihistamin lama seperti diphenhydramine (digunakan sebagai obat tidur atau pil alergi) dan doxylamine (digunakan sebagai obat tidur). Dalam sebuah studi, pasien yang mengonsumsi obat antikolinergik setara selama tiga tahun memiliki risiko demensia yang secara signifikan lebih tinggi dibandingkan pasien yang mengonsumsi obat-obatan semacam ini kurang dari tiga bulan.1 Obat depresi generasi lama juga dapat termasuk dalam kategori ini.

Obat kecemasan, yang disebut benzodiazepin, juga dikaitkan dengan masalah ingatan. Studi menunjukkan bahwa pasien yang mengonsumsi obat-obatan ini memiliki risiko lebih tinggi mengembangkan demensia dibandingkan pasien yang tidak mengonsumsinya.2

Obat kejang mungkin juga memperburuk kemampuan berpikir. Memiliki gangguan kejang tampaknya meningkatkan risiko demensia, tetapi obat-obatan tertentu yang lebih lama seperti valproate dan gabapentin tampaknya membuat orang tua lebih sulit berpikir jernih, dan beralih ke obat kejang dengan risiko lebih rendah dianjurkan (jika memungkinkan) untuk orang tua.

Ada kalanya seseorang perlu mengonsumsi obat, tetapi seiring bertambahnya usia pasien, penting untuk memikirkan risiko obat-obatan tersebut. Ada daftar obat yang paling bijaksana untuk dihindari bagi pasien berusia di atas 65 tahun, yang disebut Beers List. Mengganti dengan obat serupa yang memiliki efek samping lebih sedikit atau menggunakan dosis yang lebih rendah dianjurkan.3

Perawatan Medis

Aturan pertama dalam menangani demensia adalah memastikan bahwa semua hal metabolik berada dalam kendali sebaik mungkin. Jadi, jika seseorang menderita diabetes, yang terbaik adalah memastikan gula darah mereka terkendali sebaik mungkin. Jika seseorang memiliki tekanan darah tinggi, pastikan itu teratur dengan baik (ini terutama penting jika seseorang menderita demensia vaskular).

Ada beberapa kelas obat berbeda yang disetujui untuk mengobati demensia. Salah satunya adalah inhibitor kolinesterase. Obat-obatan ini meningkatkan kadar zat kimia yang disebut asetilkolin di otak dan sistem saraf perifer. Obat-obatan ini tentu bukan obat mujarab dan paling baik tampaknya memperlambat perkembangan kehilangan ingatan dan tidak benar-benar mengembalikan fungsi otak sebelumnya.

Obat lainnya disebut memantin. Obat ini bekerja dengan menarget reseptor glutamat di otak. Sama seperti inhibitor kolinesterase, efeknya tidak besar dan hasil akhirnya hanya memperlambat kehilangan ingatan.

Kedua obat ini berbentuk generik, dan masuk akal untuk mencobanya dan melihat bagaimana respons seseorang terhadapnya.

Satu obat terakhir yang perlu disebutkan adalah lecanemab. Ini adalah infus IV yang menarget amiloid, sejenis protein yang berkembang di otak orang dengan demensia Alzheimer. Obat ini tampaknya bekerja sangat baik dalam membersihkan amiloid dari otak pasien. Obat ini sangat mahal ($26,500 per tahun) dan telah dikaitkan dengan peningkatan stroke. Dalam studi, gejala demensia hanya diperlambat sekitar 30 persen dibandingkan dengan plasebo.

Tidak ada obat lain yang saat ini disetujui untuk mengobati demensia.

Terapi Non-obat

Ada beberapa hal yang dapat dilakukan orang untuk membantu memperlambat perkembangan demensia. Ini bisa membantu bagi orang yang memiliki riwayat keluarga kuat tentang demensia dan ingin mencegah timbulnya penyakit.

Latihan kardiovaskular sangat penting. Dokter menyebutkan olahraga terkait hampir setiap penyakit kronis karena telah terbukti efektif. Dalam kasus demensia, orang yang berolahraga secara teratur memiliki risiko sekitar 30 persen lebih rendah mengembangkan penyakit ini. Olahraga teratur tampaknya memperlambat perkembangan demensia.4

Mengerjakan teka-teki yang membutuhkan aktivitas mental, seperti Sudoku atau teka-teki silang tampaknya membantu memperlambat perkembangan kehilangan ingatan dan mungkin juga mengurangi kemungkinan mengembangkan demensia.

Terakhir, bermanfaat untuk mempelajari sesuatu yang baru. Orang yang mempelajari keterampilan baru atau fokus belajar bahasa baru sangat membantu ingatan mereka. Sebuah studi membandingkan orang tua yang mempelajari keterampilan baru dengan orang yang menghadiri acara sosial.

Intinya tampaknya otak kita perlu didorong untuk membuat jalur-jalur baru atau mereka cenderung rusak.5

Merawat Seseorang dengan Demensia

Merawat seseorang dengan demensia menantang dalam berbagai hal. Seringkali sulit menentukan seberapa banyak kemandirian yang boleh diberikan kepada orang tersebut. Sudah banyak buku yang ditulis tentang topik ini, tetapi ada beberapa hal yang layak disebutkan.

Penting untuk menghindari hal-hal berbahaya. Dua hal paling berbahaya bagi seseorang dengan ingatan yang terganggu adalah mengemudi dan memasak. Keduanya tampak biasa, dan orang tersebut mungkin terlihat baik-baik saja, tetapi keduanya bisa menjadi masalah sangat cepat.

Bahaya mengemudi mobil atau kendaraan bermesin dua arah bersifat dua sisi. Pertama, beberapa orang menjadi buntu pada titik-titik tertentu, tidak ingat bagaimana melakukan keterampilan tertentu. Ini bisa menjadi masalah, tidak hanya bagi mereka tetapi juga bagi orang lain di jalan.

Kedua, orang tua dapat memulai perjalanan singkat ke toko atau restoran lokal dan akhirnya tersesat. Aku pernah memiliki pasien yang berkeliling selama berjam-jam mencoba mencari jalan pulang ketika mereka menjadi bingung saat berkendara ke kota.

Memasak, tentu saja, pada dasarnya adalah masalah mengingat untuk mengatur timer dan mengambil sesuatu dari kompor atau oven pada waktu yang tepat.

Seringkali, orang dengan demensia tidak menyadari seberapa banyak kemampuan mereka telah menurun dan menolak gagasan bahwa mereka perlu menyerahkan kunci mobil. Mungkin ini semata-mata soal kehilangan kemandirian, tetapi sulit menghadapi kenyataan bahwa Anda tidak lagi aman di belakang kemudi.

Cobalah menjaga segala sesuatunya tetap sama di dalam kamar dan rumah. Bahkan perubahan kecil dalam susunan ruangan bisa cukup untuk mengacaukan situasi. Memindahkan seseorang dari rumah mereka – misalnya, memasukkan mereka ke rumah sakit seringkali membuat keadaan jauh lebih buruk. Tiba-tiba, kebingungan yang sebelumnya tampak ringan kini menjadi sangat tinggi.

Jika ada buah Roh yang menjadi kunci dalam berurusan dengan seseorang yang menderita demensia, itu adalah kesabaran. Tidak seorang pun dari kita memiliki kesabaran sebanyak yang kita butuhkan, karena demensia membuat kesabaran itu menipis.

Orang dengan demensia sering bertingkah seperti anak kecil dalam perjalanan panjang. Mereka bertanya berulang kali kapan mereka akan pulang. Mereka bertanya di mana kerabat yang sudah meninggal atau mengapa anak-anak belum pulang. Tidak ada penjelasan yang cukup membantu, karena hanya beberapa menit setelah mereka menanyakan pertanyaan itu, mereka telah melupakan jawabannya dan bertanya lagi.

Kemampuan mereka sering muncul dan menghilang. Suatu hari, mereka dapat mengancingkan bajunya, dan keesokan harinya, keterampilan itu tampaknya hilang. Mudah percaya bahwa mereka tidak “berusaha keras” dan bahwa mereka bisa lebih jika hanya mau berusaha.

Sayangnya, fakta bahwa seseorang dengan demensia bisa melakukan sesuatu kemarin tidak berarti mereka ingat bagaimana melakukannya hari ini. Marah kepada mereka hanya membuat hal-hal ini lebih buruk karena menambah kecemasan pada seseorang yang sudah kehilangan ingatan tentang cara melakukan suatu keterampilan.

Sejauh mungkin, jawablah orang itu dengan lembut bahkan jika itu adalah jawaban yang ke-lima puluh tiga kali Anda sampaikan untuk pertanyaan yang sama. Gunakan juga pengalihan. Jika ada aktivitas yang masih bisa mereka lakukan, seperti menjahit atau teka-teki gambar (bahkan teka-teki anak-anak dengan potongan yang sangat besar), ajak mereka melakukannya. Di tahap akhir penyakit, membiarkan mereka melihat buku bergambar yang indah atau kadang-kadang memberi mereka boneka bayi untuk dipeluk dapat membantu menenangkan mereka dan mengalihkan kecemasan mereka saat itu.

Minta Bantuan Orang Lain

Mudah menjadi frustrasi. Berusaha menyediakan semua perawatan sendirian bukanlah solusi jangka panjang. Perawatan demensia adalah lari maraton, bukan sprint. Banyak orang hidup bertahun-tahun setelah diagnosis, dan meskipun tubuh fisik mereka tetap relatif kuat, mereka membutuhkan lebih banyak perawatan.

Salah satu berkat memiliki hubungan keluarga dan komunitas gereja adalah kita memiliki orang-orang yang tersedia untuk memberikan bantuan.

Memiliki anggota keluarga atau teman yang turun tangan untuk memberi Anda jeda sangat penting agar tidak menjadi kelelahan berat atau bahkan marah kepada orang yang Anda kasihi. Sebaiknya luangkan waktu untuk beristirahat secara berkala sebelum Anda benar-benar kehabisan tenaga mental. Anda mungkin berpikir Anda baik-baik saja, tetapi kita semua cenderung menjadi lelah dalam melakukan kebaikan jika kita tidak pernah beristirahat.

Kesimpulan

Ku berharap ada lebih banyak solusi medis untuk demensia. Mungkin nanti akan datang lebih banyak. Untuk saat ini, pilihan obat sangat terbatas.

Kunci adalah menerapkan buah Roh. “But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith, meekness, temperance: against such there is no law” (Galatians 5:22-23).

Bahkan pada hari-hari yang paling membuat frustrasi, orang-orang yang berurusan dengan kehilangan ingatan yang parah membutuhkan kasih, kelembutan, dan kesabaran dari anggota keluarga mereka. Hanya melalui kuasa Roh Kudus kita dapat menyediakan perawatan yang dibutuhkan untuk seseorang yang tubuhnya kuat, tetapi yang tidak lagi mengenali Anda.

Spring is my favorite time of the year. Everything is new. Hyacinths are trying their noble best to poke their buds through the cold constraint of the winter-bound earth. Migrating waterfowl bring new sounds as they honk and quack their way to their final nesting places. This year the spring peepers in our area were “winter peepers” as they feebly squeaked their greetings to the arriving spring in mid-February. Tree buds are swelling, waiting to burst forth in full glory.

Oh, the magnificence of God’s nature joining forces to proclaim the glory of new life. Surely it must have been during this exuberant time of the year when the Psalmist wrote, “Let the floods clap their hands: let the hills be joyful together before the LORD; for he cometh to judge the earth: with righteousness shall he judge the world, and the people with equity” (Psalms 98:8-9). This display of new life springing from the earth is a beautiful representation of new life found in Christ Jesus. The wonders of the newness of life springing from the deadness of sin cannot be fully displayed by even the best show of God’s creation. It can only be experienced within the soul.

As I write this, I am flying 35,000 feet over the sub-Saharan desert land of Chad and Niger. The stark contrast between the landscape described in the previous paragraphs and the parched desert land hurrying by six miles below me is nearly beyond my comprehension. The dry earth begs for rain as livestock scrounge for anything green to fulfill their appetite. The vast dryness loudly proclaims a reminder of the millions of parched souls who have never heard of the “well of water springing up into everlasting life” (John 4:14). Millions who never experienced Christ the fountain as described in the Hymn History article in this issue:

Oh! Christ He is the foutain,
The deep sweet well of Love!
The streams on earth I’ve tasted,
More deep I’ll drink above:
There, to an ocean fullness,
His mercy doth expand,
And glory—glory dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land.

At times a yearning stirs in my heart to live the relaxed, relational lifestyle experienced in these impoverished tribal communities. Family and friends are more important than calendars and commitments. As we read in the Sister to Sister article, commitments and busyness can bring us to the overload point when we feel we cannot handle anything more. Read more to learn how to take practical steps to avoid that breaking point.

Most people in this area are Muslims. As I write this, Muslims are in the middle of Ramadan, a month-long season of fasting. They fast from food and water every day from dawn to dusk, even though daytime temperatures exceed 110 degrees. Their rigorous fasting, along with stopping their work to pray many times a day, is driven by a fervent desire to seek forgiveness of sins and obtain enough merit to enter heaven. If they only knew that true grace and mercy comes from God through the salvation of his Son, Jesus Christ. Our works can never bring us into right standing with God. The writer of the article “How to Increase Your Faith” clearly points this out “Faith is one of the basic ingredients in getting right with God. We come into the Christian life (and receive the forgiveness of sins) through faith. . . We abandon all hope for saving ourselves by our own abilities, and instead, we put complete trust in Jesus Christ for our eternal safety.”

As we plant our gardens and watch the trees burst forth in bloom, let us be reminded of the words of the prophet Isaiah, “For as the earth bringeth forth her bud, and as the garden causeth the things that are sown in it to spring forth; so the Lord GOD will cause righteousness and praise to spring forth before all the nations” (Isaiah 61:11).

Blessings to all,

Edward Martin

বসন্ত আমার বছরের প্রিয় সময়। সবকিছুই নতুন। হায়াসিন্থ পুষ্পগুলো তাদের কুঁড়ি শীতকালের বন্ধনীভূত মাটির মধ্য দিয়ে বের করে আনার অদম্য চেষ্টা করছে। অভিবাসী জলচর পাখিরা তাদের হংকার ও কাঁকার সুরে তাদের চূড়ান্ত বাসস্থলের দিকে এগোতে গিয়ে নতুন শব্দ আনছে। এই বছর আমাদের অঞ্চলের স্প্রিং পিপাররা মধ্য ফেব্রুয়ারিতে “শীতকালীন পিপার” ছিলেন, দুর্বলভাবে বসন্তে আগমনকে অভিবাদন জানিয়ে চিঞ্ছিল। গাছের কুঁড়িগুলো ফুলে ফোটার জন্য ফুলে যাওয়ার অপেক্ষায় ফুলছে।

আহা, নতুন জীবনের জৌলুস ঘোষণা করতে ঈশ্বরের প্রকৃতির মহিমা কিভাবে ঐক্যবদ্ধ হচ্ছে। নিশ্চয়ই পুরাণকার যখন লেখেছিলেন, “Let the floods clap their hands: let the hills be joyful together before the LORD; for he cometh to judge the earth: with righteousness shall he judge the world, and the people with equity” (Psalms 98:8-9), তখন এই উদ্দীপ্ত বছরের সময়টাই ছিল। মৃত পাপের মধ্য থেকে উদ্ভূত নতুন জীবনের এই প্রদর্শনী কিশোরতম ঈশ্বরের সৃষ্টির সেরা প্রদর্শনও পুরোপুরি প্রকাশ করতে পারে না। এটা কেবলমাত্র আত্মার ভিতরেই অনুভূত হতে পারে।

আমি এটা লিখছি, যখন আমি সাব-সাহারান মরুভূমি চাদ এবং নিশ্চিতভাবে নিগারের উপর দিয়ে 35,000 ফুট উঁচুতে উড়ে যাচ্ছি। পূর্বের অনুচ্ছেদে বর্ণিত ভূপটল এবং ছয় মাইল নিচে দ্রুত পেরিয়ে যেতে থাকা শুকনো মরুভূমির মধ্যে প্রখর বৈপরীত্য আমার উপলব্ধির বাইরে প্রায়। শুষ্ক মাটি বৃষ্টির জন্য আকুল হয়ে আছে, যখন পশুপালন সবুজ কোনও কিছু খুঁজে তাদের ক্ষুধো মেটাতে চেষ্টা করছে। বিশাল শুষ্কতা জোরে ঘোষণা করছে কোটি কোটি শুকিয়ে যাওয়া প্রাণের কথা, যারা কখনো “well of water springing up into everlasting life” (John 4:14) সম্পর্কে শুনে না। লক্ষ লক্ষ যারা কখনো অনুভব করেনি খ্রিস্ট—এই ইতিহাস-লেখা কীর্তিগানে বর্ণিত ফোয়ারার মতো।

Oh! Christ He is the foutain,
The deep sweet well of Love!
The streams on earth I’ve tasted,
More deep I’ll drink above:
There, to an ocean fullness,
His mercy doth expand,
And glory—glory dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land.

কখনো কখনো আমার হৃদয়ে আগ্রহ জাগে এই দারিদ্র্যপ্রবণ জনজাতিগত সম্প্রদায়গুলিতে যে বিনয়ী, সম্পর্কঘন জীবনধারা অভিজ্ঞ তা বাঁচবার। পরিবার ও বন্ধুরা ক্যালেন্ডার ও প্রতিশ্রুতির চেয়ে বেশি গুরুত্বপূর্ণ। যেমনটি আমরা Sister to Sister নিবন্ধে পড়েছি, প্রতিশ্রুতি ও ব্যস্ততা আমাদেরকে অতিভারবোধের দিকে ঠেলে দিতে পারে যখন আমরা অনুভব করি আমরা আর কিছু পরিচালনা করতে পারছি না। সেই ভাঙনের সীমা এড়াতে বৈবহারিক ধাপ কীভাবে গ্রহণ করা যায় তা জানতে আরও পড়ুন।

এই এলাকায় অধিকাংশ মানুষ মুসলমান। আমি এটা লিখছি যখন তারা রমজানের মাঝামাঝি সময়ে আছে, এক মাসব্যাপী উপবাসের মরসুম। তারা প্রতিদিন ভোর থেকে সূর্যাস্ত পর্যন্ত খাদ্য ও জল থেকে বিরত থাকে, এমনকি দিনের তাপমাত্রা 110 ডিগ্রি ছাড়িয়ে গেলেও। তাদের কঠোর উপবাস, দিনের বহুবার নামাজের জন্য কাজ বন্ধ করা—এসবই পিছনে থাকে পাপের ক্ষমার তীব্র আকাঙ্খা এবং স্বর্গে প্রবেশের জন্য পর্যাপ্ত সওয়াব অর্জনের প্রচেষ্টা। যদি তারা জানত যে সত্যিকারের অনুগ্রহ ও দয়া ঈশ্বরের কাছ থেকে তার পুত্র যীশুর মাধ্যমে আসে। আমাদের কাজগুলি কখনোই আমাদের ঈশ্বরের সাথে সঠিক অবস্থানে নিয়ে আসতে পারে না। “How to Increase Your Faith” শিরোনামের নিবন্ধের লেখক এটিকে স্পষ্টভাবে নির্দেশ করেছেন: “Faith is one of the basic ingredients in getting right with God. We come into the Christian life (and receive the forgiveness of sins) through faith. . . We abandon all hope for saving ourselves by our own abilities, and instead, we put complete trust in Jesus Christ for our eternal safety.”

যেমনি আমরা আমাদের বাগান বোনা এবং গাছগুলো ফুলে ফোটতে দেখছি, আমাদের নববাণীর শব্দ মনে করিয়ে দিই মানুষব্রত Isaiah-এর শব্দগুলি, “For as the earth bringeth forth her bud, and as the garden causeth the things that are sown in it to spring forth; so the Lord GOD will cause righteousness and praise to spring forth before all the nations” (Isaiah 61:11)।

সবাইকে আশীর্বাদ,

Edward Martin

Part 1

For Alice, life is exasperating. Each day feels like an endless grind. She loves her family, but in her heart, she questions if what she is working so hard to accomplish makes any difference at all. She didn’t always feel bogged down, and she wondered what changed to make her feel overwhelmed so much of the time.

Sometimes busyness increases so gradually that we barely recognize the change. Busyness, given the chance, will overload us with more obligations than we can realistically get done in one day, or one week, or even one lifetime. Then, without warning, we reach the overload point when we feel as though we cannot possibly handle any more. Relentless overload can cause physical and mental exhaustion to the point where we feel deprived of enthusiasm, energy, and purpose. Some women seem to have a built-in indicator of where the overload line is. Others, like myself, struggle to find that balance. Constantly. There are so many good, interesting, and exciting options right at our fingertips; without much thought, we fill our days.

Concepts that contribute to overload

Playing multiple roles can be stressful. Overloading yourself with responsibilities and commitments can make you forget what is most important. It is easy to equate busyness with self-worth. By default, we start believing that:

  • Homemakers are capable of handling everything.
  • Homemakers, especially godly homemakers, are never frustrated.
  • A homemaker should anticipate all her family’s needs.

If we are honest, we know that these statements are unrealistic. Homemakers cannot do everything. All homemakers experience frustration occasionally. A mother cannot consistently be one step ahead of her family’s needs.

Rethinking the busy life

Household duties and caring for our families fill our days. Sometimes those tasks alone make us extremely busy. But what about the extra-circular activities or the high standard we hold ourselves to? We may need to think differently so we can break free from habits that threaten to control us.

Accept your limits

Maybe you can go to a Tupperware party, attend a Bible study, and repaint the bathroom all in one week. But should you? Good homemakers allow themselves to simplify even if they prefer doing it another way. That means if you are an avid bread maker, it’s all right to toss a few loaves of bread into your shopping cart.

Evaluate what causes frustrations

Artificial smiles can hide inner frustrations, but it doesn’t cure them. It works best to admit that there is a problem and then seek a solution. I’ve had to learn this repeatedly. All my family members know that we eat dinner at 5:30. But a late arrival habit is trending, and it bothers me.

When I told my husband about the frustration, he simply said, “Why don’t you explain the issue and quit being so uptight about it?” Good point. Proactively seeking solutions works for many problem areas.

Imperfect women make good homemakers

Quit worrying about perfection and make decisions based on what is best for today. Fun-loving, happy, homemakers might have a few dust bunnies under the furniture, but they radiate an aura that draws people to their hearts and homes.

Everyone differs when it comes to how much we can handle. On the other hand, everyone is the same; we all have limits. In future installments, we will discuss how to deal with common points of overload.

Part 2

Many homemakers find themselves stretched thin among commitments that go with home, family, and other activities. As busy as we are, why do we continue to fill our schedules fuller?

It is easy for me to commit to a new project and then realize, halfway into the task, that I have overstepped my limits. Too often, I overestimate the amount of time I must have to complete a project and underestimate the amount of time a task will take.

Commitment overload happens by default. When we play multiple roles and add more responsibilities, we can easily become slaves to the promises we have made. Overload tends to drain our energy, dull our senses, and deaden our joy.

Recognizing Overload

Sometimes multiple activities take place in rapid sequence. Normally, we can flow with short-term spurts of busyness. But if the flow of activities is never-ending and we keep adding more obligations, we develop a pattern that becomes a way of life.

Too many commitments beyond normal duties make us candidates for depression and burnout. Personally, when I experience insomnia, apathy, or irritability, it is time to examine my schedule. If adjustments aren’t made, someone or something will suffer.

No one can overextend themselves indefinitely. Sometimes we suffer consequences for keeping a pace that is beyond our resources. Symptoms of overload can include lack of sleep, strained relationships, procrastination, fear of failure, and a susceptible immune system.

Breaking Free of Overload

Identifying overload takes an honest evaluation of yourself. How can you know if this is just a busy season or if busyness is the new normal? Are you declining a request because life is too full, or is it an excuse? Do you have to say “yes” on the spot? With practice, you can learn how to pull back before reaching the overload point.

Let an idea or request gel before committing

This has saved me a great deal of stress. There are so many good things to be involved in, and new inspirations come daily. Sometimes tasks can be incorporated into my/our schedule. Other times I must simply let them go and stay focused on what is most important. Consider waiting a few hours before incorporating new ideas and requests.

Seek advice, especially your husband’s

A renowned doughnut maker was asked to have a stand at an auction. She asked her husband what he thought about it. He said, “As long as you don’t complain and stress about it like you did last year, I don’t care.” Was her husband saying “yes” or “no”? This lady should take the cue that doughnut making was somehow adding stress. Either she should not do it, or together they must seek a workable solution.

Evaluate your schedule regularly

Keep a detailed calendar to have a picture of past, present, and future events. If your family had the flu last week and you plan to take an out-of-state trip next week, should you add more? What is the emotional health of your family? Is your husband stressed at work? Sometimes it is better to have a time slot of nothing so it can be filled with what is important now. You can’t do a good job at anything if you are spread too thin. Too many obligations make it hard to be personally refreshed and congenial. Choosing commitments wisely will help you invest your energy where it is most valuable for today.

Del 1

For Alice er livet irriterende. Hver dag føles som en endeløs mølle. Hun elsker familien sin, men innerst inne spør hun om det hun jobber så hardt for virkelig utgjør noen forskjell. Hun følte seg ikke alltid tynget, og hun lurte på hva som hadde endret seg slik at hun så ofte følte seg overveldet.

Noen ganger øker travelheten så gradvis at vi knapt merker forandringen. Hvis travelhet får lov, vil den overbelaste oss med flere forpliktelser enn vi realistisk kan få gjort på én dag, eller én uke, eller til og med ett liv. Så, uten varsel, når vi et overbelastningspunkt hvor vi føler at vi ikke kan håndtere mer. Uopphørlig overbelastning kan forårsake fysisk og mental utmattelse til det punktet der vi føler oss fratatt entusiasme, energi og mening. Noen kvinner ser ut til å ha en innebygd indikator for hvor overbelastningsgrensen går. Andre, som meg, sliter med å finne den balansen. Stadig. Det finnes så mange gode, interessante og spennende muligheter rett ved fingertuppene våre; uten mye ettertanke fyller vi dagene våre.

Forestillingene som bidrar til overbelastning

Å spille mange roller kan være stressende. Å overvelde seg selv med ansvar og forpliktelser kan få deg til å glemme hva som er viktigst. Det er lett å likestille travelhet med egenverdi. Som en slags standard begynner vi å tro at:

  • Husmødre kan klare alt.
  • Husmødre, spesielt fromme husmødre, er aldri frustrerte.
  • En husmor bør forutse alle familiens behov.

Hvis vi er ærlige, vet vi at disse uttalelsene er urealistiske. Husmødre kan ikke gjøre alt. Alle husmødre opplever av og til frustrasjon. En mor kan ikke konsekvent være ett skritt foran familiens behov.

Tenk nytt om det travle livet

Husarbeid og omsorg for familien fyller dagene våre. Noen ganger gjør disse oppgavene alene oss ekstremt travle. Men hva med fritidsaktiviteter eller den høye standarden vi setter for oss selv? Vi må kanskje tenke annerledes for å bryte fri fra vaner som truer med å kontrollere oss.

Aksepter dine grenser

Kanskje du kan gå på en Tupperware-fest, delta i en bibelstudiegruppe og male badet på én uke. Men bør du det? Gode husmødre tillater seg å forenkle selv om de foretrekker å gjøre det på en annen måte. Det betyr at hvis du er en ivrig brødbaker, er det greit å legge noen brød i handlevognen.

Vurder hva som forårsaker frustrasjon

Falske smil kan skjule indre frustrasjoner, men det kurerer dem ikke. Det fungerer best å innrømme at det er et problem og så søke en løsning. Jeg har måttet lære dette gjentatte ganger. Hele familien min vet at vi spiser middag kl. 17:30. Men det trender med å komme for sent, og det plager meg.

Når jeg fortalte mannen min om frustrasjonen, sa han enkelt: «Hvorfor forklarer du ikke problemet og slutter å være så opphengt i det?» Godt poeng. Å proaktivt søke løsninger fungerer for mange problemområder.

Ufullkomne kvinner blir gode husmødre

Slutt å bekymre deg for perfeksjon og ta beslutninger basert på hva som er best for i dag. Livsglade, lykkelige husmødre kan ha noen støvkaniner under møblene, men de utstråler et vesen som trekker folk mot deres hjerter og hjem.

Alle er forskjellige når det gjelder hvor mye vi kan tåle. På den annen side er alle like; vi har alle grenser. I fremtidige avsnitt vil vi diskutere hvordan vi kan håndtere vanlige overbelastningspunkter.

Del 2

Mange husmødre finner seg strukket tynne mellom forpliktelser som følger med hjem, familie og andre aktiviteter. Så travle som vi er, hvorfor fortsetter vi å fylle timeplanene våre mer og mer?

Det er lett for meg å påta meg et nytt prosjekt og så innse, halvveis i oppgaven, at jeg har overtrådt mine grenser. Altfor ofte overvurderer jeg hvor mye tid jeg må ha for å fullføre et prosjekt og undervurderer hvor lang tid en oppgave vil ta.

Forpliktelsesoverbelastning skjer som standard. Når vi spiller flere roller og legger til flere ansvar, kan vi lett bli slaver av de løftene vi har gitt. Overbelastning har en tendens til å tappe energien vår, sløve sansene og gjøre oss likeglade.

Å kjenne igjen overbelastning

Noen ganger skjer flere aktiviteter i rask rekkefølge. Vanligvis kan vi flyte med kortvarige perioder av travelhet. Men hvis strømmen av aktiviteter aldri tar slutt og vi stadig legger til flere forpliktelser, utvikler vi et mønster som blir en livsstil.

For mange forpliktelser utover normale plikter gjør oss utsatt for depresjon og utbrenthet. Personlig, når jeg opplever søvnløshet, apati eller irritabilitet, er det på tide å undersøke timeplanen min. Hvis ikke justeringer gjøres, vil noen eller noe lide.

Ingen kan presse seg selv i det uendelige. Noen ganger får vi konsekvenser for å holde et tempo som overstiger våre ressurser. Symptomer på overbelastning kan inkludere mangel på søvn, anstrengte relasjoner, prokrastinering, frykt for å mislykkes og et sårbart immunforsvar.

Bryte fri fra overbelastning

Å identifisere overbelastning krever en ærlig vurdering av deg selv. Hvordan kan du vite om dette bare er en travel periode eller om travelhet er den nye normalen? Avviser du en forespørsel fordi livet er for fullt, eller er det en unnskyldning? Må du si «ja» der og da? Med øvelse kan du lære å trekke deg tilbake før du når overbelastningspunktet.

La en idé eller forespørsel få modne før du forplikter deg

Dette har spart meg for mye stress. Det finnes så mange gode ting å være med på, og nye inspirasjoner kommer daglig. Noen ganger kan oppgaver innpasses i min/vår timeplan. Andre ganger må jeg ganske enkelt la dem gå og holde fokus på det som er viktigst. Vurder å vente et par timer før du innlemmer nye ideer og forespørsler.

Søk råd, spesielt fra mannen din

En berømt smultringbaker ble spurt om hun ville ha en stand på en auksjon. Hun spurte mannen sin hva han mente. Han sa: «Så lenge du ikke klager og stresser over det som du gjorde i fjor, bryr jeg meg ikke.» Sa mannen hennes «ja» eller «nei»? Denne kvinnen bør ta signalet om at smultringbaking på en eller annen måte la til stress. Enten skal hun la være å gjøre det, eller så må de sammen finne en gjennomførbar løsning.

Vurder timeplanen din jevnlig

Ha en detaljert kalender for å få et bilde av fortid, nåtid og fremtidige hendelser. Hvis familien din hadde influensa forrige uke og du planlegger en tur til en annen stat neste uke, bør du legge til mer da? Hva er familiens emosjonelle helse? Er mannen din stresset på jobben? Noen ganger er det bedre å ha et tidsglipp uten planer slik at det kan fylles med det som er viktig nå. Du kan ikke gjøre en god jobb med noe hvis du er spredt for tynt. For mange forpliktelser gjør det vanskelig å bli personlig forfrisket og vennlig. Å velge forpliktelser klokt vil hjelpe deg å investere energien din der den er mest verdifull for i dag.

Part 1

For Alice, life is exasperating. Each day feels like an endless grind. She loves her family, but in her heart, she questions if what she is working so hard to accomplish makes any difference at all. She didn’t always feel bogged down, and she wondered what changed to make her feel overwhelmed so much of the time.

Sometimes busyness increases so gradually that we barely recognize the change. Busyness, given the chance, will overload us with more obligations than we can realistically get done in one day, or one week, or even one lifetime. Then, without warning, we reach the overload point when we feel as though we cannot possibly handle any more. Relentless overload can cause physical and mental exhaustion to the point where we feel deprived of enthusiasm, energy, and purpose. Some women seem to have a built-in indicator of where the overload line is. Others, like myself, struggle to find that balance. Constantly. There are so many good, interesting, and exciting options right at our fingertips; without much thought, we fill our days.

Concepts that contribute to overload

Playing multiple roles can be stressful. Overloading yourself with responsibilities and commitments can make you forget what is most important. It is easy to equate busyness with self-worth. By default, we start believing that:

  • Homemakers are capable of handling everything.
  • Homemakers, especially godly homemakers, are never frustrated.
  • A homemaker should anticipate all her family’s needs.

If we are honest, we know that these statements are unrealistic. Homemakers cannot do everything. All homemakers experience frustration occasionally. A mother cannot consistently be one step ahead of her family’s needs.

Rethinking the busy life

Household duties and caring for our families fill our days. Sometimes those tasks alone make us extremely busy. But what about the extra-circular activities or the high standard we hold ourselves to? We may need to think differently so we can break free from habits that threaten to control us.

Accept your limits

Maybe you can go to a Tupperware party, attend a Bible study, and repaint the bathroom all in one week. But should you? Good homemakers allow themselves to simplify even if they prefer doing it another way. That means if you are an avid bread maker, it’s all right to toss a few loaves of bread into your shopping cart.

Evaluate what causes frustrations

Artificial smiles can hide inner frustrations, but it doesn’t cure them. It works best to admit that there is a problem and then seek a solution. I’ve had to learn this repeatedly. All my family members know that we eat dinner at 5:30. But a late arrival habit is trending, and it bothers me.

When I told my husband about the frustration, he simply said, “Why don’t you explain the issue and quit being so uptight about it?” Good point. Proactively seeking solutions works for many problem areas.

Imperfect women make good homemakers

Quit worrying about perfection and make decisions based on what is best for today. Fun-loving, happy, homemakers might have a few dust bunnies under the furniture, but they radiate an aura that draws people to their hearts and homes.

Everyone differs when it comes to how much we can handle. On the other hand, everyone is the same; we all have limits. In future installments, we will discuss how to deal with common points of overload.

Part 2

Many homemakers find themselves stretched thin among commitments that go with home, family, and other activities. As busy as we are, why do we continue to fill our schedules fuller?

It is easy for me to commit to a new project and then realize, halfway into the task, that I have overstepped my limits. Too often, I overestimate the amount of time I must have to complete a project and underestimate the amount of time a task will take.

Commitment overload happens by default. When we play multiple roles and add more responsibilities, we can easily become slaves to the promises we have made. Overload tends to drain our energy, dull our senses, and deaden our joy.

Recognizing Overload

Sometimes multiple activities take place in rapid sequence. Normally, we can flow with short-term spurts of busyness. But if the flow of activities is never-ending and we keep adding more obligations, we develop a pattern that becomes a way of life.

Too many commitments beyond normal duties make us candidates for depression and burnout. Personally, when I experience insomnia, apathy, or irritability, it is time to examine my schedule. If adjustments aren’t made, someone or something will suffer.

No one can overextend themselves indefinitely. Sometimes we suffer consequences for keeping a pace that is beyond our resources. Symptoms of overload can include lack of sleep, strained relationships, procrastination, fear of failure, and a susceptible immune system.

Breaking Free of Overload

Identifying overload takes an honest evaluation of yourself. How can you know if this is just a busy season or if busyness is the new normal? Are you declining a request because life is too full, or is it an excuse? Do you have to say “yes” on the spot? With practice, you can learn how to pull back before reaching the overload point.

Let an idea or request gel before committing

This has saved me a great deal of stress. There are so many good things to be involved in, and new inspirations come daily. Sometimes tasks can be incorporated into my/our schedule. Other times I must simply let them go and stay focused on what is most important. Consider waiting a few hours before incorporating new ideas and requests.

Seek advice, especially your husband’s

A renowned doughnut maker was asked to have a stand at an auction. She asked her husband what he thought about it. He said, “As long as you don’t complain and stress about it like you did last year, I don’t care.” Was her husband saying “yes” or “no”? This lady should take the cue that doughnut making was somehow adding stress. Either she should not do it, or together they must seek a workable solution.

Evaluate your schedule regularly

Keep a detailed calendar to have a picture of past, present, and future events. If your family had the flu last week and you plan to take an out-of-state trip next week, should you add more? What is the emotional health of your family? Is your husband stressed at work? Sometimes it is better to have a time slot of nothing so it can be filled with what is important now. You can’t do a good job at anything if you are spread too thin. Too many obligations make it hard to be personally refreshed and congenial. Choosing commitments wisely will help you invest your energy where it is most valuable for today.

1부

앨리스에게 삶은 답답하다. 매일이 끝없는 수고처럼 느껴진다. 그녀는 가족을 사랑하지만, 마음속으로 그녀가 그렇게 열심히 이루려고 애쓰는 일이 과연 어떤 차이를 만드는지 의문을 품는다. 그녀가 항상 이렇게 짐에 눌린 기분을 느낀 것은 아니었고, 무엇이 변해서 그녀가 이렇게 자주 압도당하는 기분이 들게 했는지 궁금해했다.

때로는 바쁨이 너무 서서히 증가해서 우리가 변화한 것을 거의 알아차리지 못할 때가 있다. 바쁨은 기회가 주어지면 현실적으로 하루, 일주일, 심지어 평생 안에 해낼 수 있는 것보다 더 많은 의무로 우리를 과부하 상태로 만들 것이다. 그러다 경고 없이 우리는 더 이상 감당할 수 없을 것 같은 지점에 도달한다. 끊임없는 과부하는 열정, 에너지, 목적을 빼앗아 신체적·정신적 탈진을 초래할 수 있다. 어떤 여성들은 과부하 한계가 어디인지 알아차리는 내재적 지표를 가지고 있는 것 같다. 나 같은 사람들은 그 균형을 찾기 위해 끊임없이 애쓴다. 손끝에 좋은 것들, 흥미로운 것들, 신나는 선택들이 너무 많아서 별생각 없이 우리의 날들을 채운다.

과부하를 부추기는 개념들

다중 역할을 수행하는 것은 스트레스를 줄 수 있다. 책임과 약속으로 자신을 과부하시키면 무엇이 가장 중요한지 잊게 할 수 있다. 바쁨을 자존감과 동일시하기 쉽다. 기본적으로 우리는 다음과 같이 믿기 시작한다:

  • 가정주부는 모든 것을 처리할 수 있다.
  • 가정주부들, 특히 경건한 가정주부들은 절대 좌절하지 않는다.
  • 가정주부는 가족의 모든 필요를 예측해야 한다.

솔직해지자면 우리는 이러한 진술들이 비현실적이라는 것을 안다. 가정주부는 모든 것을 할 수 없다. 모든 가정주부는 때때로 좌절을 겪는다. 어머니가 항상 가족의 필요를 한 발 앞서 예측할 수는 없다.

바쁜 삶을 재고하기

집안일과 가족 돌봄이 우리 날들을 채운다. 때로는 그 일들만으로도 우리는 매우 바쁘다. 그러나 추가 활동이나 우리가 자신에게 요구하는 높은 기준은 어떠한가? 통제하려 드는 습관에서 벗어나기 위해서는 다르게 생각할 필요가 있을지도 모른다.

자신의 한계를 받아들이라

아마 한 주에 테이퍼웨어 파티에 가고, 성경 공부에 참석하고, 욕실을 다시 페인트칠할 수 있을 것이다. 하지만 그래야 할까? 좋은 가정주부는 자신이 다른 방식을 선호하더라도 단순화하는 것을 허용한다. 즉, 당신이 열성적인 빵 굽는 사람이라면 몇 덩이 빵을 쇼핑카트에 담아오는 것도 괜찮다는 뜻이다.

무엇이 좌절을 일으키는지 평가하라

겉으로 보이는 인위적인 미소는 내적 좌절을 숨길 수 있지만 그것을 치료하지는 못한다. 문제를 인정한 다음 해결책을 찾는 것이 가장 효과적이다. 나는 이것을 반복해서 배워야 했다. 우리 가족 모두는 저녁을 5시 30분에 먹는다는 것을 안다. 그러나 늦는 습관이 유행처럼 번지고 있고, 그것이 나를 괴롭힌다.

남편에게 그 좌절감을 이야기했을 때 그는 단지 이렇게 말했다. “왜 문제를 설명하고 그 일에 대해 그렇게 잔소리하지 않는 거야?” 일리가 있다. 문제를 능동적으로 해결하려는 시도는 많은 문제 영역에서 효과가 있다.

불완전한 여성들이 훌륭한 가정주부가 된다

완벽을 걱정하는 것을 그만두고 오늘을 위해 무엇이 최선인지에 근거해 결정을 내리라. 즐거움을 사랑하고 행복한 가정주부들은 가구 아래에 먼지 뭉치가 조금 있을 수 있지만, 사람들을 그들의 마음과 집으로 끌어당기는 아우라를 발산한다.

우리가 감당할 수 있는 양에 관해서는 모두 다르다. 반면에 모두 같다; 우리 모두에게 한계가 있다. 다음 연재에서 우리는 과부하의 일반적 지점을 다루는 방법을 논의할 것이다.

2부

많은 가정주부들은 가정, 가족, 그리고 다른 활동들과 관련된 약속들 사이에서 자신이 얇게 펼쳐진 것을 발견한다. 우리가 아무리 바빠도, 왜 계속해서 일정을 더 채우는가?

새 프로젝트에 쉽게 참여를 결심했다가 과제의 중간 즈음에 내가 한계를 넘었다는 것을 깨닫는 경우가 많다. 너무 자주 나는 프로젝트를 완료하기 위해 필요한 시간을 과대평가하고, 과제가 걸릴 시간을 과소평가한다.

약속 과부하는 기본값으로 발생한다. 우리가 여러 역할을 수행하고 더 많은 책임을 추가할 때 우리는 쉽게 우리가 한 약속의 노예가 될 수 있다. 과부하는 우리의 에너지를 고갈시키고 감각을 둔화시키며 기쁨을 무디게 하는 경향이 있다.

과부하 인식하기

때로는 여러 활동이 빠른 연속으로 일어난다. 보통 우리는 단기적인 바쁨의 급증을 흐름에 따라갈 수 있다. 그러나 활동의 흐름이 끝없이 계속되고 우리가 더 많은 의무를 계속 추가한다면, 우리는 삶의 방식이 되는 패턴을 발전시킨다.

일상적 의무를 넘어선 과도한 약속은 우리를 우울증과 번아웃의 후보로 만든다. 개인적으로 나는 불면증, 무관심 또는 과민함을 경험할 때 일정표를 점검할 때임을 안다. 조정이 이루어지지 않으면 누군가 혹은 무언가는 고통받게 된다.

아무도 무기한으로 자신을 과도하게 확장할 수 없다. 때때로 우리가 자원 이상의 속도를 유지한 대가를 치른다. 과부하의 증상으로는 수면 부족, 긴장된 관계, 미루기, 실패에 대한 두려움, 그리고 취약한 면역 체계가 포함될 수 있다.

과부하에서 벗어나기

과부하를 확인하려면 자신을 정직하게 평가해야 한다. 이것이 단지 바쁜 계절인지 아니면 바쁨이 새로운 정상인지 어떻게 알 수 있는가? 삶이 너무 가득 차서 요청을 거절하는가, 아니면 그것이 변명인가? 즉시 “예”라고 말해야 하는가? 연습을 통해 과부하 지점에 도달하기 전에 물러나는 법을 배울 수 있다.

약속하기 전에 아이디어나 요청을 숙성시켜라

이것은 나에게 큰 스트레스를 많이 덜어주었다. 참여할 만한 좋은 일들이 너무 많고, 새로운 영감이 날마다 온다. 때로는 과제가 우리의 일정에 통합될 수 있다. 다른 때에는 단순히 놓아 버리고 가장 중요한 것에 집중해야 한다. 새로운 아이디어와 요청을 받아들이기 전에 몇 시간을 기다려보는 것을 고려하라.

조언을 구하라, 특히 남편의 조언을

유명한 도넛 제조업자가 경매에서 판매대를 갖기를 요청받았다. 그녀는 남편에게 어떻게 생각하는지 물었다. 그는 말했다. “작년에 너처럼 불평하고 스트레스받지 않는 한 나는 상관없어.” 남편은 “예”라고 한 것일까 아니면 “아니오”라고 한 것일까? 이 여성은 도넛 만들기가 어떤 식으로든 스트레스를 더하고 있다는 신호를 받아야 한다. 그녀는 그것을 하지 말아야 하거나, 아니면 함께 실현 가능한 해결책을 찾아야 한다.

일정을 정기적으로 평가하라

과거, 현재, 미래의 사건들을 한눈에 볼 수 있도록 상세한 달력을 유지하라. 가족이 지난주에 독감에 걸렸고 다음주에 주 밖으로 여행을 갈 계획이라면, 더 추가해야 하는가? 가족의 정서적 건강은 어떤가? 남편이 직장에서 스트레스를 받고 있는가? 때로는 지금 중요한 것으로 채워질 수 있도록 아무것도 없는 시간대를 비워두는 것이 더 낫다. 너무 얇게 펼쳐져 있다면 어떤 일도 잘할 수 없다. 너무 많은 약속은 개인적으로 재충전되고 온화하게 행동하기 어렵게 만든다. 약속을 현명하게 선택하면 오늘에 가장 가치 있는 곳에 에너지를 투자하는 데 도움이 될 것이다.

Part 1

For Alice, life is exasperating. Each day feels like an endless grind. She loves her family, but in her heart, she questions if what she is working so hard to accomplish makes any difference at all. She didn’t always feel bogged down, and she wondered what changed to make her feel overwhelmed so much of the time.

Sometimes busyness increases so gradually that we barely recognize the change. Busyness, given the chance, will overload us with more obligations than we can realistically get done in one day, or one week, or even one lifetime. Then, without warning, we reach the overload point when we feel as though we cannot possibly handle any more. Relentless overload can cause physical and mental exhaustion to the point where we feel deprived of enthusiasm, energy, and purpose. Some women seem to have a built-in indicator of where the overload line is. Others, like myself, struggle to find that balance. Constantly. There are so many good, interesting, and exciting options right at our fingertips; without much thought, we fill our days.

Concepts that contribute to overload

Playing multiple roles can be stressful. Overloading yourself with responsibilities and commitments can make you forget what is most important. It is easy to equate busyness with self-worth. By default, we start believing that:

  • Homemakers are capable of handling everything.
  • Homemakers, especially godly homemakers, are never frustrated.
  • A homemaker should anticipate all her family’s needs.

If we are honest, we know that these statements are unrealistic. Homemakers cannot do everything. All homemakers experience frustration occasionally. A mother cannot consistently be one step ahead of her family’s needs.

Rethinking the busy life

Household duties and caring for our families fill our days. Sometimes those tasks alone make us extremely busy. But what about the extra-circular activities or the high standard we hold ourselves to? We may need to think differently so we can break free from habits that threaten to control us.

Accept your limits

Maybe you can go to a Tupperware party, attend a Bible study, and repaint the bathroom all in one week. But should you? Good homemakers allow themselves to simplify even if they prefer doing it another way. That means if you are an avid bread maker, it’s all right to toss a few loaves of bread into your shopping cart.

Evaluate what causes frustrations

Artificial smiles can hide inner frustrations, but it doesn’t cure them. It works best to admit that there is a problem and then seek a solution. I’ve had to learn this repeatedly. All my family members know that we eat dinner at 5:30. But a late arrival habit is trending, and it bothers me.

When I told my husband about the frustration, he simply said, “Why don’t you explain the issue and quit being so uptight about it?” Good point. Proactively seeking solutions works for many problem areas.

Imperfect women make good homemakers

Quit worrying about perfection and make decisions based on what is best for today. Fun-loving, happy, homemakers might have a few dust bunnies under the furniture, but they radiate an aura that draws people to their hearts and homes.

Everyone differs when it comes to how much we can handle. On the other hand, everyone is the same; we all have limits. In future installments, we will discuss how to deal with common points of overload.

Part 2

Many homemakers find themselves stretched thin among commitments that go with home, family, and other activities. As busy as we are, why do we continue to fill our schedules fuller?

It is easy for me to commit to a new project and then realize, halfway into the task, that I have overstepped my limits. Too often, I overestimate the amount of time I must have to complete a project and underestimate the amount of time a task will take.

Commitment overload happens by default. When we play multiple roles and add more responsibilities, we can easily become slaves to the promises we have made. Overload tends to drain our energy, dull our senses, and deaden our joy.

Recognizing Overload

Sometimes multiple activities take place in rapid sequence. Normally, we can flow with short-term spurts of busyness. But if the flow of activities is never-ending and we keep adding more obligations, we develop a pattern that becomes a way of life.

Too many commitments beyond normal duties make us candidates for depression and burnout. Personally, when I experience insomnia, apathy, or irritability, it is time to examine my schedule. If adjustments aren’t made, someone or something will suffer.

No one can overextend themselves indefinitely. Sometimes we suffer consequences for keeping a pace that is beyond our resources. Symptoms of overload can include lack of sleep, strained relationships, procrastination, fear of failure, and a susceptible immune system.

Breaking Free of Overload

Identifying overload takes an honest evaluation of yourself. How can you know if this is just a busy season or if busyness is the new normal? Are you declining a request because life is too full, or is it an excuse? Do you have to say “yes” on the spot? With practice, you can learn how to pull back before reaching the overload point.

Let an idea or request gel before committing

This has saved me a great deal of stress. There are so many good things to be involved in, and new inspirations come daily. Sometimes tasks can be incorporated into my/our schedule. Other times I must simply let them go and stay focused on what is most important. Consider waiting a few hours before incorporating new ideas and requests.

Seek advice, especially your husband’s

A renowned doughnut maker was asked to have a stand at an auction. She asked her husband what he thought about it. He said, “As long as you don’t complain and stress about it like you did last year, I don’t care.” Was her husband saying “yes” or “no”? This lady should take the cue that doughnut making was somehow adding stress. Either she should not do it, or together they must seek a workable solution.

Evaluate your schedule regularly

Keep a detailed calendar to have a picture of past, present, and future events. If your family had the flu last week and you plan to take an out-of-state trip next week, should you add more? What is the emotional health of your family? Is your husband stressed at work? Sometimes it is better to have a time slot of nothing so it can be filled with what is important now. You can’t do a good job at anything if you are spread too thin. Too many obligations make it hard to be personally refreshed and congenial. Choosing commitments wisely will help you invest your energy where it is most valuable for today.

Deel 1

Vir Alice is die lewe ergerlik. Elke dag voel soos ’n eindelose geswoeg. Sy is lief vir haar gesin, maar in haar hart vra sy af of dit waarvoor sy so hard werk enige verskil maak. Sy het nie altyd so oorlaai gevoel nie, en sy wonder wat verander het sodat sy so gereeld oorweldig voel.

Soms neem besig-wees so stadig toe dat ons die verandering skaars opmerk. Besig-wees, as dit ’n kans kry, sal ons oorlaai met meer verpligtinge as wat ons realisties in een dag, of een week, of selfs een leeftyd kan klaarkry. Dan, sonder waarskuwing, bereik ons die oorlaaipunt wanneer ons voel asof ons nie meer kan hanteer nie. Onophoudelike oorlading kan liggaamlike en geestelike uitputting veroorsaak tot die punt waar ons uitgeput voel van entoesiasme, energie en doel. Sommige vroue lyk asof hulle ’n ingeboude aanduiding het van waar die oorlaaigrens lê. Ander, soos ek self, sukkel om daardie balans te vind. Konstant. Daar is soveel goeie, interessante en opwindende moontlikhede binne ons bereik; sonder veel nadenke vul ons ons dae.

Konsepte wat tot oorlading bydra

Om meerdere rolle te speel kan stresvol wees. Jouself oorlaai met verantwoordelikhede en verpligtinge kan jou laat vergeet wat die belangrikste is. Dit is maklik om besig-wees met selfwaarde te vergelyk. Standaard begin ons glo dat:

  • Huisvroue in staat is om alles te hanteer.
  • Huisvroue, veral godvrugtige huisvroue, nooit gefrustreerd is nie.
  • ’n Huisvrou alle haar gesin se behoeftes vooraf behoort te voorsien.

As ons eerlik is, weet ons dat hierdie stellings onrealisties is. Huisvroue kan nie alles doen nie. Alle huisvroue ervaar soms frustrasie. ’n Ma kan nie konsekwent een tree voor haar gesin se behoeftes wees nie.

Hersien die besige lewe

Huishoudelike pligte en die versorging van ons gesinne vul ons dae. Soms maak daardie take alleen ons baie besig. Maar wat van die buitemuurse aktiwiteite of die hoë standaard waaraan ons onsself onderwerp? Ons mag anders moet dink sodat ons kan breek uit gewoontes wat dreig om ons te beheer.

Aanvaar jou perke

Miskien kan jy in een week by ’n Tupperware-partytjie gaan, by ’n Bybelstudie teenwoordig wees en die badkamer oopsit. Maar moet jy? Goeie huisvroue laat hulself toe om te vereenvoudig al verkies hulle om dit op ’n ander manier te doen. Dit beteken as jy ’n ywerige broodmaker is, is dit reg om ’n paar brode in jou inkopiemandjie te gooi.

Evalueer wat frustrasies veroorsaak

Kunsmatige glimlagte kan innerlike frustrasies wegsteek, maar dit genees dit nie. Dit werk die beste om te erken dat daar ’n probleem is en dan ’n oplossing te soek. Ek moes dit herhaaldelik leer. Al my gesinslede weet dat ons om 17:30 eet. Maar ’n trend van laat aankomsmis gewoonte ontstaan, en dit pla my.

Toe ek my man van die frustrasie vertel het, sê hy eenvoudig, “Hoekom verduidelik jy nie die probleem en hou op om so gespanne daaroor te wees?” Goeie punt. Proaktief oplossings soek werk vir baie probleemareas.

Onvolmaakte vroue maak goeie huisvroue

Hou op om oor volmaaktheid te bekommer en neem besluite op grond van wat die beste is vir vandag. Pret-liefhebbende, vrolike huisvroue mag ’n paar stofkonyns onder die meubels hê, maar hulle straal ’n aura uit wat mense na hul harte en huise trek.

Almal verskil wanneer dit kom by hoeveel ons kan hanteer. Aan die ander kant is almal dieselfde; ons het almal perke. In toekomstige aflewerings sal ons bespreek hoe om met algemene oorlaaipunte te werk.

Deel 2

Baie huisvroue vind hulself dun gestrek tussen verpligtinge wat by die huis, gesin en ander aktiwiteite hoort. So besig as wat ons is, waarom bly ons dan ons skedules voller maak?

Dit is maklik vir my om by ’n nuwe projek aan te meld en dan, halfpad deur die taak, te besef dat ek my perke oorskry het. Te dikwels oorskat ek die hoeveelheid tyd wat ek nodig het om ’n projek te voltooi en onderskat ek die hoeveelheid tyd ’n taak sal neem.

Toewysing-oorlading gebeur by verstek. Wanneer ons meerdere rolle speel en meer verantwoordelikhede byvoeg, kan ons maklik slawe van die beloftes wat ons gemaak het word. Oorlading neig om ons energie te droog te maak, ons sintuie te verskerp—sorry—te verslui, en ons vreugde te verdoof.

Herken oorlading

Soms vind baie aktiwiteite in vinnige opvolg plaas. Normaalweg kan ons met korttermyn-uitbarstings van besig-wees meevloei. Maar as die vloei van aktiwiteite nooit eindig nie en ons bly meer verpligtinge byvoeg, ontwikkel ons ’n patroon wat ’n leefwyse word.

Te veel verpligtinge bo normale pligte maak ons kandidaat vir depressie en uitbranding. Persoonlik, wanneer ek slapeloosheid, apatie of prikkelbaarheid ervaar, is dit tyd om my skedule te ondersoek. As aanpassings nie gemaak word nie, sal iemand of iets ly.

Nobody kan hulleself oneindig ooruit strek. Soms ly ons aan gevolge vir die handhawing van ’n pas wat ons hulpbronne oorskry. Simptome van oorlading kan insluit ’n gebrek aan slaap, gespanne verhoudings, uitstel, vrees vir mislukking, en ’n vatbare immuunstelsel.

Breek vry van oorlading

Om oorlading te identifiseer vereis ’n eerlike evaluering van jouself. Hoe kan jy weet of dit net ’n besige seisoen is of as besig-wees die nuwe normaal is? Weier jy ’n versoek omdat die lewe te vol is, of is dit ’n verskoning? Moet jy dadelik “ja” sê? Met oefening kan jy leer hoe om terug te trek voordat jy die oorlaaipunt bereik.

Laat ’n idee of versoek sit voordat jy toewy

Dit het my baie spanning bespaar. Daar is soveel goeie dinge om by betrokke te raak, en nuwe inspirasies kom daagliks. Soms kan take in my/onsskedule ingesluit word. Ander kere moet ek dit eenvoudig laat gaan en fokus op wat die belangrikste is. Oorweeg om ’n paar uur te wag voordat jy nuwe idees en versoeke insluit.

Soek advies, veral van jou man

’n Bekende doughnutmaker is gevra om ’n stalletjie by ’n veiling te hê. Sy het haar man gevra wat hy daarvan dink. Hy sê, “Solank jy nie kla en jou daaroor stres soos verlede jaar nie, gee dit my niks om.” Was haar man “ja” of “nee” sê? Hierdie dame moet die aanduiding neem dat doughnutmaak op een of ander manier stres bygevoeg het. Of sy moet dit nie doen nie, of saam moet hulle ’n werkbare oplossing probeer vind.

Evalueer jou skedule gereeld

Hou ’n gedetailleerde kalender om ’n prentjie van verlede, hede en toekomstige gebeure te hê. As jou gesin verlede week die griep gehad het en jy beplan om volgende week ’n reis buite staat te maak, moet jy nog byvoeg? Wat is die emosionele gesondheid van jou gesin? Is jou man gestres by die werk? Soms is dit beter om ’n tydgleuf van niks te hê sodat dit gevul kan word met wat nou belangrik is. Jy kan nie ’n goeie werk by enigiets doen as jy te veel versprei is nie. Te veel verpligtinge maak dit moeilik om persoonlik verfris en aangenaam te wees. Kies verpligtinge wyslik sal jou help om jou energie te belê waar dit vandag die meeste waarde het.

It's incredible to me to see how God uses His people throughout history to bring glory to His name. He uses the weak things to confound the wise; the base things to bring to nothing the wisdom of earthly wise men. God uses physical weakness, hardship, loss, grief, toil, and pain to increase our spiritual treasures and build His Kingdom here on the earth!

This hymn became precious to my family and me several years ago as we awaited the birth of our fourth genetically challenged baby. We knew she couldn't stay with us very long. She passed away at just three days old. After researching this hymn, I was amazed to find out that the man whose story had inspired this hymn had lost eight out of his nine children.

The story of this man is a notable one. His 61 years on earth were marked by grief and loss, persecution and imprisonment. Yet, his dedication to Christ was outstanding, and his fire for God and zeal for preaching the gospel never waned until his last day.

Samuel Rutherford, son of a prosperous farmer, was born in the year 1600. His life began in the small village of Nisbet, Scotland. As we glimpse into his life, we notice the hand of God at work in Samuel’s early years. At only three years old, he was playing with his friends when he fell into the town well. His sister and friends ran to get help. When they returned, they found a very wet Samuel sitting on the grass beside the well. They asked him how he got out, and his reply was, "A bonny white man came and drew me out of the well." His family believed that God sent an angel to rescue him that day.

From what we know about Samuel Rutherford, he had two brothers and one sister. He was sent to school when he was young, and he became a very diligent scholar. He learned Latin and Greek so well that he eventually became a professor. He married Eupham Hamilton around 1624, soon after he began teaching at Edinburgh University. At this time, Samuel was yet unconverted and cared only for pursuing his academic goals.

In 1626, at the age of 26, Samuel came to a clear and saving faith in the Lord Jesus Christ. He said, "O but Christ hath a saving eye. When He first looked on me I was saved. It cost Him but a look to make hell quit to me." From that moment he was filled with a passion to preach and to speak about his Saviour. This change of life caused such a stir in the university that Rutherford ended up resigning his professorship.

In 1627, Samuel took his wife and two young children to Galloway, Scotland, where he began pastoring the small church of Anwoth. As he commenced his calling there he said, "I have received the commission from the royal and princely Master, my Lord Jesus, to preach Christ to the people." His passion was for the conversion of the people, and it is said that he seemed to be always praying, always preaching, always visiting the sick, always teaching and instructing, always writing or studying. The zeal with which he preached and his concern for the welfare of his congregation had a great effect on them. Not only them, but folks came from the surrounding towns and villages to hear his preaching. A friend once reported, "Many times I thought he would have flown out of the pulpit when he came to speak of Jesus Christ."

Samuel was not estranged from grief and sorrow. In 1631, only four short years after he began his work as a pastor, his wife passed away. His two children also became ill and left this world. In 1636, after nine years of preaching, he was banished to Aberdeen, where he was forbidden to preach the gospel. This was a very difficult time for him as he greatly missed his wife and children as well as his congregation, the Church at Anwoth. This time in his life is indeed one reason he is so well remembered, for he began writing letters back to his church people and friends. Out of the 365 letters he wrote, 220 of them were written during these 22 months of banishment.

The government eventually changed hands, which gave more liberty to the non-conformist Covenanters. Thereupon Rutherford quickly returned to his beloved flock at Anwoth. About a year later, in the fall of 1639, he again reluctantly left Anwoth but this time to fulfill an appointment to become Professor of Divinity at St Mary's College in St. Andrews. This change was difficult for him, as he again greatly missed his congregation. He writes, "My removal from my flock is so heavy to me, that it maketh my life a burden to me, I had never such a longing for death. The Lord help and hold up this sad clay."

After five months in his new position and having been alone for nearly ten years, the 40-year-old Samuel married Jean McMath. Together they had seven children. Sadly, six of them died in infancy and early childhood. Only a daughter named Agnes survived to adulthood.

Rutherford continued to be an influential leader in the non-conformist movement in Scotland for the next 20 years until 1660. With the death of Cromwell, the rule of the commonwealth came to an end, and Charles II was restored to power. Once again, the wrath of the monarchy fell on Samuel. He was summoned to appear before the judge and charged with high treason against the government for preaching the truth. He was put in prison to await execution. However, before the king could put him to death, Samuel became quite sick. He said, "I have a summons already from a superior Judge, and I behoove to answer my first summons and when your day arrives I shall be where few Kings and great folks come."

Late in the afternoon of the last day of his life in answer to the question, "What think ye now of Christ?" answered thusly, "Oh, that all my brethren in the land may know what a Master I have served, and what peace I have this day! I shall sleep in Christ, and when I awake, I shall be satisfied with His likeness. This night shall close the door, and put my anchor within the veil, and I shall go away in a sleep by five of the clock in the morning. Glory! glory to my Creator and my Redeemer forever! I Shall live and adore Him. Oh, for arms to embrace Him! Oh, for a well-tuned harp! Glory! glory dwelleth in Immanuel's land!" These words were heard by his wife, daughter and friends, and he was indeed with his Lord by five in the morning.

Nearly two centuries later, Annie Ross Cousin, a Scottish poet and hymn writer and the wife of a minister, was inspired by the life and writings of Samuel Rutherford. She summarized his life in a biographical hymn,"The Sands of Time are Sinking". This hymn was first published in 1857 in the Christian Treasury. Out of the nineteen original verses, only four are used in our hymn books. (in bold copy)

The sands of time are sinking,
The dawn of heaven breaks,
The summer morn I’ve sighed for,
The fair, sweet morn awakes:
Dark, dark hath been the midnight,
But dayspring is at hand,
And glory—glory dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land.

2. Oh! well it is forever,
Oh! well forevermore
My nest hung in no forest
Of all this death-doomed shore!
Yea, let the vain world vanish,
As from the ship the stand,
While glory—glory dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land.

3. There the Red Rose of Sharon
Unfolds its heart-most bloom.
And fills the air of Heaven
With ravishing perfume;
Oh, to behold its blossom,
While by its fragrance fann’d
Where glory—glory dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land.

4. The King there in His beauty,
Without a veil is seen:
It were a well-spent journey
Though seven deaths lay between:
The Lamb with His fair army,
Doth on Mount Zion stand;
And glory—glory dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land.

5. Oh! Christ He is the fountain,
The deep sweet well of Love!
The streams on earth I’ve tasted,
More deep I’ll drink above;
There, to an ocean fullness,
His mercy doth expand,
And glory—glory dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land.

6. E’en Anwoth was not heaven—
E’en preaching was not Christ;
And in my sea-beat prison
My Lord and I held tryst:
And aye my murkiest storm-cloud
Was by a rainbow spann’d,
Caught from the glory dwelling
In Immanuel’s land.

7. But that He built a heaven
Of His surpassing love,
A little New Jerus’lem,
Like to the one above,—
“Lord, take me o’er the water,”
Had been my loud demand,
“Take me to love’s own country,
Unto Immanuel’s land.”

8. But flowers need night’s cool darkness,
The moonlight and the dew;
So Christ, from one who loved it,
His shining oft withdrew;
And then, for cause of absence,
My troubled soul I scann’d—
But glory, shadeless, shineth
In Immanuel’s land.

9. The little birds of Anwoth,
used to count them blest,—
Now, beside happier alters,
go to built my nest:
O’er these there broods no silence,
No graves around them stand,
For glory, deathless, dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land.

10. Fair Anwoth by the Solway,
To me thou still art dear!
E’en from the verge of Heaven
I drop for thee a tear.
Oh! if one soul from Anwoth
Meet me at God’s right hand,
My Heaven will be two Heavens,
In Immanuel’s land!

11. I’ve wrestled on towards Heaven,
‘Ganst storm, and wind, and tide;—
Now, like a weary traveler,
That leaneth on his guide,
Amid the shades of evening,
While sinks life’s ling’ring sand,
I hail the glory dawning
From Immanuel’s land.

12. Deep waters cross’d life’s pathway,
The hedge of thorns was sharp;
Now these lie all behind me,—
Oh, for a well-tuned harp!
Oh, to join Hallelujah
With yon triumphant band,
Who sing where glory dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land!

13. With mercy and with judgment
My web of time He wove,
And aye the dews of sorrow
Were lustered with His love!
I’ll bless the hand that guided,
I’ll bless the heart that plann’d,
When throned where glory dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land.

14. Soon shall the cup of glory
Wash down earth’s bitterest woes,
Soon shall the desert brier
Break into Eden’s rose:
The curse shall change to blessing–
The name on earth that’s bann’d,
Be graven on the white stone
In Immanuel’s land.

15. Oh! I am my Beloved’s,
And my Beloved’s mine!
He brings a poor vile sinner
Into His “house of wine:”
I stand upon His merit,
I know no other stand,
Not e’en where glory dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land.

16. I shall sleep sound in Jesus,
Fill’d with His likeness rise,
To live and to adore Him,
To see Him with these eyes:
‘Tween me and resurrection
But Paradise doth stand;
Then—then for glory dwelling
In Immanuel’s land!

17. The bride eyes not her garment,
But her dear Bridegroom’s face;
I will not gaze at glory,
But on my King of Grace—
Not at the crown He giveth,
But on His pierced hand:
The Lamb is all the glory
Of Immanuel’s land.

18. I have borne scorn and hatred,
I have borne wrong and shame,
Earth’s proud ones have reproach’d me,
For Christ’s thrice blessed name:
Where God His seal set fairest
They’ve stamp’d their foulest brand;
But judgment shines like noonday
In Immanuel’s land.

19. They’ve summoned me before them,
But there I may not come,—
My Lord says, “Come up hither,”
My Lord says, “Welcome home!
My King now at His white throne,
My presence doth command,
Where glory—glory dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land.

The fine complementary tune for this text was composed in the early 1800s by a French musician, Chretien D`Urhan. It is well fitted to the words of the hymn—its solemn tempo matches the solemnity of the words. The rising melodic line of the last phrase perfectly matches the anticipated joy expressed by the refrain—"And glory, glory dwelleth in Immanuel's land."

As we conclude this hymn history, let us continue to marvel at the providence of God in the lives of those who have gone before us. May we follow Christ with all our hearts and be vessels ready for the Master's use! One last quote by Samuel Rutherford to take with us. "They lose nothing who gain Christ."

역사를 통틀어 하나님께서 자신의 백성을 어떻게 사용하셔서 자신의 이름에 영광을 돌리시는지를 보는 일은 나에게 놀라운 일입니다. 하나님은 약한 것들을 사용하여 지혜로운 자들을 당혹케 하시고, 천한 것들을 사용하여 세상 지식의 지혜를 무너뜨리십니다. 하나님은 우리의 영적 보화를 더하시고 이 땅에 자신의 왕국을 세우기 위해 육체적 연약함, 고난, 상실, 슬픔, 수고, 그리고 고통을 사용하십니다!

이 찬송은 몇 년 전 우리 가족과 나에게 소중한 것이 되었습니다. 우리는 유전적으로 문제가 있는 네 번째 아이의 탄생을 기다리고 있었고, 그녀가 우리와 오래 있지 못할 것임을 알고 있었습니다. 그녀는 단지 사흘 만에 세상을 떠났습니다. 이 찬송을 조사해 본 후, 이 찬송에 영감을 준 한 사람의 이야기가 그의 아홉 자녀 중 여덟을 잃었다는 사실을 알게 되어 나는 놀랐습니다.

이 사람의 이야기는 주목할 만합니다. 그가 이 땅에서 보낸 61년은 슬픔과 상실, 박해와 투옥으로 점철되어 있었습니다. 그럼에도 불구하고 그리스도를 향한 그의 헌신은 탁월했고, 하나님에 대한 그의 불같은 열정과 복음을 전하려는 열심은 마지막 날까지 결코 사그라들지 않았습니다.

사무엘 러더퍼드(Samuel Rutherford)는 부유한 농부의 아들로 1600년에 태어났습니다. 그의 삶은 스코틀랜드의 작은 마을 니스벳(Nisbet)에서 시작되었습니다. 그의 생애를 들여다보면 사무엘의 어린 시절에 역사하신 하나님의 손길을 볼 수 있습니다. 겨우 세 살 때 그는 친구들과 놀다가 마을 우물에 빠졌습니다. 그의 누이와 친구들은 도움을 청하러 달려갔습니다. 그들이 돌아왔을 때 그들은 우물 옆 잔디에 앉아 매우 젖어 있는 사무엘을 발견했습니다. 그들이 그가 어떻게 나왔는지 물었을 때, 그의 대답은 "한 아름다운 흰 옷을 입은 사람이 와서 나를 우물에서 끌어내 주었다"였습니다. 그의 가족은 그날 하나님께서 한 천사를 보내 그를 구하셨다고 믿었습니다.

우리가 사무엘 러더퍼드에 대해 아는 바로는, 그는 두 형제와 한 여동생이 있었습니다. 그는 어렸을 때 학교에 보내졌고 아주 부지런한 학자가 되었습니다. 그는 라틴어와 그리스어를 매우 잘 배워 결국 교수직을 맡게 되었습니다. 그는 1624년경, 에든버러 대학교에서 가르치기 시작한 직후 유팜 해밀턴(Eupham Hamilton)과 결혼했습니다. 이때 사무엘은 아직 회심하지 않았고 학문적 목표만을 추구했습니다.

1626년, 26세에 사무엘은 주 예수 그리스도 안에서 분명하고 구원에 이르는 믿음을 갖게 되었습니다. 그는 "오, 그러나 그리스도께서는 구원하시는 눈을 가지셨다. 그가 처음 나를 보실 때 나는 구원받았다. 나를 구원하는 데 그에게 드는 것은 오직 한 번의 눈길이었다."고 말했습니다. 그 순간부터 그는 자신의 구주에 대해 전하고 말하려는 열정으로 충만했습니다. 이러한 삶의 변화는 대학교에 엄청난 파문을 일으켜 결국 러더퍼드는 교수직을 사임하게 되었습니다.

1627년, 사무엘은 아내와 두 어린 자녀를 데리고 스코틀랜드의 갤러웨이(Galloway)로 가서 작은 안워스(Anwoth) 교회의 목회 사역을 시작했습니다. 그는 그곳에서 소명을 시작하면서 "나는 왕이신 주 나의 예수님으로부터 백성들에게 그리스도를 전하라는 사명을 받았다."고 말했습니다. 그의 열정은 백성들의 회심을 향한 것이었고, 그는 항상 기도하는 것 같고, 항상 설교하는 것 같고, 항상 병자를 방문하는 것 같고, 항상 가르치고 가르침을 주는 것 같고, 항상 글을 쓰거나 연구하는 것 같았다고 전해집니다. 그가 전한 설교의 열정과 회중의 복지에 대한 그의 관심은 그들에게 큰 영향을 미쳤습니다. 그들뿐 아니라 주변 마을과 촌락의 사람들도 그의 설교를 들으러 왔습니다. 한 친구는 이렇게 보고했습니다. "그가 예수 그리스도에 대해 말할 때 몇 번이나 설교단에서 날아갈 것 같았다."

사무엘은 슬픔과 비탄에서 멀리 떨어져 있지 않았습니다. 1631년, 목회 사역을 시작한 지 불과 4년 만에 그의 아내가 세상을 떠났습니다. 그의 두 자녀도 병들어 이 세상을 떠났습니다. 1636년, 9년간의 설교 후 그는 단죄되어 아베르딘(Aberdeen)으로 유배되었고, 그곳에서 복음을 전하는 것이 금지되었습니다. 그는 그의 아내와 자녀들뿐 아니라 그의 회중인 안워스 교회를 몹시 그리워했기 때문에 이 시기는 그에게 매우 힘든 시간이었습니다. 그의 삶의 이 시기는 그가 매우 기억되는 한 이유이기도 한데, 그는 자기 교인들과 친구들에게 편지를 쓰기 시작했습니다. 그가 쓴 365통의 편지 가운데 220통이 이 22개월의 유배 기간에 쓰여졌습니다.

그 후 정부가 교체되어 비순응파 언약자들에게 더 많은 자유가 주어졌습니다. 그리하여 러더퍼드는 사랑하는 안워스 회중에게 재빨리 돌아왔습니다. 약 1년 후, 1639년 가을 그는 다시 마지못해 안워스를 떠났지만 이번에는 세인트앤드루스의 세인트메리스 대학(St Mary's College)에서 신학 교수로 임명된 직무를 수행하기 위해서였습니다. 이 변화는 그에게 어려웠고, 그는 또다시 그의 회중을 크게 그리워했습니다. 그는 "내가 내 양 떼를 떠나는 것은 내게 너무 무겁기에, 내 삶을 나에게 짐으로 만든다. 나는 결코 이토록 죽음을 갈망해 본 적이 없다. 주께서 이 슬픈 흙을 도우시고 붙드소서."라고 적었습니다.

새 직위에서 다섯 달을 지내고 거의 십 년 동안 혼자 지낸 뒤, 40세의 사무엘은 장 진 맥매스(Jean McMath)와 결혼했습니다. 그들 사이에는 일곱 자녀가 태어났습니다. 슬프게도 그들 중 여섯은 유아기와 어린 시절에 사망했습니다. 다만 애그니스(Agnes)라는 딸 하나만이 성인으로 성장했습니다.

러더퍼드는 이후 1660년까지 향후 20년 동안 스코틀랜드 비순응파 운동에서 영향력 있는 지도자로 계속 활동했습니다. 크롬웰의 죽음으로 공화정의 통치는 끝났고 찰스 2세가 권력을 회복했습니다. 다시 한 번 군주의 분노가 사무엘에게 떨어졌습니다. 그는 법정에 소환되어 국가에 대한 반역죄로 기소되었는데 그 이유는 진리를 설교했기 때문이었습니다. 그는 처형을 기다리며 감옥에 수감되었습니다. 그러나 왕이 그를 사형에 처하기 전에 사무엘은 병에 걸렸습니다. 그는 "나는 이미 더 높은 심판자에게 소환장을 받았고, 나는 나의 첫 소환에 응답해야 한다. 너희의 날이 임할 때 나는 몇몇 왕들과 위대한 사람들은 오지 못하는 곳에 있을 것이다."라고 말했습니다.

그가 삶의 마지막 날 오후 늦게 "이제 그리스도에 대해 어떻게 생각하느냐?"는 질문에 이렇게 답했습니다. "오, 이 땅의 내 모든 형제들이 내가 섬겨온 주가 어떠하였는지, 그리고 오늘 내가 가진 평화가 어떠한지 알게 되기를! 나는 그리스도 안에서 잠들 것이다. 깨어나면 나는 그의 형상을 보고 만족하리라. 이 밤은 문을 닫고 내 닻을 휘장 안에 두리니, 나는 아침 다섯 시쯤에 잠에 들어 떠나리라. 영광! 나의 창조주와 나의 구속자께 영원한 영광! 나는 살아 그를 경배하리라. 오, 그를 껴안을 수 있는 팔이 있기를! 오, 잘 조율된 수금이 있기를! 영광! 영광이 임마누엘의 땅에 거하도다!" 이 말들은 그의 아내와 딸과 친구들이 들었고, 그는 아침 다섯 시에 실제로 그의 주님과 함께 있었습니다.

거의 두 세기 후, 스코틀랜드의 시인이자 찬송가 작가이며 한 목사의 아내였던 애니 로스 커즌(Annie Ross Cousin)은 사무엘 러더퍼드의 생애와 저작에서 영감을 받았습니다. 그녀는 그의 삶을 전기적 찬송 "The Sands of Time are Sinking"으로 요약했습니다. 이 찬송은 1857년 Christian Treasury에 처음 실렸습니다. 원래의 19절 가운데 우리 찬송책에는 단지 네 절만 사용됩니다. (굵은 글로 복사됨)

시간의 모래는 가라앉고,
천국의 새벽이 밝아오네,
내가 갈망하던 여름의 아침이여,
그 아름답고 달콤한 아침이 깨어나네:
어둠, 어둠은 자욱한 한밤이었으나,
새벽이 가까이 왔네,
그리고 영광—영광이 거하네
임마누엘의 땅에.

2. 오! 영원히 좋은 것이여,
오! 영원토록 좋은 것이여
내 둥지는 어느 숲에도 매달리지 않네
이 죽음이 정한 해안의 어느 곳에도!
그래, 헛된 세상은 사라지게 하라,
배에서 떨어져 나가는 돛처럼,
그 사이에 영광—영광이 거하네
임마누엘의 땅에.

3. 그곳에 샤론의 붉은 장미가
그 가장 깊은 꽃망울을 펼치네.
그리고 천국의 공기를 가득 채우네
황홀한 향기로;
오, 그 꽃을 바라보기를,
그 향기에 부채질되며
그 곳에 영광—영광이 거하네
임마누엘의 땅에.

4. 그 왕이 거기 그의 아름다움으로
베일 없이 보이네:
비록 일곱 번의 죽음이 가로놓여 있어도
그 여정은 잘 보낸 여행이라 하리라:
어린 양이 그의 아름다운 군대와 함께
시온 산에 서 있네;
그리고 영광—영광이 거하네
임마누엘의 땅에.

5. 오! 그리스도는 샘이시며,
깊고 달콤한 사랑의 우물이시라!
내가 땅에서 맛본 시냇물보다
위에서 더 깊이 마리라;
그곳에서 바다 같은 충만함으로,
그의 자비가 펼쳐지네,
그리고 영광—영광이 거하네
임마누엘의 땅에.

6. 심지어 안워스도 천국은 아니었고—
설교하는 것이 곧 그리스도가 아니었네;
그리고 나의 파도에 부딪힌 감옥 안에서
나의 주와 나는 약속을 나누었네:
그리고 언제나 나의 가장 어두운 폭풍구름은
무지개로 가로질러졌네,
영광이 거하는 곳에서 잡힌 빛이여
임마누엘의 땅에서.

7. 그러나 그가 그의 초월적 사랑으로
천국을 지었고,
위의 것과 같은 작은 새 예루살렘을,—
"주여, 나를 물 건너로 데려가소서,"
내가 크게 요구했을 것이다,
"나를 사랑의 고향으로 데려가소서,
임마누엘의 땅으로."

8. 그러나 꽃들은 밤의 서늘한 어둠을 필요로 하고,
달빛과 이슬을 필요로 하네;
그러므로 그리스도께서는, 그것을 사랑하던 사람에게서
그의 광채를 자주 거두셨네;
그리고 그 부재 때문에
나의 괴로운 영혼을 살폈네—
그러나 영광은 그늘 없는 빛을 발하네
임마누엘의 땅에서.

9. 안워스의 작은 새들,
그들을 복되다 여겼었네,—
이제 더 행복한 제단 옆에서
나의 둥지를 지으러 가네:
그들 위에는 침묵이 깃들지 않고,
무덤이 그들 주위에 서 있지 않네,
영광이, 죽지 않음이 거하네
임마누엘의 땅에.

10. 솔웨이(Solway) 옆의 아름다운 안워스여,
너는 여전히 내게 소중하도다!
천국의 가장자리에서조차
나는 너를 위해 눈물을 떨어뜨리네.
오! 만일 안워스에서 한 영혼이
하나님의 오른손에서 나를 만나면,
나의 천국은 두 천국이 되리라,
임마누엘의 땅에서!

11. 나는 천국을 향해 씨름하며 나아왔네,
폭풍과 바람과 조류와 싸우며;—
이제, 지친 여행자처럼,
그의 안내자에 기대는 자처럼,
저녁의 어둠 속에서,
생명의 남은 모래가 가라앉을 때,
나는 임마누엘의 땅에서
떠오르는 영광을 맞이하네.

12. 깊은 물들이 생의 길을 건넜고,
가시의 울타리는 날카로웠네;
이제 이 모든 것은 내 뒤에 놓였네,—
오, 잘 조율된 수금이여!
오, 저 승리의 무리와 함께
알렐루야에 참여하리라
그들이 노래하는 곳, 영광이 거하는 곳에서
임마누엘의 땅에!

13. 자비와 심판으로
나의 시간의 직물을 그가 짰고,
항상 슬픔의 이슬은
그의 사랑으로 빛났네!
나는 인도한 손을 찬양하리라,
계획한 마음을 찬양하리라,
그가 왕좌에 앉아 영광이 거하는 곳에서
임마누엘의 땅에.

14. 곧 영광의 잔이
땅의 가장 쓰라린 고통을 씻어주리라,
곧 사막의 가시덤불이
에덴의 장미로 피어나리라:
저주가 축복으로 바뀌리니–
땅에서 금지된 그 이름이여,
희고 빛나는 돌에 새겨지리라
임마누엘의 땅에서.

15. 오! 나는 나의 사랑하는 이의 것이요,
나의 사랑하는 이는 나의 것이네!
그는 비천한 죄인을 데려오사
그의 "포도주 집"으로 들이시네:
나는 그의 공로 위에 서 있나니,
다른 어떤 버팀목도 알지 못하리라,
심지어 영광이 거하는 곳에서도
임마누엘의 땅에.

16. 나는 예수 안에서 평안히 잘 것이요,
그의 형상으로 충만하여 일어나리라,
살아 그를 찬양하고 경배하며,
그의 얼굴을 보리라:
나와 부활 사이에는
오직 낙원이 놓여 있네;
그러면—그때는 영광이 거하리라
임마누엘의 땅에!

17. 신부는 자신의 옷이 아니라
사랑하는 신랑의 얼굴을 보네;
나는 영광을 바라보지 않으리라,
오직 은혜의 내 왕을—
그가 주는 왕관을 보지 않으리라,
오직 그의 찔린 손을 보리라:
어린 양이 임마누엘의 땅의 모든 영광이네.

18. 나는 멸시와 증오를 견디어왔고,
부당함과 수치를 견디어왔네,
세상의 교만한 자들이 나를 비난했네,
그리스도의 세 번 복된 이름 때문에:
하나님께서 가장 공정하게 도장을 찍으신 곳에
그들은 가장 더러운 낙인을 찍었네;
그러나 심판은 한낮처럼 빛나리라
임마누엘의 땅에서.

19. 그들이 나를 그들 앞에 소환했으나,
나는 거기에 올 수 없으리라,—
나의 주께서 "이리 올라오라" 말씀하시네,"
나의 주께서 "집에 오신 것을 환영하노라" 말씀하시네!
나의 왕이 지금 그의 흰 보좌에 계시고,
나의 임재가 명령하네,
그 곳에 영광—영광이 거하네
임마누엘의 땅에서.

이 가사에 잘 어울리는 세련된 보완 선율은 1800년대 초 프랑스 음악가 크레티앵 뒤르한(Chretien D`Urhan)에 의해 작곡되었습니다. 그 선율은 찬송의 가사에 잘 맞아 그 의례적인 템포는 가사의 엄숙함과 어울립니다. 마지막 구절의 상승 멜로디는 후렴구의 기대된 기쁨—"And glory, glory dwelleth in Immanuel's land."—을 완벽하게 맞춥니다.

이 찬송의 역사를 마무리하면서 우리보다 먼저 간 이들의 삶에 역사하신 하나님의 섭리에 계속 놀라워합시다. 우리가 온 마음으로 그리스도를 따르며 주인의 쓰임에 준비된 그릇이 되기를 소망합니다! 사무엘 러더퍼드의 마지막 한마디를 함께 가집시다. "그리스도를 얻는 자는 아무것도 잃지 아니하리라."
