Through the Gospel

“In whom the god of this world hath blinded the minds of them which believe not, lest the light of the glorious gospel of Christ, who is the image of God, should shine unto them. For we preach not ourselves, but Christ Jesus the Lord; and ourselves your servants for Jesus' sake. For God, who commanded the light to shine out of darkness, hath shined in our hearts, to give the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ” (2 Corinthians 4:4-6). Katika uzito wa Mateso ya Kristo, tunapata uzuri wa kina na wa kukasirisha— uzuri wa dhabihu iliyofanywa na Mwokozi asiye na dhambi kwa wanadamu wasioostahili. Wakati mwingine aina ya uzuri unaogusa moyo zaidi hupatikana katika vitu ambavyo hatuwezi vyao kuelewa kikamilifu.

Kuna uzuri katika kilio cha Mariamu na wanafunzi karibu na msalaba uliohifadhi mwili usio na uhai wa Mwalimu wao aliyewapenda. Lakini alfajiri ilipotokea siku ya ufufuko, kukata tamaa kuligeuka kuwa matumaini na huzuni kuwa furaha.

Tunaona tukio la uzuri katika Mlima wa Mizeituni siku arobaini baadaye wakati wanafunzi hao walipotazama kwa kusikitisha angani, wakitazama Bwana wao aliyefufuka akitoweka mbinguni. Kwa furaha kuu, walirudi Yerusalemu, na ahadi ya kurudi Kwake ikiwa moto moyoni mwao, kusubiri kuja kwa Roho Mtakatifu.

Leo tunasubiri kwa matumaini Mwana wa Mungu aonekane kutoka mbinguni kwa nguvu na utukufu mkubwa kukamilisha kazi ya wokovu. Ndipo tutakapotazama Yeye katika utukufu na uzuri Wake wote. “For now we see through a glass, darkly; but then face to face: now I know in part; but then shall I know even as also I am known” (1 Corinthians 13:12).

Tunawezaje sisi, kama wabeba-kielelezo wa Mungu, kuakisha uzuri Wake kupitia Injili? Mungu ni kiumbe asiyeumbika wa milele, na mwanadamu aliumbwa kwa kielelezo chake ili kuakisha utukufu na uzuri Wake. Hata hivyo, uzuri huu umeharibika kwa dhambi na hauwezi tena kuwa mwakilishi stahili wa tabia ya Mungu. Lakini, kuna ufufuzi! Hakuna kinachozidi uzuri wa maisha yaliyokuwa vilivyopasuka na kuvunjika kwa dhambi lakini sasa yamerudishwa, yameokolewa, na kupewa uzima kamili kwa Injili. “To appoint unto them that mourn in Zion, to give unto them beauty for ashes, the oil of joy for mourning, the garment of praise for the spirit of heaviness; that they might be called trees of righteousness, the planting of the LORD, that He might be glorified” (Isaiah 61:3). Wamfuasi wa kutokuwepo kwa Mungu wanapinga uhai wa Mungu, wanasayansi wanapingana na uumbaji wa Biblia, wanataaluma wanauliza ukamilifu wa maandiko, lakini hakuna mtu anayeweza kupinga ushuhuda wa maisha yaliyookolewa.

Through Creation

“The heavens declare the glory of God; and the firmament showeth His handy work” (Psalm 19:1). Uzuri wote katika ulimwengu ulioumbwa unatoka kwa Mungu. Machweo mazuri, waridi mzuri, mti mkubwa wa redwood, kilele cha mlima chenye hadhi, vyote vinaonyesha uzuri wa Mungu uliolengwa katika uumbaji. Kama alama za barabara kwenye barabara kuu zinatuongoza kwenye hatima yetu, vivyo hivyo, uumbaji unaelekeza binadamu kwa Mungu mwenyewe. “For the invisible things of Him from the creation of the world are clearly seen . . .” (Romans 1:20). Zawadi hizi za uumbaji zimetolewa kutupatia mtazamo mfupi wa Yule aliyewaumba.

Tunawezaje sisi, kama sehemu ya uumbaji wa Mungu, kuakisha uzuri Wake wa uumbaji? Ingawa hatuwezi kuumba kitu kutoka kwa chochote, Mungu ametutengeneza tuwe wabunifu, tukitumia rasilimali za uumbaji Wake na uwezo wetu wa akili kufanya maisha yawe ya utekelezaji. Hisia ya kuridhika inayotokana na kazi iliyofanywa vizuri ina asili yake katika uumbaji, ambapo Mungu alitazama kazi Yake na kusema ilikuwa nzuri. Katika jitihada zetu za kuishi maisha yasiyo ya kutawanyika mara nyingine tunashindwa kuchukua furaha katika vitu vya uzuri maishani. Ni sawa na ni jema na inakubaliana na jinsi tulivyoundwa kufurahia vitu vya uzuri. Watu wasiokuwa wa Mungu wamewahi kutumia zawadi hii ya ubunifu mara nyingi kwa madhumuni mabaya. Hivyo basi, twendelee kumtukuza Mungu kwa kutumia uumbaji Wake kwa njia zinazoakisha tabia Yake.

Tahadhari kwa wote wanaopenda asili na uumbaji (wa asili na wa binadamu): tuwe waangalifu kutoainisha uzuri wa duniani juu ya Muumba, jambo linalopelekea ibada za sanamu. Machweo yanapotea, miti ya redwood huanguka, waridi hukauka, mwili wa binadamu hubadilika kuwa vumbi tena, lakini Mungu anabaki. Maisha na uzuri wake wote huanza na kumalizika na Mungu.

Through Music and Sound

“And I heard a voice from heaven, as the voice of many waters, and as the voice of a great thunder: and I heard the voice of harpers harping with their harps” (Revelation 14:2) Kulingana na kitabu cha Ufunuo, kiti cha enzi cha Mungu kimezungukwa na sauti: radi na umeme; sifa zinotiririka kutoka kwa malaika, viumbe wanne na wazee ishirini, na umati mkubwa ambao hakuna mtu anayejua idadi yake; na wimbo mpya uliotolewa na wachache mia moja na arobaini na nne.

Mungu aliumba uzuri wa sauti kumtukuza mwenyewe kwa njia ambazo maneno pekee hayawezi. Ugumu wa ubunifu Wake unaonyeshwa kwa nguvu katika jinsi miondoko mbalimbali ya sauti zinavyojumuika kuunda muafaka mzuri wa mbinguni. Ni heshima kwa Mungu kwa binadamu kuchukua furaha katika uzuri wa sauti alizoumba kwa utukufu Wake. Mtu ambaye anampenda Mungu atavutiwa kwake wakati wowote anapofurahia sauti zinazoifaa: watu wa Mungu wakiimba nyimbo za Sioni, maombi ya watakatifu, upepo ukipiga kati ya matawi ya miti, ndege mchungaji akimtukuza Muumba wake, radi taratibu, au patapaka ya mvua juu ya paa.

Tunawezaje sisi, kama vyombo vya sauti, kuakisha uzuri wa Mungu kupitia sauti? Tunapaswa daima kutafuta kusikiliza na kufanana na sauti na midundo ya mbinguni. Ingawa hatutaweza kabisa kutimiza hili duniani, inapaswa kuwa jitihada ya maisha yote. Maswali yameulizwa, “Je, tunapaswa kila wakati kujaribu kuboresha uimbaji wetu?” na “tutafika lini kwenye ‘vizuri vya kutosha’?” Hatutaweza kamwe kufikia ukamilifu wa mbinguni, hivyo swali linapaswa badala yake kuwa, “Je, tunamwipa Mungu bora zaidi tuliyonayo?” Watu wengine wana uwezo zaidi wa kuimba kuliko wengine, lakini swali linabaki. “Je, tunamwipa bora yetu au tumekubali dhabihu duni?” Tuwa wafanyaji wa sauti zinazomtukuza Mungu zinazorudisha furaha moyoni mwa Muumba!

Through the Church:

Biblia inazungumza kwa kina kuhusu uzuri wa watu wa Mungu. “Zion,” “Hekalu,” “Mlima wa Mungu,” “Yerusalemu,” na “Kanisa” ni maneno yanayolingana yaliyotumia maandiko yote yanayorejea makao ya watu wa Mungu duniani. Ni mapenzi ya Mungu kwamba uzuri Wake uakishwe katika maisha ya watu Wake. “Great is the LORD, and greatly to be praised in the city of our God, in the mountain of His holiness. Beautiful for situation, the joy of the whole earth, is Mount Zion, on the sides of the north, the city of the great King” (Psalm 48:1-2).

Hakuna kitu kipendwa zaidi moyoni mwa Mungu kuliko kanisa lake. Wakati watoto wa Israeli walipotembea jangwani, waliweka hema kama mahali pa Mungu kuishi kati yao. Wakati Sulemani alipoiweka hekalu kama makao ya Mungu, Mungu alifurahi sana na 2 Chronicles 7:1 inasema utukufu wa Bwana ulijaza hekalu. Hekalu lilichukuliwa kama Nyumba ya Bwana— Yesu mwenyewe alirejea kwake mara nyingi kama nyumba ya Mungu na alikuwa na shauku sana kwamba iendelezwe takatifu.

Leo, wala hema wala hekalu havianishi uwepo wa Mungu bali hisia Yake ya kiungu imekazia kanisa la Yesu Kristo. Hapa ndiyo watu ambao kweli wanampenda Yeye na wako tayari kutoa maisha yao Yeye. Hapa ndiyo watu ambao wako tayari kuacha haki zao kama watu binafsi na kujisalimisha kwa ajili ya kusudi kubwa. Hapa ndipo mtumishi wengi wamekutoa damu yao kwa ajili ya Injili. Na hapa ndipo siku moja Mwokozi wetu ataporudi kama alivyowaahidi, na atamchukua mkewe, kanisa, hadi makao yake ya milele. “And I John saw the holy city, New Jerusalem, coming down from God out of heaven, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband. And I heard a great voice out of heaven saying, Behold, the tabernacle of God is with men, and he will dwell with them, and they shall be His people, and God Himself shall be with them, and be their God” (Revelation 21:2-3).

Tunawezaje sisi, kama watu wa Mungu, kuakisha uzuri Wake kanisani? Kwa kuishi pamoja kwa umoja na muafaka kwa upendo kwa watu wote, hasa nyumba ya Mungu. Kanisa inapaswa kuwa mahali ambapo dunia inaweza kupata mtazamo wa kile kinachotokea mbinguni. Inapaswa kuwa mahali ambapo Kristo daima anainuliwa kama mshindi wa dhambi, kifo, na kuzimu.

Kwa bahati mbaya, watu wengi wamepoteza mwelekeo kutokana na kushindwa kwa kanisa na wameiondoka imani ya mitume ya kweli. Licha ya kuchanganyikiwa kwetu, tuchukue “mikono iliyoinama na magoti yaliyo dhaifu” (Hebrews 12:12) na tuendelee kusukuma mbele. Hatutaweza kuwa na wito wa juu zaidi, wala vita bora zaidi ya kuingia humo.

Mwishowe, tunawezaje kuakisha uzuri Wake katika maisha yetu? Kwa kumfurahia Yeye. “Delight thyself also in the LORD; and He shall give thee the desires of thine heart” (Psalm 37:4). Kuridhika kuu maishani kunatokana na kupata raha kwa kumletea Mungu furaha kwa kufurahia kile anachokifurahia na kupenda kile anachokipenda. Tusipoteze kamwe mshangao wa uzuri wa Ukombozi wetu!

The winter of 1882 unfolded in the small southern town of Tuscumbia, Alabama. A happy, normal two-year-old girl fell desperately ill with a strange fever. The fever came and went, came and went, and came again. The family doctor feared the child would die of the strain, but the child was strong and one day the fever finally left for good. The following day the mother waved a hand past her daughter's face, but the child did not blink. Subsequent efforts wrought no results and a new day dawned upon the family with a blind daughter.

As the child gained strength enough to resume play, the great dinner bell released its peal to all around, but Helen did not respond. Other noises produced similar results and the Keller family came to the stark realization that life would never be the same again. Most of us may never face the grim circumstances that Helen Keller's family did, but each of us will certainly endure hardships tailored specifically by our God.

The human mind is an amazing and intricate creation. Though many have sought to understand it, its operational ability remains incomprehensible to mankind. It is no small wonder that a portion of the keenest insight into the health of the mind is revealed in God's Word. “For God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind.” (2 Timothy 1:7)

Fear is the ominous adversary to a sound mind. It towers over the soul and taunts the saint with its menacing derision. Fear can take a sunny meadow and turn it into a lonely wilderness. It can render a grand wedding celebration as dark as a cave, and turn a banquet fit for a king into a nauseating affair. It is the most powerful and devastating tool in the devil's employment. Despite many bold claims, none are exempt from its wielding. “A dreadful sound is in his ears: in prosperity the destroyer shall come upon him. He believeth not that he shall return out of darkness, and he is waited for of the sword.” (Job 15:21, 22) It is fear that stands to attack and quench all the prosperity of the soul. If we are to resist it in these days, we he must rise with all diligence in defiant warfare.

We do not need to look very far to behold the disarmament and weakening of man's mind. Medication for the mind ranks among the leading prescriptions consumed in America today. This is no pointed accusation at any individuals who may find themselves in need of medical assistance to control their mind. But it takes no scholar to look at obesity and consider the diet, to see rebellious teens and connect it to the infrastructure of the home, or to see men's hearts (minds) failing them and believe that fear is at the root. While some may totally master their diet, few can claim to be accomplished parents. Fewer yet are those who are not, at times, accosted by fear. Though pride and sense may keep the outward man in check, and remaining perfectly calm, the inward man, at least subconsciously, must deal with the strain. Americans love to claim the motto, "No fear!" but our medication consumption tells a different story. Paul claimed no exemption, for he was “troubled on every side; without were fightings, within were fears.” (2 Corinthians 7:5)

What do we fear? Loss, pain, and humility. No one likes to lose something that we have fought to obtain. No one enjoys pain. No one loves to be humiliated. Still, we do not need to read far in the Scriptures to realize that these are often the avenues that God uses to further urge His servants down the path into His likeness. There is no insurance on earth that can secure the vibrancy of youth, the love of a family, or the respect of friends. The things that supply us with earth's greatest vanguard are all vulnerable to the risks of loss. Therefore, we fear. Though we lie in bed until the dawn of the morning, we can in no wise increase our stature nor alleviate the loss that God has laid upon our lives. This anxiety only furthers our grief and adds fuel to our fears.

“Be careful for nothing; but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God. And the peace of God, which passeth all understanding, shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus.” (Philippians 4:6 7) Herein is the keeping of our hearts and minds: prayer, peace, and thanksgiving.

Like a skillful artisan we must carefully weave these two scriptures together on the loom of life for there seems to be a direct correlation between the fruitful - power, love and sound mind, to the “rootful”- prayer, peace, and thankfulness. There will be no conquering of our fears without these things, and every society that is anemic to these ingredients will certainly be handicapped.

Prayer Begets Power

In our weakened condition we cannot apprehend prayer as we ought. It is then we must rely on those who can or perhaps the Spirit, which maketh intercession for us with groanings which cannot be uttered. Communing with the Omnipotent Head of the universe is a tremendously bold task. Many will administer prayer as merely a formal task, seeking to be perfectly reverent in it. This is not communing as with a friend, nor is it bold. It is more apt to fall under the description of fear. The remedial therapy for fear is in pouring out all our anxiety, bitterness, and complaint onto our God. The saints of yesteryear had been known to vehemently pour out their accusations and the bitterness of their soul unto God.

“Then Job answered and said, Even to day is my complaint bitter: my stroke is heavier than my groaning. Oh that I knew where I might find him! That I might come even to his seat! I would order my cause before him, and fill my mouth with arguments. I would know the words which he would answer me, and understand what he would say unto me. Will he plead against me with his great power? No; but he would put strength in me.” (Job 23:1-6)

  • David —“I poured out my complaint before him; I shewed before him my trouble.” (Psalm 142:2)
  • Hannah —“For out of the abundance of my complaint and grief have I spoken hitherto.” (1 Samuel 1:16)
  • Jeremiah —“He hath filled me with bitterness, he hath made me drunken with wormwood.”
    (Lamentations 3:15)
  • Naomi —“Call me Mara: for the Almighty hath dealt very bitterly with me.” (Ruth 1:20)
  • Hezekiah —“He will cut me off with pining sickness: from day even to night wilt thou make an end of me.” (Isaiah 38:12)
  • Jesus — “My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?” (Matthew 27:46)

All these spewed forth bold accusations and complaints against God in fervent prayer and none of them offended Him. On the contrary, God had not given them the spirit of fear but of power, and they serve as our examples. It was faithless Ahab who was told to ask of God a sign in the heavens or earth. In his pious reply he refused to "tempt" God. This lack of boldness and abundance of fear is more tempting to God than the abundance of bitterness in our complaint for “there is no fear in love; but perfect love casteth out fear: because fear hath torment. He that feareth is not made perfect in love.” (1 John 4:18)

Peace Begets Love

We are all at rest with the things we love. "Great peace have they which love thy law: and nothing shall offend them.” (Psalm 119:165) A sparkling young child who is at peace with his father worships the man and strives to imitate him. Through the lad's tender eyes, his father's character is unflawed. His skill is unmatched. Even the brand of vehicle he drives is the best, and he emulates his every action. Even though every father knows the limitations of his son's expectations, we all bask in the seasonal loyalty. It is knowledge and fear that undermines this loyal love. An abusive father will destroy such childhood esteem and fear will be its replacement. It was through base fear that the evil servant buried his talent and did not trade with it. In his eyes his master was austere and to be feared. But God has not given us the spirit of fear but of love.

“We love him, because he first loved us. If a man say, I love God, and hateth his brother, he is a liar: for he that loveth not his brother whom he hath seen, how can he love God whom he hath not seen?” (1 John 4:19, 20) The soul who is affected by this love cannot but imitate it. He is at great peace with his Father’s love and the eyes through which he views his Father's character can only enlist replication. However dire the circumstances we may find ourselves in, this spirit of love and peace will carry us through whatever opposition we may meet with on life's pathway. Jacob made nothing of the hard service he was to endure for Rachel; the spirit of love to God will set us above the fear of man, and all the hurt that a man can do us.

Thankfulness Begets a Sound Mind

We do not need to study happy souls long to find buried within the bedrock of each one, a foundation of gratitude. The spirit of a sound mind, or quietness of mind, is a peaceable enjoyment of life. We are oftentimes discouraged in our way when the features of our environment do not measure not up to our own fancy and imagination. A mere sober, solid, thinking mind would obviate and defuse such fruitless notions, yet we are all tempted to entertain formidable ingratitude. It takes no brainpower to expose things we disdain, for Satan is certain to magnify and outline every unsatisfactory detail we encounter. We each may think ourselves into a deep cave, but we must thank ourselves out.

Fear of losing our health, wealth, reputation, and happiness is the biggest hindrance to securing it. To focus on our pain is to invite more. To be constantly analyzing our life to see if we are being fulfilled is a sure avenue to ingratitude. The world is constantly asking, "Are we having fun yet?" The answer is, "No". To these souls, life will never be adequate, and they must wander forth seeking the bigger fulfillment that the last one did not secure. It is the fear that we are not receiving our fair allotment in life that breeds discontentment. It is discontentment that produces more fear, and the downward spiral progresses. Such was the consternation of the soul who asked Christ to speak to his brother to divide the inheritance with him. This may be logical thinking, but it is not conducive to a sound and peaceable mind. This offended soul has no root in himself and will forever be wronged in some fashion and spend his days in search of a savior to come and fix the other party. “... neither fear ye their fear, nor be afraid. Sanctify the LORD of hosts himself; and let him be your fear, and let him be your dread.” (Isaiah 8:12, 13)

There is no earthly level of attainment or perfect environment that will promote a sound mind. It can only be secured through prayer, peace, and thankfulness. This may take some reprogramming of our minds to reach into the subconscious recesses, but we must soberly gird up the loins of our minds and exercise them if we ever hope to obtain “the grace that is to be brought unto you at the revelation of Jesus Christ;” (1 Peter 1:13)

“And the peace of God,
which passeth all understanding,
shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus.
Finally, brethren, whatsoever things are true,
whatsoever things are honest, whatsoever things are just,
whatsoever things are pure, whatsoever things are lovely,
whatsoever things are of good report;
if there be any virtue, and if there be any praise,
think on these things.

— Philippians 4:7, 8

L'hiver 1882 se déroulait dans la petite ville du sud de Tuscumbia, en Alabama. Une fillette joyeuse et normale de deux ans tomba gravement malade d'une étrange fièvre. La fièvre revenait, s'en allait, revenait encore. Le médecin de famille craignait que l'enfant ne meure de l'épreuve, mais l'enfant était robuste et un jour la fièvre disparut enfin pour de bon. Le lendemain, la mère agita la main devant le visage de sa fille, mais l'enfant ne cligna pas des yeux. Les tentatives suivantes ne donnèrent aucun résultat et un nouveau jour se leva pour la famille avec une fille aveugle.

Lorsque l'enfant retrouva assez de forces pour reprendre ses jeux, la grande cloche du dîner fit entendre son carillon tout autour, mais Helen ne répondit pas. D'autres bruits eurent des résultats similaires et la famille Keller prit la cruelle conscience que la vie ne serait plus jamais la même. La plupart d'entre nous ne feront peut‑être jamais face aux circonstances sinistres qu'a connues la famille d'Helen Keller, mais chacun de nous endurera certainement des épreuves spécifiquement façonnées par notre Dieu.

L'esprit humain est une création étonnante et complexe. Bien que beaucoup aient cherché à le comprendre, sa capacité opérationnelle reste incompréhensible pour l'humanité. Il n'est pas surprenant qu'une partie des aperçus les plus pénétrants sur la santé de l'esprit soit révélée dans la Parole de Dieu. “For God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind.” (2 Timothy 1:7)

La peur est l'ennemi sombre d'un esprit sain. Elle domine l'âme et nargue le saint par sa dérision menaçante. La peur peut transformer une prairie ensoleillée en un désert solitaire. Elle peut rendre une grande fête de mariage aussi sombre qu'une grotte, et transformer un banquet digne d'un roi en un repas écœurant. C'est l'outil le plus puissant et le plus dévastateur dans l'arsenal du diable. Malgré de nombreuses prétentions hardies, personne n'en est exempté. “A dreadful sound is in his ears: in prosperity the destroyer shall come upon him. He believeth not that he shall return out of darkness, and he is waited for of the sword.” (Job 15:21, 22) C'est la peur qui attaque et éteint toute la prospérité de l'âme. Si nous devons lui résister en ces jours, nous devons nous lever avec toute diligence dans une guerre défiant l'ennemi.

Nous n'avons pas besoin d'aller bien loin pour voir le désarmement et l'affaiblissement de l'esprit humain. Les médicaments pour l'esprit figurent parmi les prescriptions les plus consommées en Amérique aujourd'hui. Ce n'est pas une accusation directe envers des individus qui peuvent avoir besoin d'assistance médicale pour contrôler leur esprit. Mais nul besoin d'être savant pour regarder l'obésité et en considérer le régime, voir des adolescents rebelles et relier cela à l'infrastructure du foyer, ou voir des cœurs d'hommes (esprits) qui faiblissent et croire que la peur en est la racine. Alors que certains peuvent parfaitement maîtriser leur régime alimentaire, peu peuvent se prétendre parents accomplis. Encore moins sont ceux qui ne sont pas, parfois, accablés par la peur. Bien que l'orgueil et le bon sens puissent contenir l'homme extérieur et le maintenir parfaitement calme, l'homme intérieur, au moins subconscientement, doit faire face à la tension. Les Américains aiment proclamer la devise «"No fear!"», mais notre consommation de médicaments raconte une histoire différente. Paul n'a revendiqué aucune exemption, car il était “troubled on every side; without were fightings, within were fears.” (2 Corinthians 7:5)

De quoi avons‑nous peur ? De la perte, de la douleur et de l'humiliation. Personne n'aime perdre quelque chose pour lequel il a combattu. Personne n'apprécie la douleur. Personne n'aime être humilié. Pourtant, il ne faut pas lire bien loin dans les Écritures pour réaliser que ce sont souvent des voies par lesquelles Dieu pousse ses serviteurs davantage sur le chemin de sa ressemblance. Il n'existe sur terre aucune assurance qui puisse garantir la vigueur de la jeunesse, l'amour d'une famille ou le respect des amis. Les choses qui nous procurent les plus grandes avant‑gardes de la terre sont toutes vulnérables aux risques de perte. Dès lors, nous craignons. Même si nous restons au lit jusqu'à l'aube, nous ne pouvons en aucune façon accroître notre stature ni alléger la perte que Dieu a mise sur nos vies. Cette anxiété ne fait qu'amplifier notre douleur et alimenter nos peurs.

“Be careful for nothing; but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God. And the peace of God, which passeth all understanding, shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus.” (Philippians 4:6 7) Voici la garde de nos cœurs et de nos esprits : la prière, la paix et l'action de grâces.

Comme un artisan habile, nous devons tisser soigneusement ces deux Écritures ensemble sur le métier de la vie, car il semble exister une corrélation directe entre le fructueux — pouvoir, amour et esprit sain — et le «radical» — prière, paix et action de grâces. Il n'y aura pas de conquête de nos peurs sans ces choses, et toute société anémique à ces ingrédients sera certainement handicapée.

La prière engendre le pouvoir

Dans notre état affaibli nous ne pouvons appréhender la prière comme il le faudrait. C'est alors que nous devons compter sur ceux qui peuvent prier ou peut‑être sur l'Esprit, qui maketh intercession for us with groanings which cannot be uttered. Communier avec la Tête omnipotente de l'univers est une tâche extrêmement audacieuse. Beaucoup pratiquent la prière comme une simple formalité, cherchant à y être parfaitement révérencieux. Ce n'est pas communier comme avec un ami, ni être audacieux. Cela relève plutôt de la peur. Le remède contre la peur consiste à déverser sur notre Dieu toute notre anxiété, notre amertume et nos plaintes. Les saints d'autrefois avaient l'habitude de répandre véhémentement leurs accusations et l'amertume de leur âme devant Dieu.

“Then Job answered and said, Even to day is my complaint bitter: my stroke is heavier than my groaning. Oh that I knew where I might find him! That I might come even to his seat! I would order my cause before him, and fill my mouth with arguments. I would know the words which he would answer me, and understand what he would say unto me. Will he plead against me with his great power? No; but he would put strength in me.” (Job 23:1-6)

  • David —“I poured out my complaint before him; I shewed before him my trouble.” (Psalm 142:2)
  • Hannah —“For out of the abundance of my complaint and grief have I spoken hitherto.” (1 Samuel 1:16)
  • Jeremiah —“He hath filled me with bitterness, he hath made me drunken with wormwood.”
    (Lamentations 3:15)
  • Naomi —“Call me Mara: for the Almighty hath dealt very bitterly with me.” (Ruth 1:20)
  • Hezekiah —“He will cut me off with pining sickness: from day even to night wilt thou make an end of me.” (Isaiah 38:12)
  • Jesus — “My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?” (Matthew 27:46)

Tous ont déversé des accusations et des plaintes audacieuses contre Dieu dans une prière fervente et aucun d'eux ne L'a offensé. Au contraire, Dieu ne leur avait pas donné l'esprit de peur mais de puissance, et ils nous servent d'exemples. C'est le sans‑foi Achab à qui l'on dit de demander à Dieu un signe dans les cieux ou sur la terre. Dans sa réponse pieuse il refusa de «tenter» Dieu. Ce manque d'audace et cet excès de peur sont plus tentants pour Dieu que l'abondance d'amertume dans notre plainte, car “there is no fear in love; but perfect love casteth out fear: because fear hath torment. He that feareth is not made perfect in love.” (1 John 4:18)

La paix engendre l'amour

Nous sommes tous en paix avec les choses que nous aimons. "Great peace have they which love thy law: and nothing shall offend them.” (Psalm 119:165) Un enfant vif et étincelant qui est en paix avec son père admire l'homme et s'efforce de l'imiter. Aux yeux tendres du garçon, le caractère de son père est sans défaut. Sa compétence est inégalée. Même la marque du véhicule qu'il conduit est la meilleure, et il reproduit chacun de ses gestes. Même si tout père connaît les limites des attentes de son fils, nous profitons tous de cette loyauté saisonnière. C'est la connaissance et la crainte qui sapent cet amour loyal. Un père abusif détruira une telle estime enfantine et la peur en sera le substitut. C'est par une peur basse que le mauvais serviteur enterra son talent et ne l'exploita pas. À ses yeux son maître était austère et à craindre. Mais Dieu ne nous a pas donné l'esprit de peur mais d'amour.

“We love him, because he first loved us. If a man say, I love God, and hateth his brother, he is a liar: for he that loveth not his brother whom he hath seen, how can he love God whom he hath not seen?” (1 John 4:19, 20) L'âme touchée par cet amour ne peut que l'imiter. Elle est en grande paix avec l'amour de son Père et les yeux par lesquels elle voit le caractère de son Père n'inspirent que la réplication. Aussi graves que soient les circonstances dans lesquelles nous pouvons nous trouver, cet esprit d'amour et de paix nous portera à travers toute opposition que nous rencontrerons sur le chemin de la vie. Jacob ne s'est pas soucié du dur service qu'il devait endurer pour Rachel ; l'esprit d'amour pour Dieu nous élèvera au‑dessus de la crainte de l'homme, et de tout le mal qu'un homme peut nous faire.

La reconnaissance engendre un esprit sain

Il n'est pas nécessaire d'étudier longtemps des âmes heureuses pour trouver enfoui dans le socle de chacune une fondation de gratitude. L'esprit d'un esprit sain, ou la tranquillité d'esprit, est un jouissement paisible de la vie. Nous sommes souvent découragés en chemin lorsque les traits de notre environnement ne correspondent pas à notre fantaisie ou à notre imagination. Un esprit sobre, solide et pensant ferait disparaître et désamorcer de telles notions infructueuses, et pourtant nous sommes tous tentés d'entretenir une ingratitude redoutable. Il ne faut pas d'intelligence particulière pour exposer ce que nous méprisons, car Satan est certain d'amplifier et de souligner chaque détail insatisfaisant que nous rencontrons. Chacun de nous peut se penser dans une grotte profonde, mais nous devons nous remercier pour en sortir.

La peur de perdre notre santé, notre richesse, notre réputation et notre bonheur est le principal obstacle à leur conservation. Se concentrer sur notre douleur, c'est en inviter davantage. Analyser constamment notre vie pour voir si nous sommes comblés est une voie sûre vers l'ingratitude. Le monde demande sans cesse : "Are we having fun yet?" La réponse est : «Non». Pour ces âmes, la vie ne sera jamais adéquate, et elles erreront en quête d'une plus grande satisfaction que la précédente n'a pas apportée. C'est la peur de ne pas recevoir notre juste part dans la vie qui engendre l'insatisfaction. L'insatisfaction produit plus de peur, et la spirale descendante s'accentue. Telle était la consternation de l'âme qui demanda à Christ de parler à son frère pour partager l'héritage avec lui. Cela peut relever d'un raisonnement logique, mais ce n'est pas propice à un esprit sain et paisible. Cette âme offensée n'a pas de racine en elle‑même et sera toujours lésée d'une manière ou d'une autre et passera ses jours à chercher un sauveur qui viendra arranger la partie adverse. “... neither fear ye their fear, nor be afraid. Sanctify the LORD of hosts himself; and let him be your fear, and let him be your dread.” (Isaiah 8:12, 13)

Il n'existe aucun niveau d'accomplissement terrestre ni environnement parfait qui favorise un esprit sain. Il ne peut être assuré que par la prière, la paix et la reconnaissance. Cela peut nécessiter une certaine reprogrammation de nos esprits pour atteindre les recoins subconscients, mais nous devons ceindre sobrement les reins de nos pensées et les exercer si nous espérons un jour obtenir “the grace that is to be brought unto you at the revelation of Jesus Christ;” (1 Peter 1:13)

Part 1

For Alice, life is exasperating. Each day feels like an endless grind. She loves her family, but in her heart, she questions if what she is working so hard to accomplish makes any difference at all. She didn’t always feel bogged down, and she wondered what changed to make her feel overwhelmed so much of the time.

Sometimes busyness increases so gradually that we barely recognize the change. Busyness, given the chance, will overload us with more obligations than we can realistically get done in one day, or one week, or even one lifetime. Then, without warning, we reach the overload point when we feel as though we cannot possibly handle any more. Relentless overload can cause physical and mental exhaustion to the point where we feel deprived of enthusiasm, energy, and purpose. Some women seem to have a built-in indicator of where the overload line is. Others, like myself, struggle to find that balance. Constantly. There are so many good, interesting, and exciting options right at our fingertips; without much thought, we fill our days.

Concepts that contribute to overload

Playing multiple roles can be stressful. Overloading yourself with responsibilities and commitments can make you forget what is most important. It is easy to equate busyness with self-worth. By default, we start believing that:

  • Homemakers are capable of handling everything.
  • Homemakers, especially godly homemakers, are never frustrated.
  • A homemaker should anticipate all her family’s needs.

If we are honest, we know that these statements are unrealistic. Homemakers cannot do everything. All homemakers experience frustration occasionally. A mother cannot consistently be one step ahead of her family’s needs.

Rethinking the busy life

Household duties and caring for our families fill our days. Sometimes those tasks alone make us extremely busy. But what about the extra-circular activities or the high standard we hold ourselves to? We may need to think differently so we can break free from habits that threaten to control us.

Accept your limits

Maybe you can go to a Tupperware party, attend a Bible study, and repaint the bathroom all in one week. But should you? Good homemakers allow themselves to simplify even if they prefer doing it another way. That means if you are an avid bread maker, it’s all right to toss a few loaves of bread into your shopping cart.

Evaluate what causes frustrations

Artificial smiles can hide inner frustrations, but it doesn’t cure them. It works best to admit that there is a problem and then seek a solution. I’ve had to learn this repeatedly. All my family members know that we eat dinner at 5:30. But a late arrival habit is trending, and it bothers me.

When I told my husband about the frustration, he simply said, “Why don’t you explain the issue and quit being so uptight about it?” Good point. Proactively seeking solutions works for many problem areas.

Imperfect women make good homemakers

Quit worrying about perfection and make decisions based on what is best for today. Fun-loving, happy, homemakers might have a few dust bunnies under the furniture, but they radiate an aura that draws people to their hearts and homes.

Everyone differs when it comes to how much we can handle. On the other hand, everyone is the same; we all have limits. In future installments, we will discuss how to deal with common points of overload.

Part 2

Many homemakers find themselves stretched thin among commitments that go with home, family, and other activities. As busy as we are, why do we continue to fill our schedules fuller?

It is easy for me to commit to a new project and then realize, halfway into the task, that I have overstepped my limits. Too often, I overestimate the amount of time I must have to complete a project and underestimate the amount of time a task will take.

Commitment overload happens by default. When we play multiple roles and add more responsibilities, we can easily become slaves to the promises we have made. Overload tends to drain our energy, dull our senses, and deaden our joy.

Recognizing Overload

Sometimes multiple activities take place in rapid sequence. Normally, we can flow with short-term spurts of busyness. But if the flow of activities is never-ending and we keep adding more obligations, we develop a pattern that becomes a way of life.

Too many commitments beyond normal duties make us candidates for depression and burnout. Personally, when I experience insomnia, apathy, or irritability, it is time to examine my schedule. If adjustments aren’t made, someone or something will suffer.

No one can overextend themselves indefinitely. Sometimes we suffer consequences for keeping a pace that is beyond our resources. Symptoms of overload can include lack of sleep, strained relationships, procrastination, fear of failure, and a susceptible immune system.

Breaking Free of Overload

Identifying overload takes an honest evaluation of yourself. How can you know if this is just a busy season or if busyness is the new normal? Are you declining a request because life is too full, or is it an excuse? Do you have to say “yes” on the spot? With practice, you can learn how to pull back before reaching the overload point.

Let an idea or request gel before committing

This has saved me a great deal of stress. There are so many good things to be involved in, and new inspirations come daily. Sometimes tasks can be incorporated into my/our schedule. Other times I must simply let them go and stay focused on what is most important. Consider waiting a few hours before incorporating new ideas and requests.

Seek advice, especially your husband’s

A renowned doughnut maker was asked to have a stand at an auction. She asked her husband what he thought about it. He said, “As long as you don’t complain and stress about it like you did last year, I don’t care.” Was her husband saying “yes” or “no”? This lady should take the cue that doughnut making was somehow adding stress. Either she should not do it, or together they must seek a workable solution.

Evaluate your schedule regularly

Keep a detailed calendar to have a picture of past, present, and future events. If your family had the flu last week and you plan to take an out-of-state trip next week, should you add more? What is the emotional health of your family? Is your husband stressed at work? Sometimes it is better to have a time slot of nothing so it can be filled with what is important now. You can’t do a good job at anything if you are spread too thin. Too many obligations make it hard to be personally refreshed and congenial. Choosing commitments wisely will help you invest your energy where it is most valuable for today.

חלק 1

עבור אליס, החיים מייגעים. כל יום מרגיש כמטלה אינסופית. היא אוהבת את משפחתה, אבל בליבה היא תוהה האם מה שהיא עובדת קשה כדי להגשימו בכלל עושה הבדל. לא תמיד היא הרגישה מוטלת תחת עומס, והיא תהתה מה השתנה עד שהיא התחילה להרגיש מוצפת כל כך הרבה מהזמן.

לפעמים העומס עלול לגדול בהדרגה עד שאנו בקושי מזהות את השינוי. העסוקנות, אם נותנים לה הזדמנות, תגזים בנו עם יותר מחויבויות ממה שנוכל להשליט מציאותית ביום אחד, או בשבוע אחד, או אפילו במשך כל החיים. ואז, ללא אזהרה, אנו מגיעות לנקודת העומס שבה נדמה שלא נוכל להתמודד עוד. עומס בלתי פוסק יכול לגרום לעייפות גופנית ונפשית עד כדי חוסר התלהבות, אנרגיה ותכלית. חלק מהנשים נדמה שיש להן אינדיקטור פנימי המצביע היכן קו העומס נמצא. אחרות, כמוני, מתקשות למצוא את האיזון. כל הזמן. יש כל כך הרבה אפשרויות טובות, מעניינות ומרגשות בהישג יד; בלי מחשבה רבה, אנו ממלאות את ימינו.

מושגים התורמים לעומס

מילוי תפקידים רבים עלול להיות מלחיץ. להעמיס על עצמך באחריוּת ובמחויבויות יכול לגרום לך לשכוח מה החשוב ביותר. קל לשוות בין העסוקנות לערך העצמי. כברירת מחדל, אנחנו מתחילות להאמין ש:

  • עושות הבית מסוגלות לטפל בכל דבר.
  • עושות הבית, ובפרט עושות בית חסידות, אינן מתוסכלות לעולם.
  • עושה הבית צריכה לצפות את כל צרכי משפחתה.

אם נהיה כן-כן עם עצמנו, אנחנו יודעות שהודעות אלה לא ריאליות. עושות בית אינן יכולות לעשות הכל. כל עושות הבית חוות תסכול מדי פעם. אם אם לא תמיד יכולה להיות צעד אחד לפני צרכי משפחתה.

לחשוב מחדש על החיים העמוסים

מטלות הבית וטיפוח המשפחה ממלאות את ימינו. לפעמים המטלות האלה לבדן הופכות אותנו לעסוקות מאוד. אבל מה לגבי הפעילויות החוץ‑בית‑ספריות או הסטנדרט הגבוה שאנו מציבות לעצמנו? ייתכן שעלינו לחשוב אחרת כדי להשתחרר מהרגלים המאיימים להשתלט עלינו.

קבלי את גבולותייך

אולי את יכולה ללכת למסיבת טאפאוור, להשתתף בלימוד מקרא, ולצבוע מחדש את חדר האמבטיה—כל זה בשבוע אחד. אבל האם כדאי? עושות בית טובות מאפשרות לעצמן לפשט גם אם הן מעדיפות לעשות זאת בדרך אחרת. זאת אומרת, אם את אופים לחם בהתלהבות, זה בסדר להשליך כמה כיכרות לעגלה בסופר.

העריכי מה גורם לתסכולים

חיוכים מלאכותיים יכולים להסתיר תסכולים פנימיים, אך הם אינם מרפאים אותם. עדיף להודות שיש בעיה ואז לחפש פתרון. נאלצתי ללמוד זאת שוב ושוב. כל בני משפחתי יודעים שאנו אוכלים ארוחת ערב בשעה 17:30. אבל נטיית איחור תופסת פופולריות, וזה מציק לי.

כשהסברתי לבעלי על התסכול, הוא פשוט אמר, "למה שלא תסבירי את העניין ותפסיקי להיות כל כך מתוחה לגבי זה?" נקודה טובה. חיפוש פרואקטיבי אחר פתרונות עובד עבור תחומי בעיה רבים.

נשים בלתי מושלמות עושות עושות בית טובות

תפסיקי לדאוג לשלמות וקבלי החלטות על פי מה שטוב להיום. עושות בית שמחות, אוהבות-כיף, אולי יש להן כמה כדורי אבק מתחת לרהיטים, אבל הן מקרינות הילה שמושכת אנשים ללבן ולבתים שלהן.

יש שונות בכמה כל אחת מאיתנו מסוגלת להתמודד. מצד שני, כולנו זהות בכך שכולנו יש לנו גבולות. בהמשכים הבאים נדון כיצד להתמודד עם נקודות עומס נפוצות.

חלק 2

עשרות רבות של עושות בית מוצאות את עצמן מתוחות בין מחויבויות הנלוות לבית, למשפחה ולפעילויות נוספות. למרות היותנו כל כך עסוקות, מדוע אנחנו ממשיכות למלא את לוחות הזמנים שלנו עוד יותר?

קל לי להתחייב לפרוייקט חדש ואז להבחין, באמצע המשימה, שעברתי את גבולותיי. לעתים קרובות מדי, אני מעריכה ביתר את כמות הזמן הנחוצה להשלמת פרוייקט וממעיטה בהערכת הזמן שמטלה תיקח.

עודף מחויבויות קורה כברירת מחדל. כשאנו ממלאות תפקידים מרובים ומוסיפות יותר אחריויות, קל להיהפך לעבדים של ההבטחות שעשינו. העומס נוטה לרוקן מאיתנו אנרגיה, לטשטש את החושים ולהכהות את השמחה.

להכיר בעומס

לפעמים פעילויות מרובות מתרחשות ברצף מהיר. בדרך כלל, אנו יכולות לזרום עם פרצי עסוקנות קצרים. אבל אם זרם הפעילויות איננו נגמר ואנו ממשיכות להוסיף עוד התחייבויות, נפתח דפוס שנעשה דרך חיים.

יותר מדי מחויבויות מעבר לחובות הרגילות מעמידות אותנו כמועמדות לדיכאון או לשחיקה. באופן אישי, כשאני חווה נדודי שינה, אפאתיה או רוגזנות, זה הזמן לבדוק את לוח הזמנים שלי. אם לא נעשים התאמות, מישהי או משהו יסבול.

אף אחת אינה יכולה להעמיס על עצמה לנצח. לעתים אנו סובלות משילולים על קיום קצב העולה על משאבינו. תסמיני עומס יכולים לכלול חוסר שינה, מערכות יחסים מתוחות, דחיינות, פחד מכישלון ומערכת חיסון מוחלשת.

להשתחרר מהעומס

זיהוי העומס דורש הערכה כנה של עצמך. איך תוכלי לדעת אם זו רק עונת עומס או שהעסוקנות היא הנורמה החדשה? האם את דוחה בקשה כי החיים מלאים מדי, או שזה התירוץ? האם את חייבת לומר "כן" באותו רגע? עם תרגול, תוכלי ללמוד איך להסיג גבול לפני שמגיעים לנקודת העומס.

תנו לרעיון או לבקשה להתבשל לפני שמתחייבים

זה הציל אותי מלחץ רב. יש כל כך הרבה דברים טובים להיות מעורבים בהם, והשראות חדשות מגיעות מדי יום. לעתים משימות יכולות להשתלב בלוח הזמנים שלי/שלנו. לפעמים אחרות עלי פשוט לוותר ולהתמקד במה שחשוב ביותר. שקלי להמתין כמה שעות לפני שילוב רעיונות ובקשות חדשות.

חפשי עצה, במיוחד של בעלך

אשת סמנכרת סופגניות ידועה נתבקשה לפתוח דוכן במכירה פומבית. היא שאלה את בעלה מה דעתו על זה. הוא אמר, "כל עוד את לא מתלוננת ומסתעפת מזה כמו בשנה שעברה, זה לא מפריע לי." האם בעלה אמר "כן" או "לא"? האישה הזאת צריכה לקחת את הרמז שסביבת הכנת הסופגניות הוסיפה במשהו מתח. או שהיא לא תעשה את זה, או שהם יחד צריכים למצוא פתרון שניתן לממש.

העריכי את לוח הזמנים שלך באופן קבוע

שמרי לוח שנה מפורט כדי לקבל תמונה של האירועים בעבר, בהווה ובעתיד. אם משפחתך חלתה בשפעת בשבוע שעבר ואת מתכננת יציאה מחוץ למדינה בשבוע הבא, האם כדאי להוסיף עוד? מה מצב הבריאות הרגשי של משפחתך? האם בעלך לחוץ בעבודה? לפעמים עדיף להשאיר משבצת זמן ריקה כדי שתוכל להתמלא במה שחשוב עכשיו. את לא יכולה לעשות דבר היטב אם את מפוזרת מדי. יותר מדי התחייבויות מקשות להיות מרוקנת באופן אישי ונעימה חברתית. בחירת מחויבויות בחוכמה תעזור לך להשקיע את אנרגייתך היכן שהיא בעלת ערך להיום.

The glory of the spring, how sweet!
The newborn life, how glad!
What joy the happy earth to greet
In new, bright raiment clad!

Divine Redeemer, Thee I bless;
I greet Thy going forth;
I love Thee in the loveliness
Of Thy renewed earth.

But O these wonders of Thy grace,
These nobler works of Thine,
These marvels sweeter far to trace,
These new births more divine:

This new-born glow of faith so strong,
This bloom of love so fair,
This new-born ecstasy of song,
And fragrancy of prayer!

Creator Spirit, work in me
These wonders sweet of Thine;
Divine Redeemer, graciously
Renew this heart of mine.

Still, let new life and strength upspring,
Still, let new joy be given;
And grant the glad new song to ring
Through the new earth and Heaven.

Maar o, deze wonderen van Uw trouw,

Deze wonderen, zoeter om te aanschouwen,
Deze nieuwgeboren daden meer goddelijk en grand:

Deze zoete wonderen van U;

Dit hart van mij erbij, als 't rouwt en ru.

Laat toch nieuwe leven en kracht ontspringen,
Laat toch nieuwe vreugd gegeven zijn;
En schenk het blije nieuwe lied te klinken
Door de nieuwe aarde en de Hemel, rein.

Part 1

For Alice, life is exasperating. Each day feels like an endless grind. She loves her family, but in her heart, she questions if what she is working so hard to accomplish makes any difference at all. She didn’t always feel bogged down, and she wondered what changed to make her feel overwhelmed so much of the time.

Sometimes busyness increases so gradually that we barely recognize the change. Busyness, given the chance, will overload us with more obligations than we can realistically get done in one day, or one week, or even one lifetime. Then, without warning, we reach the overload point when we feel as though we cannot possibly handle any more. Relentless overload can cause physical and mental exhaustion to the point where we feel deprived of enthusiasm, energy, and purpose. Some women seem to have a built-in indicator of where the overload line is. Others, like myself, struggle to find that balance. Constantly. There are so many good, interesting, and exciting options right at our fingertips; without much thought, we fill our days.

Concepts that contribute to overload

Playing multiple roles can be stressful. Overloading yourself with responsibilities and commitments can make you forget what is most important. It is easy to equate busyness with self-worth. By default, we start believing that:

  • Homemakers are capable of handling everything.
  • Homemakers, especially godly homemakers, are never frustrated.
  • A homemaker should anticipate all her family’s needs.

If we are honest, we know that these statements are unrealistic. Homemakers cannot do everything. All homemakers experience frustration occasionally. A mother cannot consistently be one step ahead of her family’s needs.

Rethinking the busy life

Household duties and caring for our families fill our days. Sometimes those tasks alone make us extremely busy. But what about the extra-circular activities or the high standard we hold ourselves to? We may need to think differently so we can break free from habits that threaten to control us.

Accept your limits

Maybe you can go to a Tupperware party, attend a Bible study, and repaint the bathroom all in one week. But should you? Good homemakers allow themselves to simplify even if they prefer doing it another way. That means if you are an avid bread maker, it’s all right to toss a few loaves of bread into your shopping cart.

Evaluate what causes frustrations

Artificial smiles can hide inner frustrations, but it doesn’t cure them. It works best to admit that there is a problem and then seek a solution. I’ve had to learn this repeatedly. All my family members know that we eat dinner at 5:30. But a late arrival habit is trending, and it bothers me.

When I told my husband about the frustration, he simply said, “Why don’t you explain the issue and quit being so uptight about it?” Good point. Proactively seeking solutions works for many problem areas.

Imperfect women make good homemakers

Quit worrying about perfection and make decisions based on what is best for today. Fun-loving, happy, homemakers might have a few dust bunnies under the furniture, but they radiate an aura that draws people to their hearts and homes.

Everyone differs when it comes to how much we can handle. On the other hand, everyone is the same; we all have limits. In future installments, we will discuss how to deal with common points of overload.

Part 2

Many homemakers find themselves stretched thin among commitments that go with home, family, and other activities. As busy as we are, why do we continue to fill our schedules fuller?

It is easy for me to commit to a new project and then realize, halfway into the task, that I have overstepped my limits. Too often, I overestimate the amount of time I must have to complete a project and underestimate the amount of time a task will take.

Commitment overload happens by default. When we play multiple roles and add more responsibilities, we can easily become slaves to the promises we have made. Overload tends to drain our energy, dull our senses, and deaden our joy.

Recognizing Overload

Sometimes multiple activities take place in rapid sequence. Normally, we can flow with short-term spurts of busyness. But if the flow of activities is never-ending and we keep adding more obligations, we develop a pattern that becomes a way of life.

Too many commitments beyond normal duties make us candidates for depression and burnout. Personally, when I experience insomnia, apathy, or irritability, it is time to examine my schedule. If adjustments aren’t made, someone or something will suffer.

No one can overextend themselves indefinitely. Sometimes we suffer consequences for keeping a pace that is beyond our resources. Symptoms of overload can include lack of sleep, strained relationships, procrastination, fear of failure, and a susceptible immune system.

Breaking Free of Overload

Identifying overload takes an honest evaluation of yourself. How can you know if this is just a busy season or if busyness is the new normal? Are you declining a request because life is too full, or is it an excuse? Do you have to say “yes” on the spot? With practice, you can learn how to pull back before reaching the overload point.

Let an idea or request gel before committing

This has saved me a great deal of stress. There are so many good things to be involved in, and new inspirations come daily. Sometimes tasks can be incorporated into my/our schedule. Other times I must simply let them go and stay focused on what is most important. Consider waiting a few hours before incorporating new ideas and requests.

Seek advice, especially your husband’s

A renowned doughnut maker was asked to have a stand at an auction. She asked her husband what he thought about it. He said, “As long as you don’t complain and stress about it like you did last year, I don’t care.” Was her husband saying “yes” or “no”? This lady should take the cue that doughnut making was somehow adding stress. Either she should not do it, or together they must seek a workable solution.

Evaluate your schedule regularly

Keep a detailed calendar to have a picture of past, present, and future events. If your family had the flu last week and you plan to take an out-of-state trip next week, should you add more? What is the emotional health of your family? Is your husband stressed at work? Sometimes it is better to have a time slot of nothing so it can be filled with what is important now. You can’t do a good job at anything if you are spread too thin. Too many obligations make it hard to be personally refreshed and congenial. Choosing commitments wisely will help you invest your energy where it is most valuable for today.

Partie 1

Pour Alice, la vie est exaspérante. Chaque jour ressemble à une corvée sans fin. Elle aime sa famille, mais au fond d’elle, elle se demande si ce à quoi elle s’emploie si ardemment fait vraiment une différence. Elle ne s’est pas toujours sentie accablée, et elle se demande ce qui a changé pour la faire se sentir dépassée si souvent.

Parfois, l’occupation augmente si graduellement que nous reconnaissons à peine le changement. L’occupation, si on lui en laisse l’occasion, nous surcharge de plus d’obligations que ce que nous pouvons réaliser raisonnablement en une journée, une semaine, ou même une vie entière. Puis, sans prévenir, nous atteignons le point de surcharge où nous avons l’impression de ne plus pouvoir en supporter davantage. Une surcharge incessante peut provoquer une épuisement physique et mental au point où nous perdons enthousiasme, énergie et sens. Certaines femmes semblent avoir un indicateur intégré de l’endroit où se situe la ligne de surcharge. D’autres, comme moi, peinent constamment à trouver cet équilibre. Il y a tant d’options bonnes, intéressantes et excitantes à portée de main ; sans y réfléchir beaucoup, nous remplissons nos journées.

Concepts qui contribuent à la surcharge

Cumuler plusieurs rôles peut être source de stress. Se surcharger de responsabilités et d’engagements peut vous faire oublier ce qui est le plus important. Il est facile d’assimiler l’occupation à la valeur personnelle. Par défaut, nous commençons à croire que :

  • Les femmes au foyer sont capables de tout gérer.
  • Les femmes au foyer, surtout les femmes au foyer pieuses, ne sont jamais frustrées.
  • Une femme au foyer doit anticiper tous les besoins de sa famille.

Si nous sommes honnêtes, nous savons que ces affirmations sont irréalistes. Les femmes au foyer ne peuvent pas tout faire. Toutes les femmes au foyer éprouvent de la frustration de temps à autre. Une mère ne peut pas être systématiquement un pas en avant par rapport aux besoins de sa famille.

Repenser la vie occupée

Les tâches ménagères et les soins apportés à nos familles remplissent nos journées. Parfois, ces seules tâches nous rendent extrêmement occupées. Mais qu’en est-il des activités extra-scolaires ou du niveau d’exigence élevé que nous nous imposons ? Il se peut que nous devions penser différemment afin de nous libérer d’habitudes qui menacent de nous contrôler.

Acceptez vos limites

Peut-être pouvez-vous assister à une réunion Tupperware, participer à une étude biblique et repeindre la salle de bain en une seule semaine. Mais devriez-vous le faire ? Les bonnes femmes au foyer s’autorisent à simplifier, même si elles préfèrent faire autrement. Cela signifie que si vous êtes une adepte de la fabrication de pain, il est acceptable de glisser quelques miches dans votre panier d’achats.

Évaluez ce qui cause des frustrations

Les sourires forcés peuvent cacher des frustrations intérieures, mais cela ne les guérit pas. Il est préférable d’admettre qu’il y a un problème puis de chercher une solution. J’ai dû apprendre cela à maintes reprises. Tous les membres de ma famille savent que nous dînons à 17 h 30. Mais l’habitude d’arriver en retard est en vogue, et cela me dérange.

Quand j’ai parlé de ma frustration à mon mari, il a simplement dit : « Pourquoi n’expliques-tu pas le problème et arrêtes d’être aussi tendue à ce sujet ? » Bon point. Chercher proactivement des solutions fonctionne pour de nombreux domaines problématiques.

Des femmes imparfaites font de bonnes femmes au foyer

Cessez de vous inquiéter de la perfection et prenez des décisions basées sur ce qui est le mieux pour aujourd’hui. Les femmes au foyer joyeuses et aimant s’amuser peuvent avoir quelques moutons de poussière sous les meubles, mais elles dégagent une aura qui attire les gens vers leur cœur et leur maison.

Tout le monde est différent quant à la quantité que nous pouvons gérer. D’un autre côté, tout le monde est pareil : nous avons tous des limites. Dans de futurs numéros, nous discuterons de la façon de gérer les points communs de surcharge.

Partie 2

Beaucoup de femmes au foyer se retrouvent étirées entre les engagements liés au foyer, à la famille et à d’autres activités. Aussi occupées que nous soyons, pourquoi continuons-nous à remplir nos agendas davantage ?

Il m’est facile de m’engager dans un nouveau projet puis de réaliser, à mi-chemin de la tâche, que j’ai dépassé mes limites. Trop souvent, j’ai surestimé le temps nécessaire pour mener à bien un projet et sous-estimé le temps qu’une tâche prendrait.

La surcharge d’engagements se produit par défaut. Lorsque nous jouons plusieurs rôles et ajoutons davantage de responsabilités, nous pouvons rapidement devenir esclaves des promesses que nous avons faites. La surcharge a tendance à épuiser notre énergie, émousser nos sens et anesthésier notre joie.

Reconnaître la surcharge

Parfois, plusieurs activités s’enchaînent rapidement. Normalement, nous pouvons composer avec des poussées d’activité à court terme. Mais si le flux d’activités est sans fin et que nous continuons d’ajouter des obligations, nous développons un schéma qui devient un mode de vie.

Trop d’engagements au-delà des devoirs normaux font de nous des candidates à la dépression et à l’épuisement. Personnellement, quand j’éprouve de l’insomnie, de l’apathie ou de l’irritabilité, il est temps d’examiner mon emploi du temps. Si des ajustements ne sont pas faits, quelqu’un ou quelque chose en pâtira.

Personne ne peut se surmener indéfiniment. Parfois, nous subissons des conséquences à force de maintenir un rythme qui dépasse nos ressources. Les symptômes de surcharge peuvent inclure un manque de sommeil, des relations tendues, la procrastination, la peur de l’échec et un système immunitaire vulnérable.

Se libérer de la surcharge

Identifier la surcharge exige une évaluation honnête de soi. Comment savoir si ce n’est qu’une saison occupée ou si l’occupation est devenue la nouvelle norme ? Refusez-vous une demande parce que la vie est trop pleine, ou est-ce une excuse ? Devez-vous dire « oui » immédiatement ? Avec de la pratique, vous pouvez apprendre à vous retirer avant d’atteindre le point de surcharge.

Laissez mûrir une idée ou une demande avant de vous engager

Cela m’a épargné beaucoup de stress. Il y a tant de bonnes choses auxquelles participer, et de nouvelles inspirations arrivent chaque jour. Parfois, les tâches peuvent être intégrées dans mon/notre emploi du temps. D’autres fois, je dois simplement les laisser tomber et rester concentrée sur ce qui est le plus important. Envisagez d’attendre quelques heures avant d’intégrer de nouvelles idées et demandes.

Cherchez des conseils, surtout ceux de votre mari

Une célèbre productrice de beignets a été invitée à tenir un stand lors d’une vente aux enchères. Elle a demandé à son mari ce qu’il en pensait. Il a dit : « Tant que tu ne te plains pas et ne stresses pas comme l’an dernier, ça m’est égal. » Son mari disait-il « oui » ou « non » ? Cette dame devrait saisir l’indice que la fabrication de beignets ajoutait d’une manière ou d’une autre du stress. Soit elle ne devrait pas le faire, soit ils doivent ensemble chercher une solution viable.

Évaluez régulièrement votre emploi du temps

Tenez un calendrier détaillé pour avoir une image des événements passés, présents et futurs. Si votre famille a eu la grippe la semaine dernière et que vous prévoyez un voyage hors de l’État la semaine prochaine, devez-vous ajouter davantage ? Quelle est la santé émotionnelle de votre famille ? Votre mari est-il stressé par son travail ? Parfois, il vaut mieux garder un créneau vide afin qu’il puisse être comblé par ce qui est important maintenant. Vous ne pouvez rien faire correctement si vous êtes trop dispersée. Trop d’obligations rendent difficile d’être personnellement reposée et agréable. Choisir ses engagements avec sagesse vous aidera à investir votre énergie là où elle est le plus précieuse pour aujourd’hui.

A wonderful thing about being a Christian is anticipating the day when we feast our eyes on the magnificent beauty of our God. Quite likely, we have all created mental pictures of what we think God might look like, although we know that our wildest imaginations will be exceeded. “Thine eyes shall see the king in his beauty: they shall behold the land that is very far off” (Isaiah 33:17). The Bible is full of descriptive word pictures attempting to give us a brief glimpse into the realms of the heavenly. The landscape on the hills of glory, the wonderful creatures that dwell there, and most of all, the Supreme Being on the throne, all defy our human attempt to grasp and understand the beauty and glory of our God.

At times we admire beauty in a song, a work of art, a story, or even another person, but David describes the delight of gazing at the beauty of God. “One thing have I desired of the LORD, that will I seek after; that I may dwell in the house of the LORD all the days of my life, to behold the beauty of the LORD, and to inquire in his temple” (Psalm 27:4). God is beautiful because His excellence is attractive— His character is flawless. David experienced the pleasure that comes from knowing and experiencing God in all His fullness. How does God express His Beauty?

Through the Gospel

“In whom the god of this world hath blinded the minds of them which believe not, lest the light of the glorious gospel of Christ, who is the image of God, should shine unto them. For we preach not ourselves, but Christ Jesus the Lord; and ourselves your servants for Jesus' sake. For God, who commanded the light to shine out of darkness, hath shined in our hearts, to give the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ” (2 Corinthians 4:4-6). In the awfulness of the Passion of Christ, we find a profound and sober beauty— the beauty of a sacrifice made by a sinless Savior for undeserving humanity. Sometimes the most stirring kind of beauty is found in things we cannot fully comprehend.

There is beauty in weeping of Mary and the disciples around the cross that held the lifeless body of their beloved Master. But when dawn broke on resurrection morning, despair turned into hope and grief into joy.

We see a beautiful scene at the Mount of Olives forty days later as the same disciples wistfully gazed into the sky, watching as their risen Lord disappeared into the heavens. With great joy, they returned to Jerusalem, with the promise of His return burning in their hearts, to wait for the coming of the Holy Spirit.

Today we expectantly wait for the Son of God to appear from heaven with power and great glory to complete the work of salvation. Then will we look upon Him in all His splendor and beauty. “For now we see through a glass, darkly; but then face to face: now I know in part; but then shall I know even as also I am known” (1 Corinthians 13:12).

How should we, as God's image-bearers, reflect His beauty through the Gospel? God is an uncreated eternal being, and man was created in His image to reflect His glory and beauty. However, this beauty has been marred by sin and is no longer a worthy representation of God's character. But, there is redemption! Very little surpasses the beauty of a life that was once bruised and broken by sin but is now restored, redeemed, and made whole by the Gospel. “To appoint unto them that mourn in Zion, to give unto them beauty for ashes, the oil of joy for mourning, the garment of praise for the spirit of heaviness; that they might be called trees of righteousness, the planting of the LORD, that He might be glorified” (Isaiah 61:3). Atheists challenge the existence of God, scientists argue against Biblical creation, scholars question the inerrancy of scripture, but nobody can dispute the testimony of a redeemed life.

Through Creation

“The heavens declare the glory of God; and the firmament showeth His handy work” (Psalm 19:1). All beauty in the created world comes from God. A beautiful sunset, a lovely rose, a towering redwood, a majestic mountain peak, all testify of the beauty of God illustrated in creation. As road signs along the highway guide us to our destination, likewise, creation directs mankind to God himself. “For the invisible things of Him from the creation of the world are clearly seen . . .” (Romans 1:20). These gifts of creation are given to give us a brief glimpse of the One who created them.

How should we, as part of God's creation, reflect His creative beauty? Although we cannot make something out of nothing, God has designed us to be creative, using the resources of His creation and our intellectual abilities to make life practical. The fulfilling sense of accomplishment derived from a job well done has its origin in creation, where God regarded His work and declared it to be good. In our attempt to live non-extravagant lives we sometimes fail to take joy in the beautiful things in life. It is right and good and in harmony with how we were created to find pleasure in things of beauty. Ungodly men have used this gift of creativity many times for evil means. So much the more, let us glorify God by using His creation in ways that reflect His character.

A warning for all who love nature and creation (natural and man-made): let us be careful to not elevate earthly beauty above the Creator, which leads to idolatry. Sunsets fade, redwoods tumble, roses wilt, the human body turns to dust again, but God remains. Life and all of its beauty begins and ends with God.

Through Music and Sound

“And I heard a voice from heaven, as the voice of many waters, and as the voice of a great thunder: and I heard the voice of harpers harping with their harps” (Revelation 14:2) According to the book of Revelation, God's throne is surrounded by sound: thundering and lightning; praises flowing from the angels, the four beasts and twenty elders, and the great multitude which no man can number; and the new song by the one hundred and forty four thousand.

God created the beauty of sound to glorify Himself in ways that mere words cannot. The intricacy of His creativity is powerfully displayed in the way various sound frequencies come together to create a beautiful and heavenly harmony. It is honoring to God for mankind to take pleasure in the beauty of sounds He has created for His glory. The person who loves God will be drawn to Him whenever He is serenaded by pleasing sounds: the people of God singing the songs of Zion, the prayers of the saints, the wind whispering through the treetops, the songbird praising its Maker, the rumble of thunder, or the simple patter of rain on the roof.

How should we, as instruments of sound, reflect God's beauty through sound? We should always seek to listen to and resemble the sounds and harmonies of heaven. Although we will never be able to completely accomplish this on earth, it should be a lifelong endeavor. The questions have been asked,” Should we always be trying to improve our music making?” and “when have we reached ‘good enough’?” We will never be able to attain heavenly perfection, so the question should rather be asked, “Are we giving God the best we have?” Some people have more singing capabilities than others, but the question remains. “Are we giving our best or are we satisfied with an inferior sacrifice?” Let us be producers of God-honoring sounds that bring joy to the heart of the Creator!

Through the Church:

The Bible speaks extensively about the beauty of God's people. “Zion,” “The Temple,” “The Mountain of God,” “Jerusalem,” and“The Church” are synonymous expressions woven throughout scripture referring to the habitation of God's people on the earth. It is God's desire that His beauty would be reflected in the lives of His people. “Great is the LORD, and greatly to be praised in the city of our God, in the mountain of His holiness. Beautiful for situation, the joy of the whole earth, is Mount Zion, on the sides of the north, the city of the great King” (Psalm 48:1-2).

Nothing is dearer to the heart of God than His church. When the children of Israel journeyed through the wilderness, they built the tabernacle as a place for God to dwell among them. When Solomon dedicated the temple as God's dwelling place, God was very pleased and 2 Chronicles 7:1 says the glory of the Lord filled the temple. The temple was considered the House of the Lord–Jesus himself referred to it numerous times as God's house and was very passionate that it should be kept holy.

Today, neither the tabernacle nor the temple hosts the presence of God but rather His divine passion is concentrated on the church of Jesus Christ. Here are the people who truly love Him and are willing to lay down their lives for Him. Here are the people who are willing to give up their rights as individuals and surrender themselves to a greater cause. Here is where many a saint has given His very life's blood for the Gospel. And here is where one day our Savior will return as He has promised, and will transport His bride, the church, to her eternal habitation. “And I John saw the holy city, New Jerusalem, coming down from God out of heaven, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband. And I heard a great voice out of heaven saying, Behold, the tabernacle of God is with men, and he will dwell with them, and they shall be His people, and God Himself shall be with them, and be their God” (Revelation 21:2-3).

How should we, as God's people, reflect His beauty in the church? By dwelling together in unity and harmony with love for all men, especially the household of God. The church should be a place where the world can get a glimpse of what goes on in heaven. It should be a place where Christ is always elevated as the victorious conqueror of sin, death, and hell.

Sadly, many people have become disoriented with the church's failures and have walked away from the true apostolic faith. In spite of our disappointments, let us “lift up the hands which hang down and the feeble knees” (Hebrews 12:12) and let us press on. We will never have a higher calling, and never a more noble warfare to wage.

Lastly, how should we reflect His beauty in our lives? By delighting in Him. “Delight thyself also in the LORD; and He shall give thee the desires of thine heart” (Psalm 37:4). The greatest fulfillment in life comes from finding pleasure in bringing joy to the heart of God by delighting in what He delights in and loving what He loves. Let us never lose the wonder of the beauty of our Salvation!

作为基督徒，一件奇妙的事是我们可以期待有一天亲眼欣赏到我们神那极其华美的尊容。很可能，我们都曾在脑海中描绘出神可能的样子，尽管我们知道即便是最狂妄的想象也将被超越。“Thine eyes shall see the king in his beauty: they shall behold the land that is very far off” (Isaiah 33:17)。圣经充满了试图给我们短暂一瞥天国景象的描写性图画。荣耀山丘上的景致、居住于其中的奇妙生物，最重要的是宝座上的至高者，这一切都超越了人类去把握和明白神之美与荣耀的能力。

有时我们会在一首歌、一件艺术品、一个故事，甚至另一个人身上欣赏到美，但大卫描述的是注视神之美的喜乐。“One thing have I desired of the LORD, that will I seek after; that I may dwell in the house of the LORD all the days of my life, to behold the beauty of the LORD, and to inquire in his temple” (Psalm 27:4)。神之所以美，是因为他的卓越具有吸引力——他的品格无瑕。大卫经历了认识并感受那丰满之神所带来的喜乐。神如何彰显他的美？

Through the Gospel

“In whom the god of this world hath blinded the minds of them which believe not, lest the light of the glorious gospel of Christ, who is the image of God, should shine unto them. For we preach not ourselves, but Christ Jesus the Lord; and ourselves your servants for Jesus' sake. For God, who commanded the light to shine out of darkness, hath shined in our hearts, to give the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ” (2 Corinthians 4:4-6). 在基督受难的悲壮中，我们发现了一种深沉而庄严的美——一位无罪的救主为不配得的人类所献的牺牲之美。有时，最激动人心的美存在于我们无法完全理解的事物之中。

在玛利亚和门徒围绕着那装着他们所爱师傅无生命躯体的十字架而哭泣时，那里有一种美。但当复活晨曦破晓时，绝望转为盼望，悲痛转为喜乐。

四十天后，我们在橄榄山上看到一个美丽的场景：同样的门徒深情地凝望着天空，看着他们复活的主消失在天际。他们满怀大喜返回耶路撒冷，心中燃着他将再来的应许，等候圣灵降临。

今天我们带着盼望等候神的儿子从天而降，带着能力和大荣耀完成救赎的工作。到那时我们将得以看见他的一切荣光与美。“For now we see through a glass, darkly; but then face to face: now I know in part; but then shall I know even as also I am known” (1 Corinthians 13:12)。

作为神的形象承载者，我们当如何通过福音反映他的美？神是未受造的永恒存在，人被造为他的形象以反映他的荣耀与美。然而，这美因罪受损，不再是对神品格的配称表达。但有救赎！很少有事物能超越那曾被罪打伤破碎却因福音得以恢复、被救赎并重新被造为全然的生命之美。“To appoint unto them that mourn in Zion, to give unto them beauty for ashes, the oil of joy for mourning, the garment of praise for the spirit of heaviness; that they might be called trees of righteousness, the planting of the LORD, that He might be glorified” (Isaiah 61:3)。无神论者挑战神的存在，科学家质疑圣经所述的创造，学者怀疑圣经的无误，但无人能否认一个被救赎生命的见证。

Through Creation

“The heavens declare the glory of God; and the firmament showeth His handy work” (Psalm 19:1)。被造世界中的一切美都来自神。一幅美丽的落日、一朵可爱的玫瑰、一棵巍峨的红木、一座雄伟的山峰，都在见证创造中所显明的神之美。正如公路旁的路标引导我们到达目的地，创造同样把人指向神自身。“For the invisible things of Him from the creation of the world are clearly seen . . .” (Romans 1:20)。这些创造的恩赐是给我们短暂一瞥造物主的窗口。

作为神创造的一部分，我们当如何反映他创造之美？虽然我们不能无中生有，神却造我们为有创造性的，使用他所造之物的资源和我们的智慧能耐，使生命更为实用。从一项工作做得好所获得的成就感其根源在创造，当神看他的工作就说那是好的。在力求不过度奢侈的生活中，我们有时未能在世上美好的事物中找到喜乐。按照我们的受造样式，在美中找到喜乐是正当的、良善的。当不敬虔的人多次将这一创造性的恩赐用于邪恶目的时，我们更当用神所造之物以反映他品格的方式来荣耀他。

给所有热爱自然与创造（天然与人造）之人的一项警告：当心别将属世之美高举过造物主，这将导致偶像崇拜。日落会消逝，红木会倒下，玫瑰会凋谢，人体终究归于尘土，但神永存。生命与其一切美始于神，也终于神。

Through Music and Sound

“And I heard a voice from heaven, as the voice of many waters, and as the voice of a great thunder: and I heard the voice of harpers harping with their harps” (Revelation 14:2) 根据启示录，神的宝座周围充满声音：雷霆闪电；天使、四活物与二十四位长老的颂赞，及那无法计算的广大群众的赞美；还有十四万四千人所唱的新歌。

神造声音之美是为以言语无法尽述的方式荣耀自己。各类声频汇集成一段美丽而天上的和声，彰显出他创造的精巧。人若因神所造之声而得喜乐，并以此荣耀神，这是可敬的。爱神之人在悦耳之声中会被吸引到神面前：锡安子民唱赞歌，圣徒的祷告，风在树梢的低语，鸣禽赞美其造物主，雷声的轰鸣，或雨点敲打屋顶的简单节奏。

作为声音的器皿，我们当如何通过声音反映神之美？我们应常寻求听见并效法天上的声音与和声。虽然在世上我们永不能完全达成此目标，但应作为终生的追求。人们会问：“我们是否应不断努力改进我们的音乐？”以及“什么时候才算‘够好’？”我们永不能达到天上的完美，所以更应问：“我们是否把所能给的最好献给神？”有些人在歌唱上天赋优于他人，但问题依旧：“我们是献上最好的，还是满足于较差的祭物？”让我们成为发出荣耀神之声的制造者，给造物主的心带来喜乐！

Through the Church:

圣经广泛谈论神子民的美。“锡安”“殿”“神的山”“耶路撒冷”和“教会”是贯穿经文的同义表达，指向神在世上的子民所居之处。神愿意他的美在子民的生命中得以彰显。“Great is the LORD, and greatly to be praised in the city of our God, in the mountain of His holiness. Beautiful for situation, the joy of the whole earth, is Mount Zion, on the sides of the north, the city of the great King” (Psalm 48:1-2)。

没有什么比教会更为神所珍爱。当以色列人在旷野行走时，他们立会幕为神与他们同住之处。当所罗门将殿献为神居所时，神甚为喜悦，历代志下7章1节说耶和华的荣耀充满了殿。那殿被看为耶和华的殿——耶稣自己屡次称其为神的家，并极力要求当保持圣洁。

如今，既非会幕也非殿独自承载神的同在，而是神对耶稣基督之教会所集中的神圣热情。这里是那些真正爱他、愿为他舍命的人。这里是那些甘愿放弃个人权利、将自己交付给更大事业的人之所在。许多圣徒曾为福音献出宝血。并且有一天我们的救主必如他所应许的再来，将他的新妇──教会──携回她永恒的居所。“And I John saw the holy city, New Jerusalem, coming down from God out of heaven, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband. And I heard a great voice out of heaven saying, Behold, the tabernacle of God is with men, and he will dwell with them, and they shall be His people, and God Himself shall be with them, and be their God” (Revelation 21:2-3)。

作为神的子民，我们当如何在教会中反映他的美？当以爱心与彼此合一、和谐同居，尤其对神的家人保持爱心。教会应成为世人得以窥见天上情景的所在。它应成为基督常被高举为战胜罪、死与阴间的胜利征服者之处。

遗憾的是，许多人因教会的失败而迷失方向、远离了真正使徒的信仰。尽管有失望，让我们“lift up the hands which hang down and the feeble knees” (Hebrews 12:12)，并让我们继续前行。我们永远没有更高的呼召，也没有比这更为崇高的争战可打。

最后，我们当如何在个人生命中反映他的美？以在他里面喜乐为己乐。“Delight thyself also in the LORD; and He shall give thee the desires of thine heart” (Psalm 37:4)。生命中最大的满足来自于以在使神喜乐为乐：喜悦他所喜悦，爱他所爱。让我们永不失去我们得救之美的惊奇！
