Morals have to do with right and wrong behavior. Purity is being free from moral fault or guilt, marked by chastity, which is personal integrity. Purity contains nothing that does not properly belong there. As the title suggests, this article will be about doing right and being free from moral fault and guilt, living a life of integrity, and keeping our inside and outside free of anything that doesn’t properly belong.

Notice what scripture says about being pure. “Blessed are the pure in heart” (Matthew 5:8). “That ye may approve things that are excellent; that ye may be sincere (pure) and without offense till the day of Christ” (Philippians 1:10). “Think on things that are pure” (Philippians 4:8). “Keep thyself pure” (1Timothy 5:22). Revelation 19 says “The pure in heart shall see God.” Psalm 24:3-4 asks “Who shall see God?” The answer is “he that hath clean hands and a pure heart.” In other words, it is the people who are clean inside and out who will see God and enter His presence.

Being morally pure will not happen without strong determination and discipline. It has always been this way, but even more so today with the rise of technology and the availability of evil at our fingertips.

Sexual sins are not foreign to the church. In fact, they are not foreign to any people of any race. We cannot relax and let down our guard and suppose that our children will be safe from the evils of society and our humanity. We must show by example and teach our children and youth if we expect them to stay clean in this corrupt society. We cannot assume that if a person dresses a certain way, all is well on the inside. The story is not told fully by the outside. The Pharisees made the outside look good, while the inside was full of corruption. Jesus said, “Cleanse first the inside of the cup and platter that the outside may be clean also” (Matthew 23:26). We too should give primary attention to heart issues. When the heart is clean, then the outside will be able to be cleansed also.

I John 1:6 says, “if we say that we have fellowship with Him and walk in darkness (light on the outside and darkness on the inside), we lie and do not practice the truth.” Internal darkness will always destroy fellowship and kill relationships—every time.

This is intended to be a message of hope, not discouragement. If you have a hidden dark spot, confess it and get rid of it. You can be free! It is possible to be free from Satan's clutches and live an open, transparent life with joy in your soul. You don't need to go through life trying to hide the darkness of evil. Jesus wants to forgive and heal.

Satan is cruel. In John 10:10, Jesus said, “the devil wants to steal, kill, and destroy. He wants to steal your purity, kill your character, and destroy” all godly relationships. His interest is to break up your home, destroy your respect, and send you to hell. All the while, he is luring you through the lust of your flesh, with his sword drawn to bind and kill you.

Moral sin is so shameful and hard to admit. The natural thing is to try to hide when we do wrong. Children who learn to hide wrongdoing early in life naturally develop into youth who hide things from parents, schoolteachers, and ministers. This person will need to learn to be open and transparent, or the time will come when they will be hiding things from their companion. Hiding results is a double life and leads to more bondage and broken relationships. People who have closed doors in some corners of their lives will be possessive of their phones and unwilling to share their passwords with a trusted partner. It seems we easily forget how futile it is to hide from God. Hebrews 4:13 says, “Neither is there any creature that is not manifest in his sight: but all things are naked and opened unto the eyes of him with whom (we will give account to).” How can we be so naive and foolish to think we can hide anything from God? Or take it a step further: Why would we want to hide something from Him? Numbers 32:23 is still very true, saying, “Be sure your sin will find you out.” God loves you too much to let you keep hiding what needs to be brought out and forgiven.

Sexual sins are also extremely deceptive. It usually happens the way James described it in chapter one. We are enticed, drawn away, pulled like a magnet off-center, feel a surge of desire, make sure no one is looking, and our tracks are covered, step closer to the forbidden, feel more desire, and begin very quickly to lose reasoning and sound thinking, not able to calculate consequences much like an intoxicated person, then James 1:15 happens: “Then when lust hath conceived, it bringeth forth sin: and sin, when it is finished, bringeth forth death” Verse 16 says, “Do not (be deceived) my beloved brethren.”

James would tell us not to lust after what isn't ours, not even a hint. The Bible tells us to flee three things. One of these is fornication, which can be broadened to all sexual sins. Don't dabble with it; don't take a second look; get away from it! Replace those thoughts with upbuilding thoughts of God and His way. Sing an old hymn; thankfully we can't think of two things at once. Whatever it takes, flee from that lustful desire. It will take you farther than you want to go and cost more than you want to pay. Run the tape to the end and ask yourself, if I follow what I am being tempted for, will I have what I want? Satan always promises pleasure, but then delivers pain. Remember, Satan has never invented a pleasure; he only takes what God made to be pure and good, perverts it, and offers it back in its perverted form. Remember, Satan's sword is drawn to kill at this point. Flee evil desires!

Don’t follow your lust. Pornography is extremely addictive and has ensnared many a person. Promise Keepers said 65% of men in their survey were addicted. Porn addiction is like alcohol or drugs. They tell us that the brain is calling for endorphins to be poured into it, whether from addiction to alcohol, drugs, or porn. I emphasize again that the men and women who make it to victory will be those who, like Daniel of old, purpose in their hearts, not to defile themselves.

This subject is also for our sisters, and a few questions seem appropriate. What inside your life is neatly tucked away and hidden? Have life's disappointments caused an emptiness that makes taking an 'emotional Tylenol' make you feel better for a short while? Is your emotional connection secure where God has planned it to be?

Young girls should be taught to develop a healthy reserve with men. Not with a haughty attitude and never a smile, but also not too free in relating to young men. Our society is geared exactly the opposite, and from kindergarten on, boys and girls are being teased about special friendships. As a result, children grow up with little to no reserve. Socializing in messaging between genders should be avoided outside of family relationships. This will develop a habit in youth that will one day need to be broken if they expect to live an open, transparent life with a spouse. Think of it this way: would you want your spouse to socialize with the opposite gender on social media?

Sisters, be careful what books you read. Romance novels deaden the desire for the Word of God and give unrealistic expectations of married life. These books give the idea that the right man somewhere would be your key to fulfillment and happiness in life. Only Jesus can fill the hole that sin has brought to every human being today. No man or woman will ever be able to give the security and tranquility of the soul that we all want so badly. This hurt in the heart will never be quenched by Band-Aids or pain relievers. They help only for a moment, and when they wear off, the cry of the heart is even louder. Unwholesome books deaden a taste for the things of God, and instead create a craving for junk food and pain relievers.

Another concern to the sisters is the amount of time you spend online. There is no end to feeding the craving for finery, uniqueness, charm, and beauty. Don't let these things be the drive of your life as they will never cry out 'enough' and will do nothing to satisfy the soul or point your children in the right direction. Consider the amount of time you spend hosting parties. Over the years, I have seen names come and go of business opportunities and products that one must have. But alas, in a few years, we cannot even remember those names and all the while the children were growing and by now are adults. Consider the real needs in your life and your responsibilities, and then decide which will bring eternal investments. Women with children need to limit hobbies they so much enjoy because, at this moment, they are blessed with children who have never-dying souls and time with them is an eternal investment. Remember that your husband and children are far more worthy of your time than spending hours at another party.

How can we live a morally pure life?

Be Humble. James 5 says, “Confess your faults one to another that ye may be healed.” It takes humility and brokenness to acknowledge our needs, but brokenness is the key to victory. I Peter 5:5 tells us that God gives grace to the humble. One of the most comprehensive definitions of grace is unmerited divine assistance given to humans for regeneration and sanctification. Regeneration is 'redeeming grace,' and sanctification is 'transforming grace.' The truth of this is that God gives 'transforming grace' to the humble. This grace changes us from the inside out making us holy. This aspect of grace must be desired and sought after as much as redeeming grace was when God saved us. This is probably the single most important step in overcoming addictions of any kind. Be humble enough to make it a daily prayer to God for His transforming grace. Jesus taught in Matthew 23:26, where He said, "First clean the inside of the cup, so that the outside may be clean also."

Be Honest. Examine your thoughts, actions, temptations, the things you struggle with, anger, lust, pride, bitterness, etc. Are you as spiritual as you portray yourself to be on the outside? Strip the veneer and admit the need for help.

Be transparent. Romans 2:16 tells of the day when God will judge the secrets of men. We are so foolish to think we can hide evil. We can hide for a while, but someday our actions will stand naked before an all-knowing God. Why would we try to hide something now? Those hidden things can be sent before to judgment, and a guilt-free life can be a reality today. Be transparent; it must be a working goal.

Tell yourself the truth. When you are tempted, consider the end of your lustful desire. Will you get what you want? Will this craving be satisfied, or will it only crave more? If you saw your brother doing what you are going after, how would it look? How will it look thirty years down the road if you follow your evil desire? Will it bring joy or sorrow? Will it be a help to someone, or will someone else be scared? Tell yourself the truth before you become intoxicated and unable to make rational judgments.

Teach your eyes to bounce. You can't help what you look at the first time, but you can control what you look at twice. Make it a practice till it becomes a habit to turn your eyes in a different direction whenever you see a sight that leads to impure thoughts.

Teaching our children. This should be heavy on our hearts from early childhood. If we don’t teach our children that God made us in the image of Himself, which needs to be kept pure, someone else will teach them to be secretive and make them feel impure. Stay close to your children and teach them as they mature.

Keep your emotions. This is a safety in our corrupt society. The further you get from this, the more vulnerable you will be to corruption. Keep your spouse first in life, the one you share with and are tied to emotionally.

Flee lust and fornication. Run from it! These cravings are addictions that must be broken. Remember, what you feed grows, and what you starve dies. These addictions can be broken, but you will need to feed the relationships that God has given and starve the hurtful ones.

God has made us in a way that when we love the things He loves, our heart still has room to love more. No matter how many children, grandchildren, or godly friends we have, our hearts still have room to love more. But the moment we start to love what God has forbidden, it begins to replace and destroy all other love, filling our hearts with emptiness, pain, and loneliness, which leads to a bitter end.

Many a man has come to his senses and seen the utter foolishness of the path he took. Some tried to hide impure conduct and were successful until late in life. Others kept it hidden till after they were gone. A question to ponder, Is it worth it? Of course, the answer is a resounding NO!

How wonderful to live an open life free of guilt and have peace with God and the assurance of sins forgiven, so that one day we will be taken out of this evil world and ushered into the presence of our Holy God.

Two forces lie within my breast,
The one I love, the one I hate.
But the one I feed will dominate.

—The author’s dad

The more honestly I name
what is true about myself,
The less I need to hide and defend,
and posture and pretend.

—Dan Allender

道德关系到行为的是非。清洁是免于道德过失或内疚，带有贞洁之意，即个人的廉正。清洁不包含任何本不应存在之物。正如题目所示，本文将讨论行善与免于道德过失和内疚，活出廉正的生命，并保持我们内在与外在不被任何不当之物玷污。

注意圣经如何谈论清洁。“Blessed are the pure in heart” (Matthew 5:8). “That ye may approve things that are excellent; that ye may be sincere (pure) and without offense till the day of Christ” (Philippians 1:10). “Think on things that are pure” (Philippians 4:8). “Keep thyself pure” (1Timothy 5:22). Revelation 19 says “The pure in heart shall see God.” Psalm 24:3-4 asks “Who shall see God?” The answer is “he that hath clean hands and a pure heart.” In other words, it is the people who are clean inside and out who will see God and enter His presence.

要在道德上清洁，不靠坚强的决心与纪律是办不到的。历来如此，然而在今日科技兴起、邪恶触手可及的情况下，更是如此。

性方面的罪在教会并不罕见。事实上，各族各类的人都不陌生。我们不能放松警惕，想当然地以为我们的孩子会免于社会和人性之恶。若指望他们在败坏的社会中保持清洁，就必须以身作则并教导我们的儿女与青年。我们不能以为一个人外表怎么穿着内心就一定无虞。外表并不能完整叙说内里的故事。法利赛人使外表看起来光鲜，内里却充满败坏。耶稣说：“Cleanse first the inside of the cup and platter that the outside may be clean also” (Matthew 23:26). 我们也应当首先关注心的问题。当心是洁净的，外表也能够被洁净。

I John 1:6 says, “if we say that we have fellowship with Him and walk in darkness (light on the outside and darkness on the inside), we lie and do not practice the truth.” 内在的黑暗必然摧毁团契并毁坏关系——每一次都是如此。

这篇信息意在带来希望，而不是灰心。如果你有隐藏的暗点，就认罪并除去它。你可以得自由！摆脱撒但掌控、活出一个内心喜乐、坦然透明的生活是可能的。你不需终生掩饰邪恶的黑暗。耶稣愿意赦免并医治。

撒但很残酷。约翰福音10:10中，耶稣说，“the devil wants to steal, kill, and destroy. He wants to steal your purity, kill your character, and destroy” 一切敬虔的关系。他的兴趣是拆散你的家庭、毁坏你的尊荣并把你送往地狱。与此同时，他以肉体的情欲引诱你，拔剑要捆绑并杀害你。

道德之罪令人羞愧且难以承认。人的本性是当犯错时要掩饰。早年学会掩饰过错的孩子，往往自然成长为对父母、老师和传道人隐瞒事情的青年。这样的人需要学会开放与透明，否则迟早会对伴侣隐瞒。隐瞒导致双重生活，并引向更多的捆绑与破碎的关系。在人生某些角落有封闭之门的人，常会对手机占有欲强，不愿与信任的伴侣分享密码。我们似乎很容易忘记向上帝掩藏是多么徒劳。Hebrews 4:13 says, “Neither is there any creature that is not manifest in his sight: but all things are naked and opened unto the eyes of him with whom (we will give account to).” 我们怎能如此天真愚蠢以为能向神隐藏任何事？更进一步想：我们为何要向祂隐藏？Numbers 32:23 仍然真实地说，“Be sure your sin will find you out.” 神爱你，祂不会让你继续隐藏那些需要被揭露并赦免的事。

性罪同样极具欺骗性。通常如雅各在第一章所描述般发生。我们被诱惑、被引走、像磁铁般被拉离正轨，感到欲望的涌动，确保无人窥见并掩盖踪迹，向禁果又近一步，欲望更强，理性与清晰思维迅速丧失，像喝醉的人一般无法衡量后果，然后发生雅各书1:15所说：“Then when lust hath conceived, it bringeth forth sin: and sin, when it is finished, bringeth forth death” 第16节说，“Do not (be deceived) my beloved brethren.”

雅各要我们不要贪恋不属于我们的东西，哪怕是一丝一毫。圣经叫我们奔逃三样事物，其中之一是淫乱，这可扩及到一切性罪。不要涉足；不要多看一眼；远离它！以建造人的事、神和祂方式的思想取而代之。唱首旧圣歌；感谢神我们不能同时想两件事。无论如何，赶快逃离那淫欲的渴望。它会把你带到比你想去的更远的地方，代价比你想支付的更大。把事情的结局想清楚并问自己：若我顺从这诱惑，我会得到我想要的吗？撒但总是承诺享乐，最终却带来痛苦。记住，撒但从未创造任何享乐；他只是取用神所造原本纯洁美好的事物，曲解并以其堕落的形态重新奉上。记住，撒但此刻拔剑是要杀人。逃避邪欲！

不要随从你的欲望。色情极易成瘾，已缠绕许多人。Promise Keepers 的调查说有65% 的男性成瘾。色情成瘾如同酒精或毒品。他们告诉我们，无论是对酒精、毒品或色情的成瘾，大脑都在呼求内啡肽被释放。我再次强调，得胜的男女将是那些像古时但以理一样，在心里立定主意不使自己污秽的人。

这个课题也针对我们的姐妹，以下几个问题颇为适切。你内心生活中有哪些整齐地藏匿起来的东西？人生的失望是否造成一种空虚，使得服用“情绪类止痛药”能暂时让你感觉好些？你的情感连结是否在神所安排之处得到稳固？

要教导年轻女孩对男人保持健康的矜持。不是以傲慢的态度或永不微笑，而是与年轻男性相处时不要过于随便。我们的社会正好相反，从幼儿园起，男孩和女孩就被嘲弄有关特殊友谊。结果，孩子长大后几乎没有保留。性别间在通信上的私下社交应当避免，除非在家庭关系内。这样可以培养青年的习惯，若他们期望与配偶活出坦然透明的生活，将来就不必再打破旧习。这样想：你愿意你的配偶在社交媒体上与异性频繁社交吗？

姐妹们，要留心你读的书。言情小说会麻木对神话语的渴望，并对婚姻生活产生不切实际的期待。这类书让人以为某个对的人会成为你满足与幸福的钥匙。只有耶稣能填补罪给每个人带来的空洞。没有任何男女能给出我们心灵深切渴望的安全与安宁。这心中的伤口不会被创可贴或止痛药所平息。它们只暂时有用，失效之后，心的呼喊更为响亮。不健康的读物会麻木对神之事的味觉，反而制造对垃圾食品与止痛药的渴求。

另一个对姐妹们的顾虑是你在线上花费的时间。追求精致、独特、魅力与美貌的欲望无穷无尽。不要让这些成为你生命的驱动力，因为它们永不会说“够了”，也无法满足灵魂或指引你的儿女走正路。考虑你为举办聚会所花的时间。多年间，我见过一时风行的商业机会和必备产品的名字来来去去。但几年后我们连这些名字都记不起来，与此同时孩子们在成长，如今已成了成年人。思量你生活中的真实需要和你的职责，然后决定哪些会带来永恒的投资。带着孩子的妇女需要限制她们喜欢的业余爱好，因为此时此刻，她们蒙福有不朽之灵的孩子，与孩子相处的时光是一项永恒的投资。记住，你的丈夫和孩子比你去参加另一个聚会更值得你花时间。

我们如何活出道德洁净的生命？

当卑微。雅各书5章说，“Confess your faults one to another that ye may be healed.” 承认我们的需要需要谦卑与柔碎，但柔碎是得胜的关键。彼得前书5:5告诉我们，神赐恩给谦卑的人。恩典最全面的定义之一是神无酬的帮助，赐给人以重生与成圣。重生是“救赎的恩典”，成圣是“改变的恩典”。事实是神将“改变的恩典”赐给谦卑的人。这恩典从内而外改变我们，使我们成为圣洁。这样的恩典必须像我们得救时所寻求的救赎恩典一样被渴求与寻求。这大概是克服任何成瘾的最重要一步。谦卑到每天向神祈求祂的改变之恩。当耶稣在马太23:26教导说，"First clean the inside of the cup, so that the outside may be clean also."

诚实。审视你的思想、行为、诱惑、挣扎之处、愤怒、欲望、骄傲、苦毒等。你外表所呈现的属灵，是否真如你所表明？剥去表面的光泽并承认需要帮助。

透明。罗马书2:16谈到那日神要审判人的隐秘。我们多么愚蠢以为能隐藏邪恶。我们或许能隐藏一时，但有一天我们的行为要在无所不知的神面前赤裸陈明。现在为何还要试图隐藏？那些隐藏的事可被送到前面受审，如今就能过无愧的生活。要透明；这必须是一个努力的目标。

对自己讲真话。当你受诱惑时，思考你淫欲之欲望的结局。你会得到你想要的吗？这种渴求会被满足，还是只会越渴越深？如果你看见你的弟兄做你正要追求的事，会是什么样子？若你顺从邪欲，三十年后会如何？会带来喜乐还是悲伤？会帮助人，还是使他人害怕？在你被迷醉并丧失理性判断之前，先对自己讲真话。

训练你的眼睛学会移开。你无法控制第一次看见什么，但你能控制第二次会看向何处。养成习惯，每当看到引发不洁念头的景象时，立刻把目光转向别处，直至成为习惯。

教导我们的孩子。从幼年起这应当成为我们心中的重担。若我们不教孩子神照祂形象造我们，需要被保持洁净，别人就会教他们隐秘并使他们感到不洁。亲近你的孩子，并随他们成长教导他们。

节制情感。在我们败坏的社会中，这是一个安全措施。你越远离这点，越容易被败坏所侵蚀。把你的配偶放在生命的首位，与之分享并在情感上相连。

远避情欲与淫乱。逃离它们！这些渴望是必须被打破的成瘾。记住，喂养什么它就生长，饿死什么它就消亡。成瘾可以被打破，但你需要喂养神所赐的关系并饿死那些有害的关系。

神造我们的方式是：当我们爱神所爱的事物时，心仍然有空间去爱更多。无论我们有多少孩子、孙儿或虔诚的朋友，心仍然能继续去爱更多。但一旦我们开始爱神所禁止的事物，它就会开始替代并毁坏其他一切的爱，填满我们的心以空虚、痛苦与孤独，最终落得苦涩的结局。

许多男人回过神来，看见自己所走之路的极端愚蠢。有些人试图隐藏不洁行为并成功到晚年。另一些人则维持隐藏直到身后。值得深思的问题是：这值得吗？答案当然是响亮的“不”！

何等美好，能活出无愧的公开生活，与神和好，确信罪已得赦免，终有一天我们将被从这邪恶的世界带走，迎入我们圣洁神的面前。

Two forces lie within my breast,
The one I love, the one I hate.
But the one I feed will dominate.

—The author’s dad

The more honestly I name
what is true about myself,
The less I need to hide and defend,
and posture and pretend.

—Dan Allender

The winter of 1882 unfolded in the small southern town of Tuscumbia, Alabama. A happy, normal two-year-old girl fell desperately ill with a strange fever. The fever came and went, came and went, and came again. The family doctor feared the child would die of the strain, but the child was strong and one day the fever finally left for good. The following day the mother waved a hand past her daughter's face, but the child did not blink. Subsequent efforts wrought no results and a new day dawned upon the family with a blind daughter.

As the child gained strength enough to resume play, the great dinner bell released its peal to all around, but Helen did not respond. Other noises produced similar results and the Keller family came to the stark realization that life would never be the same again. Most of us may never face the grim circumstances that Helen Keller's family did, but each of us will certainly endure hardships tailored specifically by our God.

The human mind is an amazing and intricate creation. Though many have sought to understand it, its operational ability remains incomprehensible to mankind. It is no small wonder that a portion of the keenest insight into the health of the mind is revealed in God's Word. “For God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind.” (2 Timothy 1:7)

Fear is the ominous adversary to a sound mind. It towers over the soul and taunts the saint with its menacing derision. Fear can take a sunny meadow and turn it into a lonely wilderness. It can render a grand wedding celebration as dark as a cave, and turn a banquet fit for a king into a nauseating affair. It is the most powerful and devastating tool in the devil's employment. Despite many bold claims, none are exempt from its wielding. “A dreadful sound is in his ears: in prosperity the destroyer shall come upon him. He believeth not that he shall return out of darkness, and he is waited for of the sword.” (Job 15:21, 22) It is fear that stands to attack and quench all the prosperity of the soul. If we are to resist it in these days, we he must rise with all diligence in defiant warfare.

We do not need to look very far to behold the disarmament and weakening of man's mind. Medication for the mind ranks among the leading prescriptions consumed in America today. This is no pointed accusation at any individuals who may find themselves in need of medical assistance to control their mind. But it takes no scholar to look at obesity and consider the diet, to see rebellious teens and connect it to the infrastructure of the home, or to see men's hearts (minds) failing them and believe that fear is at the root. While some may totally master their diet, few can claim to be accomplished parents. Fewer yet are those who are not, at times, accosted by fear. Though pride and sense may keep the outward man in check, and remaining perfectly calm, the inward man, at least subconsciously, must deal with the strain. Americans love to claim the motto, "No fear!" but our medication consumption tells a different story. Paul claimed no exemption, for he was “troubled on every side; without were fightings, within were fears.” (2 Corinthians 7:5)

What do we fear? Loss, pain, and humility. No one likes to lose something that we have fought to obtain. No one enjoys pain. No one loves to be humiliated. Still, we do not need to read far in the Scriptures to realize that these are often the avenues that God uses to further urge His servants down the path into His likeness. There is no insurance on earth that can secure the vibrancy of youth, the love of a family, or the respect of friends. The things that supply us with earth's greatest vanguard are all vulnerable to the risks of loss. Therefore, we fear. Though we lie in bed until the dawn of the morning, we can in no wise increase our stature nor alleviate the loss that God has laid upon our lives. This anxiety only furthers our grief and adds fuel to our fears.

“Be careful for nothing; but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God. And the peace of God, which passeth all understanding, shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus.” (Philippians 4:6 7) Herein is the keeping of our hearts and minds: prayer, peace, and thanksgiving.

Like a skillful artisan we must carefully weave these two scriptures together on the loom of life for there seems to be a direct correlation between the fruitful - power, love and sound mind, to the “rootful”- prayer, peace, and thankfulness. There will be no conquering of our fears without these things, and every society that is anemic to these ingredients will certainly be handicapped.

Prayer Begets Power

In our weakened condition we cannot apprehend prayer as we ought. It is then we must rely on those who can or perhaps the Spirit, which maketh intercession for us with groanings which cannot be uttered. Communing with the Omnipotent Head of the universe is a tremendously bold task. Many will administer prayer as merely a formal task, seeking to be perfectly reverent in it. This is not communing as with a friend, nor is it bold. It is more apt to fall under the description of fear. The remedial therapy for fear is in pouring out all our anxiety, bitterness, and complaint onto our God. The saints of yesteryear had been known to vehemently pour out their accusations and the bitterness of their soul unto God.

“Then Job answered and said, Even to day is my complaint bitter: my stroke is heavier than my groaning. Oh that I knew where I might find him! That I might come even to his seat! I would order my cause before him, and fill my mouth with arguments. I would know the words which he would answer me, and understand what he would say unto me. Will he plead against me with his great power? No; but he would put strength in me.” (Job 23:1-6)

  • David —“I poured out my complaint before him; I shewed before him my trouble.” (Psalm 142:2)
  • Hannah —“For out of the abundance of my complaint and grief have I spoken hitherto.” (1 Samuel 1:16)
  • Jeremiah —“He hath filled me with bitterness, he hath made me drunken with wormwood.”
    (Lamentations 3:15)
  • Naomi —“Call me Mara: for the Almighty hath dealt very bitterly with me.” (Ruth 1:20)
  • Hezekiah —“He will cut me off with pining sickness: from day even to night wilt thou make an end of me.” (Isaiah 38:12)
  • Jesus — “My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?” (Matthew 27:46)

All these spewed forth bold accusations and complaints against God in fervent prayer and none of them offended Him. On the contrary, God had not given them the spirit of fear but of power, and they serve as our examples. It was faithless Ahab who was told to ask of God a sign in the heavens or earth. In his pious reply he refused to "tempt" God. This lack of boldness and abundance of fear is more tempting to God than the abundance of bitterness in our complaint for “there is no fear in love; but perfect love casteth out fear: because fear hath torment. He that feareth is not made perfect in love.” (1 John 4:18)

Peace Begets Love

We are all at rest with the things we love. "Great peace have they which love thy law: and nothing shall offend them.” (Psalm 119:165) A sparkling young child who is at peace with his father worships the man and strives to imitate him. Through the lad's tender eyes, his father's character is unflawed. His skill is unmatched. Even the brand of vehicle he drives is the best, and he emulates his every action. Even though every father knows the limitations of his son's expectations, we all bask in the seasonal loyalty. It is knowledge and fear that undermines this loyal love. An abusive father will destroy such childhood esteem and fear will be its replacement. It was through base fear that the evil servant buried his talent and did not trade with it. In his eyes his master was austere and to be feared. But God has not given us the spirit of fear but of love.

“We love him, because he first loved us. If a man say, I love God, and hateth his brother, he is a liar: for he that loveth not his brother whom he hath seen, how can he love God whom he hath not seen?” (1 John 4:19, 20) The soul who is affected by this love cannot but imitate it. He is at great peace with his Father’s love and the eyes through which he views his Father's character can only enlist replication. However dire the circumstances we may find ourselves in, this spirit of love and peace will carry us through whatever opposition we may meet with on life's pathway. Jacob made nothing of the hard service he was to endure for Rachel; the spirit of love to God will set us above the fear of man, and all the hurt that a man can do us.

Thankfulness Begets a Sound Mind

We do not need to study happy souls long to find buried within the bedrock of each one, a foundation of gratitude. The spirit of a sound mind, or quietness of mind, is a peaceable enjoyment of life. We are oftentimes discouraged in our way when the features of our environment do not measure not up to our own fancy and imagination. A mere sober, solid, thinking mind would obviate and defuse such fruitless notions, yet we are all tempted to entertain formidable ingratitude. It takes no brainpower to expose things we disdain, for Satan is certain to magnify and outline every unsatisfactory detail we encounter. We each may think ourselves into a deep cave, but we must thank ourselves out.

Fear of losing our health, wealth, reputation, and happiness is the biggest hindrance to securing it. To focus on our pain is to invite more. To be constantly analyzing our life to see if we are being fulfilled is a sure avenue to ingratitude. The world is constantly asking, "Are we having fun yet?" The answer is, "No". To these souls, life will never be adequate, and they must wander forth seeking the bigger fulfillment that the last one did not secure. It is the fear that we are not receiving our fair allotment in life that breeds discontentment. It is discontentment that produces more fear, and the downward spiral progresses. Such was the consternation of the soul who asked Christ to speak to his brother to divide the inheritance with him. This may be logical thinking, but it is not conducive to a sound and peaceable mind. This offended soul has no root in himself and will forever be wronged in some fashion and spend his days in search of a savior to come and fix the other party. “... neither fear ye their fear, nor be afraid. Sanctify the LORD of hosts himself; and let him be your fear, and let him be your dread.” (Isaiah 8:12, 13)

There is no earthly level of attainment or perfect environment that will promote a sound mind. It can only be secured through prayer, peace, and thankfulness. This may take some reprogramming of our minds to reach into the subconscious recesses, but we must soberly gird up the loins of our minds and exercise them if we ever hope to obtain “the grace that is to be brought unto you at the revelation of Jesus Christ;” (1 Peter 1:13)

“And the peace of God,
which passeth all understanding,
shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus.
Finally, brethren, whatsoever things are true,
whatsoever things are honest, whatsoever things are just,
whatsoever things are pure, whatsoever things are lovely,
whatsoever things are of good report;
if there be any virtue, and if there be any praise,
think on these things.

— Philippians 4:7, 8

De winter van 1882 deed zich voor in het kleine zuidelijke stadje Tuscumbia, Alabama. Een vrolijk, normaal tweejarig meisje werd hopeloos ziek met een vreemde koorts. De koorts kwam en ging, kwam en ging, en kwam weer terug. De huisarts vreesde dat het kind de ziekte niet zou overleven, maar het kind was sterk en op een dag vertrok de koorts uiteindelijk voorgoed. De volgende dag wuifde de moeder met haar hand langs het gezicht van haar dochter, maar het kind knipperde niet met haar ogen. Verdere pogingen leverden geen resultaat op en er brak een nieuwe dag aan voor het gezin met een blinde dochter.

Naarmate het kind weer kracht kreeg om te spelen, luidde de grote avondklok zijn toon voor allen in de buurt, maar Helen reageerde niet. Andere geluiden gaven hetzelfde resultaat en de familie Keller kwam tot de bittere realisatie dat het leven nooit meer hetzelfde zou zijn. De meesten van ons zullen misschien nooit de grimmige omstandigheden ervaren waarmee het gezin van Helen Keller werd geconfronteerd, maar ieder van ons zal zeker beproevingen doorstaan die specifiek door onze God voor ons zijn toegesneden.

De menselijke geest is een verbazingwekkend en ingewikkeld schepsel. Hoewel velen hebben geprobeerd haar te doorgronden, blijft haar werking voor de mens onbegrijpelijk. Het is geen geringe verwondering dat een deel van het scherpste inzicht in de gezondheid van de geest in Gods Woord wordt onthuld. “For God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind.” (2 Timothy 1:7)

Vrees is de dreigende tegenstander van een gezonde geest. Zij torent over de ziel en bespot de heilige met haar dreigende minachting. Vrees kan een zonnige wei veranderen in een eenzame woestenij. Zij kan een groot huwelijksfeest zo donker maken als een grot, en een banket dat voor een koning geschikt is veranderen in een misselijkmakende aangelegenheid. Het is het machtigste en meest verwoestende werktuig in de dienst van de duivel. Ondanks vele stoutmoedige beweringen is niemand vrijgesteld van haar invloed. “A dreadful sound is in his ears: in prosperity the destroyer shall come upon him. He believeth not that he shall return out of darkness, and he is waited for of the sword.” (Job 15:21, 22) Het is vrees die op het punt staat alle voorspoed van de ziel aan te vallen en te doven. Als wij haar in deze dagen willen weerstaan, moeten wij ons met alle ijver verheffen in uitdagende oorlogsvoering.

We hoeven niet ver te kijken om de ontwapening en verzwakking van de menselijke geest te aanschouwen. Medicatie voor de geest behoort tot de belangrijkste voorgeschreven middelen die tegenwoordig in Amerika worden gebruikt. Dit is geen gerichte beschuldiging aan het adres van individuen die mogelijk medische hulp nodig hebben om hun geest te beheersen. Maar het behoeft geen geleerde te zijn om naar obesitas te kijken en aan het dieet te denken, om opstandige tieners te zien en dat te koppelen aan de samenstelling van het gezin, of om te zien dat mensen hun hart (geest) faalt en te geloven dat vrees daaraan ten grondslag ligt. Hoewel sommigen hun dieet volledig meester kunnen zijn, kunnen weinigen zich volmaakte ouders noemen. Nog minder zijn degenen die niet, soms, door vrees worden aangevallen. Hoewel trots en verstand het uiterlijke gedrag kunnen temperen en iemand kalm kunnen laten lijken, moet de innerlijke mens, althans onderbewust, met de spanning omgaan. Amerikanen zijn dol op het motto, "No fear!" maar ons gebruik van medicatie vertelt een ander verhaal. Paulus claimde geen vrijstelling, want hij was “troubled on every side; without were fightings, within were fears.” (2 Corinthians 7:5)

Waar zijn we bang voor? Verlies, pijn en vernedering. Niemand houdt ervan iets te verliezen waarvoor we hebben gestreden om het te verkrijgen. Niemand geniet van pijn. Niemand houdt ervan vernederd te worden. Toch hoeven we niet ver in de Schrift te lezen om te beseffen dat dit vaak de wegen zijn die God gebruikt om Zijn dienstknechten verder aan te sporen op de weg naar Zijn gelijkenis. Er is geen verzekering op aarde die de levendigheid van de jeugd, de liefde van een gezin of het respect van vrienden kan veiligstellen. De dingen die ons de grootste voorhoede op aarde verschaffen, zijn allen kwetsbaar voor het risico van verlies. Daarom vrezen we. Hoewel we in bed liggen tot de dageraad, kunnen we op geen enkele wijze onze status vergroten of het verlies verlichten dat God op ons leven heeft gelegd. Deze angst vergroot alleen maar ons leed en voegt brandstof toe aan onze vrees.

“Be careful for nothing; but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God. And the peace of God, which passeth all understanding, shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus.” (Philippians 4:6 7) Hierin is het bewaren van onze harten en geesten: gebed, vrede en dankzegging.

Als een vakkundige ambachtsman moeten wij deze twee Schriftplaatsen zorgvuldig samenweven op het weefgetouw van het leven, want er lijkt een directe correlatie te bestaan tussen het vruchtbare — kracht, liefde en een gezonde geest — en het "wortelige" — gebed, vrede en dankbaarheid. Er zal geen overwinning op onze angsten zijn zonder deze dingen, en elke maatschappij die arm is aan deze bestanddelen zal zeker gehandicapt zijn.

Gebed baart kracht

In onze verzwakte toestand kunnen we gebed niet vatten zoals het behoort. Dan moeten we ons vertrouwen stellen op degenen die dat wel kunnen of misschien op de Geest, die voor ons smeekt met onuitsprekelijke verzuchtingen. Gemeenschap met het Almachtige Hoofd van het heelal is een buitengewoon stoutmoedige taak. Velen verrichten gebed slechts als een formele handeling en streven ernaar er volmaakt eerbiedig in te zijn. Dit is geen gemeenschap zoals met een vriend, noch is het stoutmoedig. Het valt meer onder de beschrijving van vrees. De remedie tegen vrees bestaat erin al onze angst, bitterheid en klacht over God uit te storten. De heiligen van vroeger waren erom bekend dat zij hun beschuldigingen en de bitterheid van hun ziel hartstochtelijk aan God uitstortten.

“Then Job answered and said, Even to day is my complaint bitter: my stroke is heavier than my groaning. Oh that I knew where I might find him! That I might come even to his seat! I would order my cause before him, and fill my mouth with arguments. I would know the words which he would answer me, and understand what he would say unto me. Will he plead against me with his great power? No; but he would put strength in me.” (Job 23:1-6)

  • David —“I poured out my complaint before him; I shewed before him my trouble.” (Psalm 142:2)
  • Hannah —“For out of the abundance of my complaint and grief have I spoken hitherto.” (1 Samuel 1:16)
  • Jeremiah —“He hath filled me with bitterness, he hath made me drunken with wormwood.”
    (Lamentations 3:15)
  • Naomi —“Call me Mara: for the Almighty hath dealt very bitterly with me.” (Ruth 1:20)
  • Hezekiah —“He will cut me off with pining sickness: from day even to night wilt thou make an end of me.” (Isaiah 38:12)
  • Jesus — “My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?” (Matthew 27:46)

Al deze personen spuwden moedige beschuldigingen en klachten jegens God uit in vurig gebed en geen van hen maakte Hem bezwaar. Integendeel, God had hun niet de geest van vrees gegeven, maar van kracht, en zij dienen ons als voorbeelden. Het was de ongelovige Achab aan wie werd gezegd dat hij van God een teken in de hemel of op aarde moest vragen. In zijn vrome antwoord weigerde hij God te "verleiden." Dit gebrek aan stoutmoedigheid en de overmaat aan vrees is voor God verleidelijker dan de overmaat aan bitterheid in onze klacht, want “there is no fear in love; but perfect love casteth out fear: because fear hath torment. He that feareth is not made perfect in love.” (1 John 4:18)

Vrede baart liefde

Wij zijn allen in rust met de dingen waar we van houden. "Great peace have they which love thy law: and nothing shall offend them.” (Psalm 119:165) Een fonkelend jong kind dat in vrede is met zijn vader, aanbidt die man en probeert hem na te bootsen. Door de tedere ogen van de jongen is het karakter van zijn vader onberispelijk. Zijn vaardigheid is onovertroffen. Zelfs het merk van het voertuig dat hij rijdt is het beste, en hij imiteert iedere handeling van hem. Hoewel elke vader de beperkingen van de verwachtingen van zijn zoon kent, genieten wij allemaal van de seizoensgebonden trouw. Het is kennis en vrees die deze trouwe liefde ondermijnen. Een gewelddadige vader zal dergelijke kinderlijk zelfbeeld vernietigen en vrees zal het vervangen. Het was door laffe vrees dat de boze dienaar zijn talent begroef en er niet mee handelde. In zijn ogen was zijn heer streng en om te vrezen. Maar God heeft ons niet de geest van vrees gegeven maar van liefde.

“We love him, because he first loved us. If a man say, I love God, and hateth his brother, he is a liar: for he that loveth not his brother whom he hath seen, how can he love God whom he hath not seen?” (1 John 4:19, 20) De ziel die door deze liefde wordt geraakt kan niet anders dan haar imiteren. Hij verkeert in grote vrede met de liefde van zijn Vader en de ogen waarmee hij het karakter van zijn Vader bekijkt zullen alleen maar tot navolging aansporen. Hoe guur de omstandigheden ook mogen zijn waarin wij ons bevinden, deze geest van liefde en vrede zal ons doordragen door welke tegenstand wij ook op het levenspad tegenkomen. Jakob deed niets met de zware dienst die hij voor Rachel moest verrichten; de geest van liefde tot God zal ons boven de vrees voor mensen stellen, en boven alle pijn die een mens ons kan aanrichten.

Dankbaarheid baart een gezonde geest

We hoeven gelukkige zielen niet lang te bestuderen om in de kern van ieder van hen een fundament van dankbaarheid te vinden. De geest van een gezonde geest, of de stilte van de geest, is een vreedzaam genieten van het leven. We raken vaak ontmoedigd wanneer de kenmerken van onze omgeving niet voldoen aan onze eigen voorkeuren en verbeelding. Een simpel nuchter, stevig denkend verstand zou zulke vruchteloze ideeën voorkomen en ontkrachten, toch worden we allemaal verzocht tot formidabele ondankbaarheid. Het vergt geen breinvermogen om de dingen bloot te leggen die we verachten, want Satan zal zeker elk onbevredigend detail vergroten en omlijnen dat we tegenkomen. Ieder van ons kan zichzelf in een diepe grot denken, maar we moeten onszelf er weer uit danken.

Vrees om onze gezondheid, rijkdom, reputatie en geluk te verliezen is het grootste beletsel om die te behouden. Zich op onze pijn concentreren nodigt meer uit. Onze levens voortdurend analyseren om te kijken of we vervuld worden, is een zekere weg naar ondankbaarheid. De wereld vraagt voortdurend: "Are we having fun yet?" Het antwoord is: "No". Voor deze zielen zal het leven nooit toereikend zijn, en zij moeten verder dwalen op zoek naar de grotere vervulling die de vorige niet heeft verzekerd. Het is de vrees dat wij niet ons billijke deel in het leven ontvangen die onvergenoegdheid doet groeien. Het is onvergenoegdheid die meer vrees voortbrengt, en de neerwaartse spiraal zet door. Zo was de verontwaardiging van de ziel die Christus vroeg tot zijn broeder te spreken om de erfenis met hem te delen. Dit kan logische overweging zijn, maar het is niet bevorderlijk voor een gezonde en vreedzame geest. Deze beledigde ziel heeft geen wortel in zichzelf en zal altijd op één of andere manier onrechtvaardig behandeld worden en zijn dagen besteden aan het zoeken naar een redder om te komen en de ander te herstellen. “... neither fear ye their fear, nor be afraid. Sanctify the LORD of hosts himself; and let him be your fear, and let him be your dread.” (Isaiah 8:12, 13)

Er is geen aards niveau van bereik of perfecte omgeving die een gezonde geest zal bevorderen. Zij kan alleen worden verkregen door gebed, vrede en dankbaarheid. Dit kan wat herprogrammering van onze geesten vergen om naar de onderbewuste afdelingen te reiken, maar wij moeten nuchterlijk de lendenen van ons verstand omgorden en ze oefenen als wij ooit hopen te verkrijgen “the grace that is to be brought unto you at the revelation of Jesus Christ;” (1 Peter 1:13)

“And the peace of God,
which passeth all understanding,
shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus.
Finally, brethren, whatsoever things are true,
whatsoever things are honest, whatsoever things are just,
whatsoever things are pure, whatsoever things are lovely,
whatsoever things are of good report;
if there be any virtue, and if there be any praise,
think on these things.

— Philippians 4:7, 8

Part 1

For Alice, life is exasperating. Each day feels like an endless grind. She loves her family, but in her heart, she questions if what she is working so hard to accomplish makes any difference at all. She didn’t always feel bogged down, and she wondered what changed to make her feel overwhelmed so much of the time.

Sometimes busyness increases so gradually that we barely recognize the change. Busyness, given the chance, will overload us with more obligations than we can realistically get done in one day, or one week, or even one lifetime. Then, without warning, we reach the overload point when we feel as though we cannot possibly handle any more. Relentless overload can cause physical and mental exhaustion to the point where we feel deprived of enthusiasm, energy, and purpose. Some women seem to have a built-in indicator of where the overload line is. Others, like myself, struggle to find that balance. Constantly. There are so many good, interesting, and exciting options right at our fingertips; without much thought, we fill our days.

Concepts that contribute to overload

Playing multiple roles can be stressful. Overloading yourself with responsibilities and commitments can make you forget what is most important. It is easy to equate busyness with self-worth. By default, we start believing that:

  • Homemakers are capable of handling everything.
  • Homemakers, especially godly homemakers, are never frustrated.
  • A homemaker should anticipate all her family’s needs.

If we are honest, we know that these statements are unrealistic. Homemakers cannot do everything. All homemakers experience frustration occasionally. A mother cannot consistently be one step ahead of her family’s needs.

Rethinking the busy life

Household duties and caring for our families fill our days. Sometimes those tasks alone make us extremely busy. But what about the extra-circular activities or the high standard we hold ourselves to? We may need to think differently so we can break free from habits that threaten to control us.

Accept your limits

Maybe you can go to a Tupperware party, attend a Bible study, and repaint the bathroom all in one week. But should you? Good homemakers allow themselves to simplify even if they prefer doing it another way. That means if you are an avid bread maker, it’s all right to toss a few loaves of bread into your shopping cart.

Evaluate what causes frustrations

Artificial smiles can hide inner frustrations, but it doesn’t cure them. It works best to admit that there is a problem and then seek a solution. I’ve had to learn this repeatedly. All my family members know that we eat dinner at 5:30. But a late arrival habit is trending, and it bothers me.

When I told my husband about the frustration, he simply said, “Why don’t you explain the issue and quit being so uptight about it?” Good point. Proactively seeking solutions works for many problem areas.

Imperfect women make good homemakers

Quit worrying about perfection and make decisions based on what is best for today. Fun-loving, happy, homemakers might have a few dust bunnies under the furniture, but they radiate an aura that draws people to their hearts and homes.

Everyone differs when it comes to how much we can handle. On the other hand, everyone is the same; we all have limits. In future installments, we will discuss how to deal with common points of overload.

Part 2

Many homemakers find themselves stretched thin among commitments that go with home, family, and other activities. As busy as we are, why do we continue to fill our schedules fuller?

It is easy for me to commit to a new project and then realize, halfway into the task, that I have overstepped my limits. Too often, I overestimate the amount of time I must have to complete a project and underestimate the amount of time a task will take.

Commitment overload happens by default. When we play multiple roles and add more responsibilities, we can easily become slaves to the promises we have made. Overload tends to drain our energy, dull our senses, and deaden our joy.

Recognizing Overload

Sometimes multiple activities take place in rapid sequence. Normally, we can flow with short-term spurts of busyness. But if the flow of activities is never-ending and we keep adding more obligations, we develop a pattern that becomes a way of life.

Too many commitments beyond normal duties make us candidates for depression and burnout. Personally, when I experience insomnia, apathy, or irritability, it is time to examine my schedule. If adjustments aren’t made, someone or something will suffer.

No one can overextend themselves indefinitely. Sometimes we suffer consequences for keeping a pace that is beyond our resources. Symptoms of overload can include lack of sleep, strained relationships, procrastination, fear of failure, and a susceptible immune system.

Breaking Free of Overload

Identifying overload takes an honest evaluation of yourself. How can you know if this is just a busy season or if busyness is the new normal? Are you declining a request because life is too full, or is it an excuse? Do you have to say “yes” on the spot? With practice, you can learn how to pull back before reaching the overload point.

Let an idea or request gel before committing

This has saved me a great deal of stress. There are so many good things to be involved in, and new inspirations come daily. Sometimes tasks can be incorporated into my/our schedule. Other times I must simply let them go and stay focused on what is most important. Consider waiting a few hours before incorporating new ideas and requests.

Seek advice, especially your husband’s

A renowned doughnut maker was asked to have a stand at an auction. She asked her husband what he thought about it. He said, “As long as you don’t complain and stress about it like you did last year, I don’t care.” Was her husband saying “yes” or “no”? This lady should take the cue that doughnut making was somehow adding stress. Either she should not do it, or together they must seek a workable solution.

Evaluate your schedule regularly

Keep a detailed calendar to have a picture of past, present, and future events. If your family had the flu last week and you plan to take an out-of-state trip next week, should you add more? What is the emotional health of your family? Is your husband stressed at work? Sometimes it is better to have a time slot of nothing so it can be filled with what is important now. You can’t do a good job at anything if you are spread too thin. Too many obligations make it hard to be personally refreshed and congenial. Choosing commitments wisely will help you invest your energy where it is most valuable for today.

Del 1

För Alice är livet irriterande. Varje dag känns som en ändlös röra. Hon älskar sin familj, men i sitt hjärta undrar hon om det hon arbetar så hårt för verkligen spelar någon roll. Hon kände sig inte alltid överväldigad, och hon undrar vad som förändrades så att hon känner sig överväldigad så ofta.

Ibland ökar upptagenheten så gradvis att vi knappt känner igen förändringen. Upptagenhet, om den ges chansen, kommer att överbelasta oss med fler åtaganden än vi realistiskt kan få gjort på en dag, eller en vecka, eller till och med en livstid. Sedan, utan varning, når vi brytpunkten då vi känner att vi omöjligen kan hantera mer. Ihållande överbelastning kan orsaka fysisk och mental utmattning till den grad att vi känner oss berövade entusiasm, energi och mening. Vissa kvinnor verkar ha en inbyggd indikator för var överbelastningslinjen går. Andra, som jag själv, kämpar ständigt för att hitta den balansen. Det finns så många bra, intressanta och spännande alternativ inom räckhåll; utan mycket eftertanke fyller vi våra dagar.

Föreställningar som bidrar till överbelastning

Att spela flera roller kan vara stressande. Att överbelasta sig själv med ansvar och åtaganden kan få dig att glömma vad som är viktigast. Det är lätt att likställa upptagenhet med självvärde. Som standard börjar vi tro att:

  • Hushållerskor kan klara allt.
  • Hushållerskor, särskilt gudfruktiga hushållerskor, är aldrig frustrerade.
  • En hushållerska bör förutse alla sin familjs behov.

Om vi är ärliga vet vi att dessa påståenden är orealistiska. Hushållerskor kan inte göra allt. Alla hushållerskor upplever ibland frustration. En mor kan inte konsekvent ligga steget före sin familjs behov.

Att ompröva det upptagna livet

Hushållssysslor och omvårdnad av våra familjer fyller våra dagar. Ibland gör de uppgifterna oss ensamma extremt upptagna. Men vad sägs om fritidsaktiviteterna eller den höga standard vi har för oss själva? Vi kan behöva tänka annorlunda för att kunna bryta oss loss från vanor som hotar att kontrollera oss.

Acceptera dina gränser

Kanske kan du gå på ett Tupperware-party, delta i en bibelstudie och måla om badrummet allt på en vecka. Men bör du det? Bra hushållerskor tillåter sig att förenkla även om de föredrar att göra det på ett annat sätt. Det betyder att om du är en ivrig brödbakare är det okej att slänga ner ett par limpor i din kundvagn.

Utvärdera vad som orsakar frustrationer

Artificiella leenden kan dölja inre frustrationer, men de botar dem inte. Det fungerar bäst att erkänna att det finns ett problem och sedan söka en lösning. Jag har fått lära mig detta upprepade gånger. Alla i min familj vet att vi äter middag klockan 17:30. Men en trend med sena ankomster har uppstått, och det stör mig.

När jag berättade för min man om frustrationen sa han helt enkelt: "Varför förklarar du inte problemet och slutar vara så nervös över det?" Bra poäng. Att proaktivt söka lösningar fungerar för många problemområden.

Ofullkomliga kvinnor blir goda hushållerskor

Sluta oroa dig för perfektion och fatta beslut utifrån vad som är bäst för idag. Lekfulla, glada hushållerskor kan ha några dammråttor under möblerna, men de utstrålar en aura som drar människor till deras hjärtan och hem.

Alla skiljer sig åt när det gäller hur mycket vi klarar av. Å andra sidan är vi alla lika; vi har alla gränser. I kommande avsnitt kommer vi att diskutera hur man hanterar vanliga överbelastningspunkter.

Del 2

Många hushållerskor finner sig dragna tunna mellan åtaganden som hör till hem, familj och andra aktiviteter. Så upptagna som vi är, varför fortsätter vi att fylla våra scheman ännu mer?

Det är lätt för mig att gå in i ett nytt projekt och sedan inse, halvvägs in i uppgiften, att jag har överskridit mina gränser. Alltför ofta överskattar jag den tid jag måste ha för att slutföra ett projekt och underskattar den tid en uppgift kommer att ta.

Överbelastning av åtaganden händer som standard. När vi spelar flera roller och lägger till fler ansvarsområden kan vi lätt bli slavar under de löften vi har gett. Överbelastning tenderar att tömma vår energi, dämpa våra sinnen och bedöva vår glädje.

Att känna igen överbelastning

Ibland äger flera aktiviteter rum i snabb följd. Normalt kan vi flyta med kortvariga perioder av upptagenhet. Men om flödet av aktiviteter aldrig tar slut och vi hela tiden lägger till fler åtaganden utvecklar vi ett mönster som blir en livsstil.

För många åtaganden utöver de vanliga plikterna gör oss till kandidater för depression och utbrändhet. Personligen, när jag upplever sömnlöshet, apati eller irritabilitet är det dags att granska mitt schema. Om ingen justering görs kommer någon eller något att lida.

Ingen kan sträcka ut sig för länge. Ibland får vi konsekvenser för att hålla ett tempo som överstiger våra resurser. Symptom på överbelastning kan inkludera sömnbrist, ansträngda relationer, prokrastinering, rädsla för misslyckande och ett mottagligt immunsystem.

Att bryta sig fri från överbelastning

Att identifiera överbelastning kräver en ärlig utvärdering av dig själv. Hur kan du veta om detta bara är en upptagen säsong eller om upptagenhet är det nya normala? Negr du tackar nej till en förfrågan för att livet är för fullt, eller är det en ursäkt? Måste du säga "ja" direkt? Med övning kan du lära dig att dra dig tillbaka innan du når överbelastningspunkten.

Låt en idé eller förfrågan mogna innan du åtar dig den

Detta har sparat mig mycket stress. Det finns så många bra saker att vara involverad i, och nya inspirationer kommer dagligen. Ibland kan uppgifter införlivas i mitt/ vårt schema. Andra gånger måste jag helt enkelt släppa dem och hålla fokus på det som är viktigast. Överväg att vänta några timmar innan du införlivar nya idéer och förfrågningar.

Sök råd, särskilt din mans

En berömd munkmakare blev tillfrågad om hon ville ha ett stånd på en auktion. Hon frågade sin man vad han tyckte om det. Han sa: "Så länge du inte klagar och stressar över det som du gjorde förra året bryr jag mig inte." Sa hennes man "ja" eller "nej"? Denna dam borde ta det som en fingervisning om att munkmakeri på något sätt lade till stress. Antingen borde hon låta bli att göra det, eller också måste de tillsammans söka en genomförbar lösning.

Utvärdera ditt schema regelbundet

Ha en detaljerad kalender för att få en bild av tidigare, nuvarande och framtida händelser. Om din familj hade influensa förra veckan och du planerar en resa utom delstaten nästa vecka, bör du lägga till mer? Hur är din familjs känslomässiga hälsa? Är din man stressad på jobbet? Ibland är det bättre att ha en tidslucka utan något så att den kan fyllas med vad som är viktigt nu. Du kan inte göra ett bra jobb med något om du är för utspridd. För många åtaganden gör det svårt att vara personligt uppfriskande och sällskaplig. Att välja åtaganden klokt hjälper dig att investera din energi där den är mest värdefull för idag.

A wonderful thing about being a Christian is anticipating the day when we feast our eyes on the magnificent beauty of our God. Quite likely, we have all created mental pictures of what we think God might look like, although we know that our wildest imaginations will be exceeded. “Thine eyes shall see the king in his beauty: they shall behold the land that is very far off” (Isaiah 33:17). The Bible is full of descriptive word pictures attempting to give us a brief glimpse into the realms of the heavenly. The landscape on the hills of glory, the wonderful creatures that dwell there, and most of all, the Supreme Being on the throne, all defy our human attempt to grasp and understand the beauty and glory of our God.

At times we admire beauty in a song, a work of art, a story, or even another person, but David describes the delight of gazing at the beauty of God. “One thing have I desired of the LORD, that will I seek after; that I may dwell in the house of the LORD all the days of my life, to behold the beauty of the LORD, and to inquire in his temple” (Psalm 27:4). God is beautiful because His excellence is attractive— His character is flawless. David experienced the pleasure that comes from knowing and experiencing God in all His fullness. How does God express His Beauty?

Through the Gospel

“In whom the god of this world hath blinded the minds of them which believe not, lest the light of the glorious gospel of Christ, who is the image of God, should shine unto them. For we preach not ourselves, but Christ Jesus the Lord; and ourselves your servants for Jesus' sake. For God, who commanded the light to shine out of darkness, hath shined in our hearts, to give the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ” (2 Corinthians 4:4-6). In the awfulness of the Passion of Christ, we find a profound and sober beauty— the beauty of a sacrifice made by a sinless Savior for undeserving humanity. Sometimes the most stirring kind of beauty is found in things we cannot fully comprehend.

There is beauty in weeping of Mary and the disciples around the cross that held the lifeless body of their beloved Master. But when dawn broke on resurrection morning, despair turned into hope and grief into joy.

We see a beautiful scene at the Mount of Olives forty days later as the same disciples wistfully gazed into the sky, watching as their risen Lord disappeared into the heavens. With great joy, they returned to Jerusalem, with the promise of His return burning in their hearts, to wait for the coming of the Holy Spirit.

Today we expectantly wait for the Son of God to appear from heaven with power and great glory to complete the work of salvation. Then will we look upon Him in all His splendor and beauty. “For now we see through a glass, darkly; but then face to face: now I know in part; but then shall I know even as also I am known” (1 Corinthians 13:12).

How should we, as God's image-bearers, reflect His beauty through the Gospel? God is an uncreated eternal being, and man was created in His image to reflect His glory and beauty. However, this beauty has been marred by sin and is no longer a worthy representation of God's character. But, there is redemption! Very little surpasses the beauty of a life that was once bruised and broken by sin but is now restored, redeemed, and made whole by the Gospel. “To appoint unto them that mourn in Zion, to give unto them beauty for ashes, the oil of joy for mourning, the garment of praise for the spirit of heaviness; that they might be called trees of righteousness, the planting of the LORD, that He might be glorified” (Isaiah 61:3). Atheists challenge the existence of God, scientists argue against Biblical creation, scholars question the inerrancy of scripture, but nobody can dispute the testimony of a redeemed life.

Through Creation

“The heavens declare the glory of God; and the firmament showeth His handy work” (Psalm 19:1). All beauty in the created world comes from God. A beautiful sunset, a lovely rose, a towering redwood, a majestic mountain peak, all testify of the beauty of God illustrated in creation. As road signs along the highway guide us to our destination, likewise, creation directs mankind to God himself. “For the invisible things of Him from the creation of the world are clearly seen . . .” (Romans 1:20). These gifts of creation are given to give us a brief glimpse of the One who created them.

How should we, as part of God's creation, reflect His creative beauty? Although we cannot make something out of nothing, God has designed us to be creative, using the resources of His creation and our intellectual abilities to make life practical. The fulfilling sense of accomplishment derived from a job well done has its origin in creation, where God regarded His work and declared it to be good. In our attempt to live non-extravagant lives we sometimes fail to take joy in the beautiful things in life. It is right and good and in harmony with how we were created to find pleasure in things of beauty. Ungodly men have used this gift of creativity many times for evil means. So much the more, let us glorify God by using His creation in ways that reflect His character.

A warning for all who love nature and creation (natural and man-made): let us be careful to not elevate earthly beauty above the Creator, which leads to idolatry. Sunsets fade, redwoods tumble, roses wilt, the human body turns to dust again, but God remains. Life and all of its beauty begins and ends with God.

Through Music and Sound

“And I heard a voice from heaven, as the voice of many waters, and as the voice of a great thunder: and I heard the voice of harpers harping with their harps” (Revelation 14:2) According to the book of Revelation, God's throne is surrounded by sound: thundering and lightning; praises flowing from the angels, the four beasts and twenty elders, and the great multitude which no man can number; and the new song by the one hundred and forty four thousand.

God created the beauty of sound to glorify Himself in ways that mere words cannot. The intricacy of His creativity is powerfully displayed in the way various sound frequencies come together to create a beautiful and heavenly harmony. It is honoring to God for mankind to take pleasure in the beauty of sounds He has created for His glory. The person who loves God will be drawn to Him whenever He is serenaded by pleasing sounds: the people of God singing the songs of Zion, the prayers of the saints, the wind whispering through the treetops, the songbird praising its Maker, the rumble of thunder, or the simple patter of rain on the roof.

How should we, as instruments of sound, reflect God's beauty through sound? We should always seek to listen to and resemble the sounds and harmonies of heaven. Although we will never be able to completely accomplish this on earth, it should be a lifelong endeavor. The questions have been asked,” Should we always be trying to improve our music making?” and “when have we reached ‘good enough’?” We will never be able to attain heavenly perfection, so the question should rather be asked, “Are we giving God the best we have?” Some people have more singing capabilities than others, but the question remains. “Are we giving our best or are we satisfied with an inferior sacrifice?” Let us be producers of God-honoring sounds that bring joy to the heart of the Creator!

Through the Church:

The Bible speaks extensively about the beauty of God's people. “Zion,” “The Temple,” “The Mountain of God,” “Jerusalem,” and“The Church” are synonymous expressions woven throughout scripture referring to the habitation of God's people on the earth. It is God's desire that His beauty would be reflected in the lives of His people. “Great is the LORD, and greatly to be praised in the city of our God, in the mountain of His holiness. Beautiful for situation, the joy of the whole earth, is Mount Zion, on the sides of the north, the city of the great King” (Psalm 48:1-2).

Nothing is dearer to the heart of God than His church. When the children of Israel journeyed through the wilderness, they built the tabernacle as a place for God to dwell among them. When Solomon dedicated the temple as God's dwelling place, God was very pleased and 2 Chronicles 7:1 says the glory of the Lord filled the temple. The temple was considered the House of the Lord–Jesus himself referred to it numerous times as God's house and was very passionate that it should be kept holy.

Today, neither the tabernacle nor the temple hosts the presence of God but rather His divine passion is concentrated on the church of Jesus Christ. Here are the people who truly love Him and are willing to lay down their lives for Him. Here are the people who are willing to give up their rights as individuals and surrender themselves to a greater cause. Here is where many a saint has given His very life's blood for the Gospel. And here is where one day our Savior will return as He has promised, and will transport His bride, the church, to her eternal habitation. “And I John saw the holy city, New Jerusalem, coming down from God out of heaven, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband. And I heard a great voice out of heaven saying, Behold, the tabernacle of God is with men, and he will dwell with them, and they shall be His people, and God Himself shall be with them, and be their God” (Revelation 21:2-3).

How should we, as God's people, reflect His beauty in the church? By dwelling together in unity and harmony with love for all men, especially the household of God. The church should be a place where the world can get a glimpse of what goes on in heaven. It should be a place where Christ is always elevated as the victorious conqueror of sin, death, and hell.

Sadly, many people have become disoriented with the church's failures and have walked away from the true apostolic faith. In spite of our disappointments, let us “lift up the hands which hang down and the feeble knees” (Hebrews 12:12) and let us press on. We will never have a higher calling, and never a more noble warfare to wage.

Lastly, how should we reflect His beauty in our lives? By delighting in Him. “Delight thyself also in the LORD; and He shall give thee the desires of thine heart” (Psalm 37:4). The greatest fulfillment in life comes from finding pleasure in bringing joy to the heart of God by delighting in what He delights in and loving what He loves. Let us never lose the wonder of the beauty of our Salvation!

דבר נפלא בלהיות נוצרי הוא הציפייה ליום שבו נשטח את עינינו מול היופי המרהיב של אלוהינו. רובנו כנראה יצרנו תמונות מנטליות של איך אנו חושבים שאלוהים עשוי להיראות, למרות שאנו יודעים שהדמיון הפרוע ביותר שלנו ייפרץ. “Thine eyes shall see the king in his beauty: they shall behold the land that is very far off” (Isaiah 33:17). התנ"ך מלא בתמונות מתיאור שמנסות לתת לנו מבט קצר אל ממלכות השמיים. הנוף על גבעות התהילה, היצורים הנפלאים השוהים שם, ומעל לכל, הישות העליונה על הכס—כל אלה מתמרדים בניסיון האנושי לתפוס ולהבין את היופי וההילה של אלוהינו.

Through the Gospel

“In whom the god of this world hath blinded the minds of them which believe not, lest the light of the glorious gospel of Christ, who is the image of God, should shine unto them. For we preach not ourselves, but Christ Jesus the Lord; and ourselves your servants for Jesus' sake. For God, who commanded the light to shine out of darkness, hath shined in our hearts, to give the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ” (2 Corinthians 4:4-6). בשקומת הסבל של היסורים המשיח, אנו מוצאים יופי עמוק ויאושני—יופי של קורבן שניתן על-ידי מושיע ללא חטא למען אנושות שאינה ראויה. לעיתים סוג היופי המעורר ביותר נמצא בדברים שאיננו יכולים להבינם במלואם.

יש יופי בבכי של מרים והתלמידים סביב הצלב שהחזיק את גופתו חסרת החיים של רבם האהוב. אבל כשהשחר פתח בבוקר התחייה, הייאוש הפך לתקווה והאבל לשמחה.

אנו רואים סצנה יפה בהר הזיתים ארבעים יום לאחר מכן כאשר אותם תלמידים הביטו במבט מלא געגוע לשמיים וצפו באדונם הקם נעלם אל השמים. בשמחה גדולה הם שבו לירושלים, עם הבטחת שובו בוערת בלבם, להמתין לבוא רוח הקודש.

היום אנו מצפים בציפייה לבן האלוהים להופיע מהשמים בעוצמה ובחדווה רבה כדי להשלים את מעשה הישועה. אז נביט בו בכל זוהרו ויופיו. “For now we see through a glass, darkly; but then face to face: now I know in part; but then shall I know even as also I am known” (1 Corinthians 13:12).

כיצד עלינו, כנושאי דמות האלוהים, לשקף את יופיו דרך הבשורה? אלוהים הוא ישות נצחית שלא נבראה, והאדם נברא בצלמו כדי לשקף את הודו ויופיו. עם זאת, יופי זה הושחת על-ידי החטא וכבר אינו ייצוג ראוי של אופיו של אלוהים. אך יש גאולה! מעט מאוד עובר על היופי של חיים שפעם נדרסו ונשברו על-ידי החטא אך כעת שוחזרו, נגאלו והושלמו על-ידי הבשורה. “To appoint unto them that mourn in Zion, to give unto them beauty for ashes, the oil of joy for mourning, the garment of praise for the spirit of heaviness; that they might be called trees of righteousness, the planting of the LORD, that He might be glorified” (Isaiah 61:3). אתאיסטים מערערים על קיום אלוהים, מדענים מתווכחים נגד הבריאה המקראית, מלומדים מטילים ספק באי-טעויות של הכתובים, אך איש אינו יכול להתווכח עם העדות של חיים נגאלים.

Through Creation

“The heavens declare the glory of God; and the firmament showeth His handy work” (Psalm 19:1). כל היופי שבעולם הבריאה בא מאלוהים. שקיעה יפה, ורד יפה, סקוויה גבוהת קומה, פסגת הר מרהיבה—כל אלה מעידים על יופיו של אלוהים המתואר בבריאה. כמו שלטי דרך על הכביש שמנחים אותנו ליעדנו, כך הבריאה מכוונת את האדם אל האל עצמו. “For the invisible things of Him from the creation of the world are clearly seen . . .” (Romans 1:20). מתנות הבריאה ניתנו כדי להעניק לנו מבט קצר על האחד שבראם.

כיצד עלינו, כחלק מבריאת אלוהים, לשקף את יופיו הבריאתי? אף שאיננו יכולים ליצור משהו מאין, אלוהים תכנן אותנו להיות יצירתיים, להשתמש במשאבי בריאתו וביכולות השכליות שלנו כדי להפוך את החיים לפרקטיים. התחושה הממלאת של הישג שנובעת מעבודה שבוצעה היטב מקוריה בבריאה, שם אלוהים הביט בעבודתו והכריזה שהיא טובה. בניסיון שלנו לחיות חיים פשוטים לפעמים נכשלנו בשמחתנו בדברים יפים בחיים. נכון וטוב ובהרמוניה עם הדרך שבה נבראנו למצוא הנאה בדברים יפים. אנשים רשעים ניצלו פעמים רבות את מתנת היצירתיות הזאת למטרות רעות. לכן, כל כך יותר נפאר את אלוהים על-ידי שימוש בבריאתו בדרכים המשקפות את אופיו.

אזהרה לכל אוהבי הטבע והבריאה (טבעית ובנויה על ידי אדם): נזהר לא להעלות את היופי הארצי מעל היוצר, כי זה מוביל לעבודת אלילים. שקיעות דועכות, סקוויות נופלות, ורדים נובלים, הגוף האנושי חוזר לעפר שוב, אבל אלוהים נשאר. החיים וכל יופיים מתחילים ומסתיימים עם אלוהים.

Through Music and Sound

“And I heard a voice from heaven, as the voice of many waters, and as the voice of a great thunder: and I heard the voice of harpers harping with their harps” (Revelation 14:2) על-פי ספר ההתגלות, כסא האלוהים מוקף בקול: רעם וברקים; שבחים הזורמים מהמלאכים, מהחיות הארבע ומזקני העשרים, ומהרבבות הרבים שאיש אינו יכול לספור; והשיר החדש על-ידי המאה ארבעים וארבע אלף.

אלוהים ברא את יופי הקול כדי להאדיר עצמו בדרכים שמילים בלבד אינן יכולות. המורכבות של יצירתו מופיעה בעוצמה באופן שבו תדירויות שונות של קול מתמזגות ליצירת הרמוניה יפה ושמימית. זה מכבד את אלוהים שאנושות תמצא הנאה ביופי הצלילים שהוא ברא לכבודו. האדם שאוהב את אלוהים יימשך אליו כאשר הוא מלווה בצלילים נעימים: עם ישראל ששרים את שירי ציון, תפילות הקדושים, רוח הלוחשת בין עלוות העצים, ציפור השיר מהללת את בוראה, רעם המתגלגל, או נקישות הגשם הפשוטות על הגג.

כיצד עלינו, ככלי-קול, לשקף את יופיו של אלוהים באמצעות הקול? עלינו תמיד לחפש להאזין ולהידמות לצלילים ולהרמוניות של השמים. אף כי לעולם לא נוכל להשיג זאת באופן שלם על הארץ, זה צריך להיות מאמץ לכל החיים. נשאלו השאלות: "האם עלינו תמיד לשאוף לשפר את עשיית המוזיקה שלנו?" ו"מתי הגענו ל'טוב מספיק'?" לעולם לא נגיע לשלמות שמימית, לכן השאלה צריכה להיות אחרת: "האם אנו נותנים לאלוהים את הטוב ביותר שיש לנו?" יש אנשים שיש להם יכולות שירה גדולות יותר מאחרים, אך השאלה נשארת. "האם אנו נותנים את המיטב שלנו או מרוצים עם קורבן חסר ערך?" נהיה יצרנים של צלילים המפארים את אלוהים ומביאים שמחה ללבו של הבורא!

Through the Church:

התנ"ך מדבר בהרחבה על יופיים של עם אלוהים. "ציון", "היכל", "הר-האל" , "ירושלים" ו"הכנסייה" הן ביטויים סימולטניים השזורים בכתובים ומתייחסים למגוריהם של עם אלוהים על הארץ. רצון האל הוא שיופיו ישתקף בחיי עמו. “Great is the LORD, and greatly to be praised in the city of our God, in the mountain of His holiness. Beautiful for situation, the joy of the whole earth, is Mount Zion, on the sides of the north, the city of the great King” (Psalm 48:1-2).

אין דבר יקר יותר ללבה של אלוהים מאשר כנסייתו. כאשר בני ישראל נסעו במדבר, הם בנו את המשכן כמקום שאלוהים ישכון בתוכם. כאשר שלמה הקדיש את המקדש כמקום משכן לאלוהים, האל שמח מאד ו2 Chronicles 7:1 אומר שכבוד ה' מלא את המקדש. המקדש נחשב לבית ה'—ישוע עצמו התייחס אליו פעמים רבות כבית אלוהים והיה נלהב שישמר קדושתו.

היום, לא המשכן ולא המקדש מארחים את נוכחות האל במובן הזה, אלא תשוקתו האלוהית מרוכזת בכנסיית ישוע המשיח. כאן נמצאים האנשים שאוהבים אותו באמת ומוכנים להקריב את חייהם בשבילו. כאן נמצאים האנשים שמוכנים לוותר על זכויותיהם כאינדיבידואלים ולהתמסר למטרה עליונה. כאן רבים מהקדושים הנתינו מדם חייהם למען הבשורה. וכאן יום אחד ישוב מושיענו כפי שהבטיח, ויוביל את כלתו—הכנסייה—למושב הנצחי שלה. “And I John saw the holy city, New Jerusalem, coming down from God out of heaven, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband. And I heard a great voice out of heaven saying, Behold, the tabernacle of God is with men, and he will dwell with them, and they shall be His people, and God Himself shall be with them, and be their God” (Revelation 21:2-3).

כיצד עלינו, כעם האלוהים, לשקף את יופיו בכנסייה? על-ידי שכינה יחד באחדות ובהרמוניה ובאהבה לכל אדם, ובעיקר למשפחת אלוהים. הכנסייה צריכה להיות מקום שבו העולם יכול לקבל הצצה למה שמתרחש בשמיים. היא צריכה להיות מקום שבו המשיח תמיד מוחשב כמנצח השולט על החטא, המוות והשאול.

לצערנו, אנשים רבים תססו בגלל כישלונות הכנסייה והתרחקו מהאמונה האפוסטולית האמתית. על אף אכזבותינו, נְרומם את הידים הנופלות ואת הברכיים המעֵתות” (Hebrews 12:12) ונמשיך הלאה. לעולם לא תהיה לנו קריאה נעלה יותר, ולעולם לא מלחמה אצילית יותר לנהל.

ולבסוף, כיצד נשקף את יופיו בחיינו? על-ידי מציאת עונג בו. “Delight thyself also in the LORD; and He shall give thee the desires of thine heart” (Psalm 37:4). הסיפוק הגדול ביותר בחיים מגיע ממציאת הנאה בכך שאנו מביאים שמחה ללבו של אלוהים על-ידי להנאות במה שהוא נהנה ואהבת מה שהוא אוהב. אל נא נאבד לעולם את הפלא של יופי הישועה שלנו!
