Msimu wa baridi wa mwaka 1882 ulitokea katika mji mdogo wa kusini wa Tuscumbia, Alabama. Msichana mwenye umri wa miaka miwili aliyefurahi na wa kawaida aliugua vibaya kwa homa isiyoeleweka. Homa ilikuja na kuondoka, ikaja na kuondoka, halafu ikarudi tena. Daktari wa familia alihofu mtoto atakufa kwa msongo, lakini mtoto alikuwa imara na siku moja homa hatimaye iliondoka kwa muda wote. Siku iliyofuata, mama akapiga mkono mbele ya uso wa binti yake, lakini mtoto hakutega. Majaribio ya baadaye hayakazaa matunda na siku mpya ikamwagika kwa familia hiyo na binti aliyekuwa kipofu.

Wakati mtoto alipokuwa akipata nguvu za kurudi kucheza, kengele kubwa ya chambeili ililia kwa sauti kwa wote waliomzunguka, lakini Helen hakajibu. Visingizio vingine vilitoa matokeo yanayofanana na familia ya Keller ikaelewa kwa ukali kuwa maisha hayatawahi kuwa yale yale tena. Sisi wengi hatutakumbana na hali za kusikitisha ambazo familia ya Helen Keller ilikumbana nazo, lakini kila mmoja wetu bila shaka atavumilia magumu yaliyotengenezwa haswa na Mungu wetu.

Kiarushi cha mwanadamu ni uumbaji wa kutisha na wa kipekee. Ingawa wengi wamejitahidi kuelewa, uwezo wake wa uendeshaji unabaki kuwa jambo gumu kwa binadamu kuelewa. Si jambo la kushangaza kwamba sehemu ya ufahamu makini juu ya afya ya akili inafunuliwa katika Neno la Mungu. “For God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind.” (2 Timothy 1:7)

Hofu ni adui wa kutisha kwa akili yenye utulivu. Inatinga juu ya nafsi na kumsumbua mtumishi kwa matusi yake ya hatari. Hofu inaweza kuchukua tambarare yenye mwangaza na kuibadilisha kuwa jangwani peke yake. Inaweza kuifanya sherehe kubwa ya ndoa kuwa giza kama pango, na kugeuza karamu inayofaa mfalme kuwa sherehe ya kutapika. Ni zana yenye nguvu zaidi na yenye uharibifu katika ajira ya Ibilisi. Licha ya madai mengi ya ujasiri, hakuna mtu asiyeathirika na utumizi wake. “A dreadful sound is in his ears: in prosperity the destroyer shall come upon him. He believeth not that he shall return out of darkness, and he is waited for of the sword.” (Job 15:21, 22) Ni hofu inayosimama kushambulia na kuzima ustawi wote wa roho. Ikiwa tutaihimili katika siku hizi, lazima tusimame kwa bidii yote katika vita ya kukataa.

Hatuhitaji kuangalia mbali sana kuona uharibifu na udhaifu wa akili ya mtu. Dawa za akili ni miongoni mwa maagizo yanayotumiwa kwa wingi nchini Amerika leo. Hii si lawama maalum kwa watu wengine wanaoweza kuhitaji msaada wa matibabu kudhibiti akili zao. Lakini haichukui mshairi kuangalia unene wa mwili na kutafakari kuhusu lishe, kuona vijana wenye tabia ya kukataliwa na kuunganisha hilo na muundo wa nyumba, au kuona mioyo ya wanaume (m akili) ikiwashindwa nao kuamini kwamba hofu ndiyo mzizi. Wakati baadhi wanaweza kumiliki kabisa mlo wao, wachache wanaweza kudai kuwa wazazi waliokomaa. Wengine wachache tena ni wale ambao mara kwa mara hawakumbani na hofu. Ingawa kiburi na fahamu vinaweza kumuweka mtu wa nje kwa utaratibu, na kubaki kimya kabisa, mtu wa ndani, angalau kwa kiwango cha chini cha fahamu, lazima atatue na msongo. Wamarekani wanapenda kudai kaulimbiu, "No fear!" lakini matumizi yetu ya dawa yanaeleza hadithi tofauti. Paulo hakudai kuachwa mkononi, kwa kuwa alikuwa “troubled on every side; without were fightings, within were fears.” (2 Corinthians 7:5)

Tunamuogopa nini? Kupoteza, maumivu, na aibu. Hakuna mtu anayependa kupoteza kitu ambacho tumepigania kupata. Hakuna mtu anayefurahia maumivu. Hakuna mtu anayependa kuonewa aibu. Hata hivyo, hatuhitaji kusoma mbali katika Maandiko ili kutambua kuwa hizi mara nyingi ni njia ambazo Mungu hutumia kuwatia watumishi wake kwa njia ya zaidi ya kuwa katika sura Yake. Hakuna bima duniani inaweza kuimarisha uhai wa ujana, upendo wa familia, au heshima ya marafiki. Vitu vinavyotupatia kinga kuu ya dunia vyote vinaweza kupatwa na hatari za kupoteza. Kwa hiyo, tunaiogopa. Ingawa tulala kitandani hadi alfajiri, hatuwezi kwa namna yoyote kuongeza hadhi yetu wala kupunguza hasara ambayo Mungu ameweka kwa maisha yetu. Wasiwasi huu huwaongeza tu huzuni yetu na kuongeza mafuta kwa hofu zetu.

“Be careful for nothing; but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God. And the peace of God, which passeth all understanding, shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus.” (Philippians 4:6 7) Hapa ndiko kunakopita kulindwa kwa mioyo na akili zetu: sala, amani, na shukrani.

Kama msanii mwenye ujuzi lazima tukae tuwekeleze kwa umakini mistari hii miwili ya maandiko kwenye ganda la maisha kwa kuwa kuna uhusiano wa moja kwa moja kati ya matokeo yenye tija - nguvu, upendo na akili iliyo imara, kwa "mzizi wenye": sala, amani, na shukrani. Hakutakuwa na kushinda kwa hofu zetu bila vitu hivi, na kila jamii isiyokuwa na virutubisho hivi bila shaka itapata kizuizi.

Sala Husababisha Nguvu

Roho, ambayo anatusihi kwa kilio ambacho hakiwezi kusema. Kuwasiliana na Kichwa Mwenye Nguvu wa ulimwengu ni jukumu la ujasiri sana. Wengi watafanya sala kama kazi ya kifani tu, wakitafuta kuwa watukufu kabisa katika hilo. Hii si kuwasiliana kama na rafiki, wala si ujasiri. Ni zaidi inafaa kuangukia chini ya maelezo ya hofu. Tiba ya kuondoa hofu ni kumwaga wasi wasi wote wetu, ubinafsi, na kero kwa Mungu wetu. Watakatifu wa zamani walijulikana kumwaga kwa ghadhabu mashambulizi yao na uchungu wa nafsi yao kwa Mungu.

“Then Job answered and said, Even to day is my complaint bitter: my stroke is heavier than my groaning. Oh that I knew where I might find him! That I might come even to his seat! I would order my cause before him, and fill my mouth with arguments. I would know the words which he would answer me, and understand what he would say unto me. Will he plead against me with his great power? No; but he would put strength in me.” (Job 23:1-6)

  • David —“I poured out my complaint before him; I shewed before him my trouble.” (Psalm 142:2)
  • Hannah —“For out of the abundance of my complaint and grief have I spoken hitherto.” (1 Samuel 1:16)
  • Jeremiah —“He hath filled me with bitterness, he hath made me drunken with wormwood.”
    (Lamentations 3:15)
  • Naomi —“Call me Mara: for the Almighty hath dealt very bitterly with me.” (Ruth 1:20)
  • Hezekiah —“He will cut me off with pining sickness: from day even to night wilt thou make an end of me.” (Isaiah 38:12)
  • Jesus — “My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?” (Matthew 27:46)

Wote hawa walitamka mashambulizi makali na malalamiko dhidi ya Mungu kwa sala yenye ari na hakuna kati yao aliyemkosea. Kinyume chake, Mungu hakuwa amewapa roho ya hofu bali ya nguvu, na wao wanatufanya kuwa mifano yetu. Ndiyo Ahabu asiye na imani aliyetakiwa kuomba kwa Mungu ishara mbinguni au ardhini. Katika jibu lake la upietaji alikataa "kumjaribu" Mungu. Ukosefu huu wa ujasiri na wingi wa hofu ni jambo la kumjaribu Mungu zaidi kuliko wingi wa uchungu katika malalamiko yetu kwa kuwa “there is no fear in love; but perfect love casteth out fear: because fear hath torment. He that feareth is not made perfect in love.” (1 John 4:18)

Amani Husababisha Upendo

Sisi sote tuko kwenye utulivu na vitu tunavyovipenda. "Great peace have they which love thy law: and nothing shall offend them.” (Psalm 119:165) Mtoto mchanga mwenye kung'aa ambaye yuko na amani na baba yake anamheshimu mtu huyo na kujitahidi kumigwa. Kupitia macho ya mvulana mwenye upole, tabia ya baba yake haina mende. Ujuzi wake hauwezi kulinganishwa. Hata chapa ya gari analoendesha ni bora zaidi, na anakigafulia kila kitendo chake. Ingawa kila baba anajua mipaka ya matarajio ya mwanawe, sote tunafurahia uaminifu wa msimu. Ni maarifa na hofu zinazoathiri upendo huu wa uaminifu. Baba mwendawazimu ataangamiza heshima ya utoto kama hiyo na hofu itakuwa badala yake. Ilikuwa kwa hofu ya chini kwamba mtumishi mwovu akafuta talanta yake na hakuwekeza nayo. Kwa macho yake bwana wake alikuwa mkali na wa kutishwa. Lakini Mungu hatuwabidhi roho ya hofu bali ya upendo.

“We love him, because he first loved us. If a man say, I love God, and hateth his brother, he is a liar: for he that loveth not his brother whom he hath seen, how can he love God whom he hath not seen?” (1 John 4:19, 20) Roho iliyoguswa na upendo huu haiwezi ila kuiga. Yuko na amani kubwa na upendo wa Baba yake na macho ambayo yanamwangalia tabia ya Baba yake hayawezi kuleta chochote ila kuiga. Haijalishi hali mbaya tunakokutana nayo, roho hii ya upendo na amani itatuletea nguvu kupitia upinzani wowote tunaoweza kukutana naye katika njia ya maisha. Yakobo hakujali huduma ngumu aliyoilazimika kuvumilia kwa rachel; roho ya upendo kwa Mungu itatutoa juu ya hofu ya binadamu, na maumivu yote ambayo mtu anaweza kutufanyia.

Shukrani Husababisha Akili Ilio Tulivu

Hatuhitaji kusoma roho zenye furaha kwa muda mrefu ili kupata ndani ya msingi wa kila moja, msingi wa shukrani. Roho ya akili iliyo imara, au utulivu wa akili, ni kufurahia maisha kwa utulivu. Mara nyingi tunakatishwa tamaa tunapokutana na mazingira ambayo hayakidhi kila kiasi cha ladha na mawazo yetu. Akili tulivu na thabiti itazuia na kupuuzia mawazo yasiyo na tija, lakini sote tunatendewa kumfikiria chuki isiyoweza kushindwa. Haichukui ujuzi mkubwa kufichua vitu tunavyokichukia, kwa kuwa Ibilisi hakosei kupanua na kuonyesha kila undani usioridhisha tunoupata. Kila mmoja wetu anaweza kufikiri kuwa ndani ya pango kubwa, lakini lazima tujihifadhi kwa shukrani.

Hofu ya kupoteza afya yetu, utajiri, sifa, na furaha ni kizuizi kikubwa cha kuikimu. Kutilia maanani maumivu yetu ni kualika zaidi. Kuwa kila mara ukichambua maisha yetu kuona kama tunaridhika ni njia nzuri ya kukosewa shukrani. Dunia kila mara inajiuliza, "Are we having fun yet?" Jibu ni, "No". Kwa roho hizi, maisha hayatakuwa kamwe ya kutosha, na watatakiwa kuendelea kutafuta kuridhika kubwa zaidi ambacho kile kilichopita hakikutafuta. Ni hofu kwamba hatupati sehemu yetu ya haki maishani ndiyo inayozalisha kutoridhika. Kutoridhika ndiko kunazalisha hofu zaidi, na mzunguko wa kushuka unaendelea. Hivyo ndivyo hasira ya nafsi ilivyomuuliza Kristo aongee kwa ndugu yake agawanye urithi pamoja naye. Hii inaweza kuwa fikira ya mantiki, lakini si ya manufaa kwa akili tulivu na ya amani. Nafsi iliyosumbuliwa hakoni mzizi ndani yake na daima atakuwa amedhalilishwa kwa namna fulani na ataendelea kumtafuta mwokozi atokee aje na kumrekebisha mtu mwingine. “... neither fear ye their fear, nor be afraid. Sanctify the LORD of hosts himself; and let him be your fear, and let him be your dread.” (Isaiah 8:12, 13)

Hakuna kiwango cha mafanikio au mazingira kamili ya kidunia yatakayokuza akili iliyo imara. Inaweza tu kupatikana kupitia sala, amani, na shukrani. Hii inaweza kuhitaji upangaji upya wa akili zetu kufikia nafddari za chini za fahamu, lakini lazima tukae kwa makini tukajishikilia nguo za fikra zetu na kuzifanya kazi ikiwa tunatarajia kupata “the grace that is to be brought unto you at the revelation of Jesus Christ;” (1 Peter 1:13)

Part 1

For Alice, life is exasperating. Each day feels like an endless grind. She loves her family, but in her heart, she questions if what she is working so hard to accomplish makes any difference at all. She didn’t always feel bogged down, and she wondered what changed to make her feel overwhelmed so much of the time.

Sometimes busyness increases so gradually that we barely recognize the change. Busyness, given the chance, will overload us with more obligations than we can realistically get done in one day, or one week, or even one lifetime. Then, without warning, we reach the overload point when we feel as though we cannot possibly handle any more. Relentless overload can cause physical and mental exhaustion to the point where we feel deprived of enthusiasm, energy, and purpose. Some women seem to have a built-in indicator of where the overload line is. Others, like myself, struggle to find that balance. Constantly. There are so many good, interesting, and exciting options right at our fingertips; without much thought, we fill our days.

Concepts that contribute to overload

Playing multiple roles can be stressful. Overloading yourself with responsibilities and commitments can make you forget what is most important. It is easy to equate busyness with self-worth. By default, we start believing that:

  • Homemakers are capable of handling everything.
  • Homemakers, especially godly homemakers, are never frustrated.
  • A homemaker should anticipate all her family’s needs.

If we are honest, we know that these statements are unrealistic. Homemakers cannot do everything. All homemakers experience frustration occasionally. A mother cannot consistently be one step ahead of her family’s needs.

Rethinking the busy life

Household duties and caring for our families fill our days. Sometimes those tasks alone make us extremely busy. But what about the extra-circular activities or the high standard we hold ourselves to? We may need to think differently so we can break free from habits that threaten to control us.

Accept your limits

Maybe you can go to a Tupperware party, attend a Bible study, and repaint the bathroom all in one week. But should you? Good homemakers allow themselves to simplify even if they prefer doing it another way. That means if you are an avid bread maker, it’s all right to toss a few loaves of bread into your shopping cart.

Evaluate what causes frustrations

Artificial smiles can hide inner frustrations, but it doesn’t cure them. It works best to admit that there is a problem and then seek a solution. I’ve had to learn this repeatedly. All my family members know that we eat dinner at 5:30. But a late arrival habit is trending, and it bothers me.

When I told my husband about the frustration, he simply said, “Why don’t you explain the issue and quit being so uptight about it?” Good point. Proactively seeking solutions works for many problem areas.

Imperfect women make good homemakers

Quit worrying about perfection and make decisions based on what is best for today. Fun-loving, happy, homemakers might have a few dust bunnies under the furniture, but they radiate an aura that draws people to their hearts and homes.

Everyone differs when it comes to how much we can handle. On the other hand, everyone is the same; we all have limits. In future installments, we will discuss how to deal with common points of overload.

Part 2

Many homemakers find themselves stretched thin among commitments that go with home, family, and other activities. As busy as we are, why do we continue to fill our schedules fuller?

It is easy for me to commit to a new project and then realize, halfway into the task, that I have overstepped my limits. Too often, I overestimate the amount of time I must have to complete a project and underestimate the amount of time a task will take.

Commitment overload happens by default. When we play multiple roles and add more responsibilities, we can easily become slaves to the promises we have made. Overload tends to drain our energy, dull our senses, and deaden our joy.

Recognizing Overload

Sometimes multiple activities take place in rapid sequence. Normally, we can flow with short-term spurts of busyness. But if the flow of activities is never-ending and we keep adding more obligations, we develop a pattern that becomes a way of life.

Too many commitments beyond normal duties make us candidates for depression and burnout. Personally, when I experience insomnia, apathy, or irritability, it is time to examine my schedule. If adjustments aren’t made, someone or something will suffer.

No one can overextend themselves indefinitely. Sometimes we suffer consequences for keeping a pace that is beyond our resources. Symptoms of overload can include lack of sleep, strained relationships, procrastination, fear of failure, and a susceptible immune system.

Breaking Free of Overload

Identifying overload takes an honest evaluation of yourself. How can you know if this is just a busy season or if busyness is the new normal? Are you declining a request because life is too full, or is it an excuse? Do you have to say “yes” on the spot? With practice, you can learn how to pull back before reaching the overload point.

Let an idea or request gel before committing

This has saved me a great deal of stress. There are so many good things to be involved in, and new inspirations come daily. Sometimes tasks can be incorporated into my/our schedule. Other times I must simply let them go and stay focused on what is most important. Consider waiting a few hours before incorporating new ideas and requests.

Seek advice, especially your husband’s

A renowned doughnut maker was asked to have a stand at an auction. She asked her husband what he thought about it. He said, “As long as you don’t complain and stress about it like you did last year, I don’t care.” Was her husband saying “yes” or “no”? This lady should take the cue that doughnut making was somehow adding stress. Either she should not do it, or together they must seek a workable solution.

Evaluate your schedule regularly

Keep a detailed calendar to have a picture of past, present, and future events. If your family had the flu last week and you plan to take an out-of-state trip next week, should you add more? What is the emotional health of your family? Is your husband stressed at work? Sometimes it is better to have a time slot of nothing so it can be filled with what is important now. You can’t do a good job at anything if you are spread too thin. Too many obligations make it hard to be personally refreshed and congenial. Choosing commitments wisely will help you invest your energy where it is most valuable for today.

حصہ 1

ایلِس کے لیے زندگی پریشان کن ہے۔ ہر دن طویل دباؤ کی طرح محسوس ہوتا ہے۔ وہ اپنے خاندان سے محبت کرتی ہے، مگر اپنے دل میں سوال اٹھاتی ہے کہ جو وہ اتنی محنت سے حاصل کرنے کی کوشش کر رہی ہے، کیا اس کا کوئی فرق پڑتا ہے۔ وہ ہمیشہ بوجھل محسوس کرتی نہیں تھی، اور وہ سوچتی تھی کہ آخر کیا تبدیل ہوا جس کی وجہ سے وہ زیادہ تر وقت مغلوب محسوس کرتی ہے۔

کبھی کبھی مصروفیت اس قدر بتدریج بڑھتی ہے کہ ہم تغیر کو بمشکل پہچان پاتے ہیں۔ اگر موقع ملے تو مصروفیت ہمیں ایسی ذمہ داریوں سے بھر دے گی جو ہم حقیقتاً ایک دن، ایک ہفتہ، یا حتیٰ کہ ایک پوری زندگی میں بھی مکمل نہیں کر سکتے۔ پھر، بغیر کسی انتباہ کے، ہم اس حدِ برداشت تک پہنچ جاتے ہیں جہاں ہمیں محسوس ہوتا ہے کہ اب مزید کچھ سنبھالنا ممکن نہیں۔ لگاتار زیادہ بوجھ جسمانی اور ذہنی تھکن پیدا کر سکتا ہے یہاں تک کہ ہم جوش، توانائی، اور مقصد سے محروم محسوس کریں۔ بعض خواتین میں یہ حدِ برداشت ایک اندرونی نشان کی صورت میں ہوتی ہے۔ دوسرے، جیسے میں خود، توازن تلاش کرنے میں جدوجہد کرتے ہیں۔ مسلسل۔ ہماری پہنچ میں بہت سی اچھی، دلچسپ اور پرکشش اختیارات ہیں؛ بغیر زیادہ سوچے ہم اپنے دن بھر دیتے ہیں۔

وہ تصورات جو بوجھ میں اضافہ کرتے ہیں

متعدد کردار ادا کرنا تناؤ زدہ ہو سکتا ہے۔ اپنے آپ کو ذمہ داریوں اور وعدوں سے اوورلوڈ کر لینے سے آپ وہ چیزیں بھول سکتی ہیں جو سب سے زیادہ اہم ہیں۔ یہ آسان ہے کہ مصروفیت کو خود قدر کے ساتھ برابر سمجھ لیں۔ بطورِ پیش فرض ہم یہ ماننا شروع کر دیتے ہیں کہ:

  • گھر سنبھالنے والے ہر چیز کو سنبھالنے کے قابل ہوتے ہیں۔
  • گھر سنبھالنے والے، خاص طور پر دین دار گھر سنبھالنے والے، کبھی مایوس نہیں ہوتے۔
  • ایک گھر سنبھالنے والی کو اپنے خاندان کی تمام ضروریات کا پیشگی اندازہ ہونا چاہیے۔

اگر ہم ایماندار ہوں تو جانتے ہیں کہ یہ بیانات حقیقت پسندانہ نہیں ہیں۔ گھر سنبھالنے والے سب کچھ نہیں کر سکتے۔ تمام گھر سنبھالنے والوں کو کبھی کبھی مایوسی کا سامنا ہوتا ہے۔ ایک ماں مسلسل اپنے خاندان کی ضروریات سے ایک قدم آگے نہیں رہ سکتی۔

مصروف زندگی پر دوبارہ غور

گھریلو فرائض اور اپنے خاندان کی دیکھ بھال ہمارے دن بھر دیتی ہیں۔ کبھی کبھی یہی کام ہمیں انتہائی مصروف کر دیتے ہیں۔ مگر غیر نصابی سرگرمیوں یا اُس بلند معیار کا کیا جو ہم اپنے لیے رکھتے ہیں؟ ہمیں شاید مختلف انداز میں سوچنے کی ضرورت ہے تاکہ ہم ان عادات سے آزاد ہو سکیں جو ہمیں کنٹرول کرنے کی دھمکی دیتی ہیں۔

اپنی حدود قبول کریں

شاید آپ ایک ہفتے میں ایک ٹپّر ویئر پارٹی میں جا سکتی ہیں، بائبل اسٹڈی میں شامل ہو سکتی ہیں، اور باتھ روم دوبارہ رنگ بھی کروا سکتی ہیں۔ مگر کیا آپ کو کرنا چاہیے؟ اچھے گھر سنبھالنے والے خود کو آسانی اختیار کرنے کی اجازت دیتے ہیں چاہے وہ کسی اور طریقے سے کرنا پسند کریں۔ اس کا مطلب یہ ہے کہ اگر آپ شوقیہ روٹی بنانے والی ہیں تو خریداری کی ٹوکری میں چند روٹیاں ڈال دینا ٹھیک ہے۔

وہ چیزیں جانچیں جو مایوسی کا سبب بنتی ہیں

مصنوعی مسکراہٹیں اندرونی مایوسیوں کو چھپا سکتی ہیں، مگر یہ انہیں ختم نہیں کرتی۔ سب سے بہتر یہی ہے کہ مسئلے کو قبول کریں اور پھر حل تلاش کریں۔ مجھے یہ بات بار بار سیکھنی پڑی ہے۔ میرے خاندان کے تمام افراد جانتے ہیں کہ ہم پانچ بجکر تیس منٹ پر کھانا کھاتے ہیں۔ مگر دیر سے پہنچنے کی عادت عام ہورہی ہے، اور یہ مجھے تکلیف دیتی ہے۔

جب میں نے اپنی مایوسی اپنے شوہر کو بتائی تو اس نے سادہ الفاظ میں کہا، “کیوں نہ آپ مسئلے کی وضاحت کریں اور اتنی زیادہ پریشان نہ ہوں؟” اچھا نکتہ ہے۔ فعال طور پر حل تلاش کرنا بہت سے مسئلہ علاقوں میں کار آمد ہے۔

ناکام خواتین بھی اچھے گھر سنبھالنے والی بنتی ہیں

کامل ہونے کی فکر چھوڑ دیں اور ایسے فیصلے کریں جو آج کے لیے بہترین ہوں۔ خوش مزاج، خوش باش گھر سنبھالنے والی فرنیچر کے نیچے چند دھول کے ذرات رکھ سکتی ہیں، مگر وہ ایک ایسی روشنی پھینکتی ہیں جو لوگوں کو ان کے دل اور گھروں کی طرف کھینچتی ہے۔

خدمت کی حد کے حوالے سے ہر شخص مختلف ہے۔ دوسری طرف، ہر کوئی ایک جیسا ہے؛ ہم سب کی حدود ہوتی ہیں۔ آئندہ قسطوں میں، ہم اس بات پر بات کریں گے کہ اوورلوڈ کے عام نکات سے کیسے نمٹا جائے گا۔

حصہ 2

بہت سی گھر سنبھالنے والی خود کو گھر، خاندان، اور دیگر سرگرمیوں سے جڑی ذمہ داریوں کے درمیان پتلا محسوس کرتی ہیں۔ جتنا ہم مصروف ہیں، پھر بھی ہم اپنے شیڈول کو مزید بھرتے کیوں رہتے ہیں؟

میرے لیے یہ آسان ہے کہ میں کسی نئے منصوبے کے لیے رضامند ہو جاؤں اور پھر کام کے وسط میں ادراک کروں کہ میں نے اپنی حد سے زیادہ قدم بڑھا دیا ہے۔ بہت بار میں کسی منصوبے کو مکمل کرنے کے لیے درکار وقت کا اندازہ زیادہ کر لیتی ہوں اور کسی کام میں لگنے والے وقت کا اندازہ کم کر دیتی ہوں۔

واضح طور پر وعدوں کا بوجھ خودبخود بنتا ہے۔ جب ہم متعدد کردار ادا کرتے ہیں اور مزید ذمہ داریاں شامل کرتے ہیں تو ہم آسانی سے ان وعدوں کے غلام بن جاتے ہیں جو ہم نے کیے ہوتے ہیں۔ اوورلوڈ ہماری توانائی نکال دیتا ہے، ہمارے احساسات کو ماند کر دیتا ہے، اور ہماری خوشی کو سست کر دیتا ہے۔

اوورلوڈ کو پہچاننا

کبھی کبھی متعدد سرگرمیاں تیز رفتاری سے ایک کے بعد ایک پیش آتی ہیں۔ عام طور پر، ہم مختصر مدت کی مصروفیوں کے ساتھ بہہ لیتے ہیں۔ مگر اگر سرگرمیوں کا سلسلہ نہ ختم ہونے والا ہو اور ہم مسلسل مزید ذمہ داریاں شامل کرتے رہیں تو ہم ایک ایسا نمونہ پیدا کر لیتے ہیں جو زندگی کا طریقہ بن جاتا ہے۔

عام فرائض سے باہر بہت زیادہ وعدے ہمیں ڈپریشن اور برن آؤٹ کے امیدوار بنا دیتے ہیں۔ ذاتی طور پر، جب مجھے بے خوابی، لاتعلقی، یا چڑچڑاپن محسوس ہوتا ہے تو یہ میرے شیڈول کا جائزہ لینے کا وقت ہوتا ہے۔ اگر تبدیلیاں نہیں کی جاتیں تو کسی نہ کسی کو یا کسی چیز کو تکلیف اٹھانی پڑے گی۔

کوئی بھی ہمیشہ کے لیے خود کو حد سے زیادہ پھیلائے نہیں رکھ سکتا۔ بعض اوقات ہم اس تیزی کے نتائج بھگتتے ہیں جو ہمارے وسائل سے بڑھ کر ہوتی ہے۔ اوورلوڈ کی علامات میں نیند کی کمی، strained relationships, التوا، ناکامی کا خوف، اور کمزور مدافعتی نظام شامل ہو سکتے ہیں۔

اوورلوڈ سے آزاد ہونا

اوورلوڈ کی شناخت کرنے کے لیے خود کا ایماندارانہ جائزہ ضروری ہے۔ آپ کیسے جان سکتی ہیں کہ یہ محض ایک مصروف موسم ہے یا کیا مصروفیت نیا معمول بن چکی ہے؟ کیا آپ ایک درخواست کو اس لیے ٹھکرا رہی ہیں کہ زندگی بہت بھری ہوئی ہے، یا یہ ایک بہانہ ہے؟ کیا آپ کو فوراً “ہاں” کہنا ضروری ہے؟ مشق کے ساتھ، آپ یہ سیکھ سکتے ہیں کہ اوورلوڈ کی حد تک پہنچنے سے پہلے پیچھے ہٹنا کیسے ہے۔

کسی خیال یا درخواست کو قبول کرنے سے پہلے اسے جمانے دیں

اس نے مجھے بہت سے ذہنی دباؤ سے بچایا ہے۔ شمولیت کے لیے بہت سی اچھی چیزیں ہیں، اور روزانہ نئے خیالات آتے ہیں۔ بعض اوقات کاموں کو ہمارے شیڈول میں شامل کیا جا سکتا ہے۔ دوسرے اوقات میں مجھے انہیں بس چھوڑ دینا چاہیے اور اس پر توجہ مرکوز رکھنی چاہیے جو سب سے زیادہ اہم ہے۔ نئے خیالات اور درخواستوں کو شامل کرنے سے پہلے چند گھنٹے انتظار کرنے پر غور کریں۔

مشورہ حاصل کریں، خاص طور پر اپنے شوہر کا

ایک معروف ڈونٹ ساز سے نیلامی میں سٹال لگانے کے لیے کہا گیا۔ اس نے اپنے شوہر سے پوچھا کہ وہ اس بارے میں کیا سوچتے ہیں۔ انہوں نے کہا، “جب تک تم اس کے بارے میں پچھلے سال کی طرح شکایت اور دباؤ نہیں بڑھاؤ گی، مجھے پرواہ نہیں ہے۔” کیا اس کے شوہر نے “ہاں” کہا یا “نہیں”？ اس خاتون کو اس اشارے کو لینا چاہیے کہ ڈونٹ بنانا کسی طرح دباؤ بڑھا رہا تھا۔ یا تو وہ اسے نہ کرے، یا دونوں مل کر قابلِ عمل حل تلاش کریں۔

اپنے شیڈول کا باقاعدگی سے جائزہ لیں

ماضی، حال، اور مستقبل کے واقعات کا منظر لینے کے لیے ایک مفصل کیلنڈر رکھیں۔ اگر آپ کے خاندان میں پچھلے ہفتے فلو تھا اور آپ اگلے ہفتے ریاست سے باہر سفر کرنے کا منصوبہ بناتی ہیں تو کیا آپ مزید چیزیں شامل کریں؟ آپ کے خاندان کی جذباتی صحت کیا ہے؟ کیا آپ کا شوہر کام پر دباؤ میں ہے؟ بعض اوقات بہتر ہوتا ہے کہ ایک خالی وقت رکھا جائے تاکہ اسے اس وقت کی اہم چیز سے بھرا جا سکے۔ اگر آپ بہت پھیل جائیں تو آپ کسی کام میں اچھا نہیں کر سکتیں۔ بہت سی ذمہ داریاں ذاتی تازگی اور خوش مزاجی کے لیے مشکل پیدا کر دیتی ہیں۔ ذمہ داریوں کا حکمتِ عملی کے ساتھ انتخاب آپ کی توانائی کو اس جگہ لگانے میں مدد دے گا جہاں آج کے لیے سب سے زیادہ قدر ہو۔

The glory of the spring, how sweet!
The newborn life, how glad!
What joy the happy earth to greet
In new, bright raiment clad!

Divine Redeemer, Thee I bless;
I greet Thy going forth;
I love Thee in the loveliness
Of Thy renewed earth.

But O these wonders of Thy grace,
These nobler works of Thine,
These marvels sweeter far to trace,
These new births more divine:

This new-born glow of faith so strong,
This bloom of love so fair,
This new-born ecstasy of song,
And fragrancy of prayer!

Creator Spirit, work in me
These wonders sweet of Thine;
Divine Redeemer, graciously
Renew this heart of mine.

Still, let new life and strength upspring,
Still, let new joy be given;
And grant the glad new song to ring
Through the new earth and Heaven.

मैं तेरे renewed पृथ्वी की शोभा में तुझसे प्रेम करूँ।

परन्तु हे ये तेरी कृपा के चमत्कार,
ये तेरे अधिक पवित्र कृत्य,
ये अचरज जो इनसे कहीं अधिक मधुर हैं देखने में,
ये नव जन्में और अधिक दैवी नवोत्पत्तियाँ:

यह इतना प्रबल नवजात विश्वास का उज्जवल रूप,
यह इतना सुंदर प्रेम का पुष्प,
यह गीत का नवजात आनंद अशेष,
और प्रार्थना की सुवास!

सृष्टिकर्ता आत्मा, मुझमें काम कर
ये तेरे मधुर चमत्कार;
दैवी उद्धारकर्ता, कृपया
इस हृदय को नवीनीकृत कर।

फिर भी, नया जीवन और शक्ति उभरने दे,
फिर भी, नया आनंद दिया जाए;
और प्रबल नया गीत गूँजने दे
नई पृथ्वी और स्वर्ग में।

“Get out of my shop! I don’t need people like you around me! And never come back!” My lips quivered as I looked into the dark, angry eyes of the yelling man. I blinked back the unbidden tears, realizing that once more, I had to leave this man that I loved. All night I could sense that we were coming to this, and I had tried so hard not to let it happen. With one last attempt, I feebly yelled above the tension, “Ken, we don’t want to ...” but once more, I was rudely cut off. With slumped shoulders and downcast eyes, I turned to escape the confines of his dingy, pawn shop, his ever-crescendoing voice drowning the last hope of respite.

The lingering smell of smoke and the echo of his angry voice joined the troubled thoughts of my emotionally overwrought mind, as I slowly walked up the street. “What do you think, Josh?” I asked my faithful, quiet friend.

“I don’t know, " he responded, and we fell back into silent anguish at the outcome of our supposed Bible study, grasping for an explanation for the terrible response. What could we have done differently? Why could he not accept the truth? What lay behind those flashing eyes, and what memories are stored beneath his ever-crowning beanie?

Ken was born on a country farm in the rolling hills of Schuylkill, Pennsylvania, a splendid place for a curious and adventurous little boy to live.

When Ken was four years old, his parents separated. He had heard them fighting a lot, but he didn’t know that it was possible for Mom and Dad to separate. It crushed his heart and confused his innocent soul. He did not know how to handle the stress and change that was tossed on his peaceful life.

The terror and confusion of his mom hurriedly packing their belongings, loading him and his siblings in the car, and driving away are still riveted in his mind. It made no sense! Why couldn’t they just go home? In his musty bedroom at their little, dingy apartment, he lay staring at the moldy ceiling, wondering endlessly what had gone so wrong.

Ken soon adjusted to his new home in the city of Pottsville with only cars, people, and sidewalks instead of cows, frogs, and mud. But fate did not leave the small security his new lifestyle provided him. His mom was not able to properly care for him and his siblings, and so the children were placed in different foster homes. That was even worse than leaving Dad! The clothes he wore were the only things familiar to him. Instead of understanding and loving him, each new family brought more yelling, hatred, and beating. Terror, tears, loneliness, and pain accompanied him.

Ken thought the second foster home that he was placed in would be a safe, loving home. The dad was tall and strong and appeared to be gentle. The mom was overweight, but her friendly smile resolved his fears. But the first night, when he reached for the food, he accidentally dumped a cup of water. She screamed at him and told him that he was worthless, and she wished they had never gotten him. The dad continued eating as if he didn't hear or care. Why didn’t the strong man stop her?

That evening, Ken crawled into his big, strange bed, already crying in loneliness, when he heard the mom yell. He quickly jumped out of bed and, with trembling legs, slipped behind the door to hide. She charged up the stairs bellowing angrily, and Ken was sure that he was in trouble. To his relief, she continued down the hall. He was still too scared to leave his hiding place for fear of receiving a beating. He wiped his tears as he began to sing under his breath a song he had heard in Sunday school, “Jesus loves the little children, all the children of the world.” He stopped to think, and his crying quit. “Then why am I here? " he wondered. “Have I done something wrong? God must not love little children. That song is not true! If God loved me I would not be here!" With that conclusion, he burst into tears and lost hope in God. He woke the next morning, still hidden behind the door.

Darkness had long fallen, and my family was all peacefully sleeping in our old farmhouse. I cried myself to sleep, crying for Ken's soul, crying because I didn’t know what to do, crying because my friend, the man I longed to see at peace with God, hated me.

Ken continued to fire questions. “How can God be good and allow so much bad? How could God let children suffer?” I listened on as he continued saying the same things that I heard so many times before, giving me no chance to talk.

Again, it was time to leave, and I was so glad to do so. He kept talking as we backed out the door. Once more, my friend and I walked up the street —tired, frustrated, and wishing never to come back.

Ken was 13 years old, and his life was no better than it had been when he was first put into the foster system. His life was in turmoil. He was continually yelled at and belittled at home. Ken was tired of crying. No one cared, and there was no one with whom he could share his problem. That’s when he came up with his clever plan. His school friend was a hippie, and his parents traveled a lot. They were called Gypsies. He heard that they were headed to California. So, Ken told them about his terrible life and asked if they would give him a ride. They were glad to help.

That exciting morning, he just did his usual thing. He left for school and instead went to California. He didn’t mind leaving all his stuff behind—he really didn’t have much anyway. His foster parents didn’t even care that he left.

In California, Ken lived on the beach and worked for fishermen, and whoever else needed help. He always had enough to eat and something to do. He had his fellow beach bums, but he was still alone inside. His heart was still empty. He longed for love.

Ken lived on the beach for a year and a half and then hitchhiked to Arizona. There he found a home in a homeless shelter and got a job. He did well and soon was on his own, but his search for love took him down the wrong roads. Ken really wanted to be married to a loving wife and have a family, but the girl he married did not marry him because of love. She was hurt, and Ken’s own hurt soul was attracted to her. They got married and all was well for a few years until he found out that his wife was seeing other men. His heart was broken, and his world was thrown into turmoil. Ken wanted desperately to provide security for the children that were born to them, and so he tried his best to stay together. He did not want to put his children through the life that he experienced. But after eight rough years, they got a divorce.

Ken moved on and tried to recover from the devastation of the divorce. His search for love brought him only more sadness and pain. Since Ken was hurt and unhappy, he found satisfaction in making others happy. He spent all his money on them, and when he had nothing more to offer, they left.

Now Ken is sitting in his pawn shop, alone, hurt, sad, and hiding. He found through his sad life that no one cared. Every time that he opened himself to love, he was always hurt. Deep down inside, he truly felt that God did not care. He lost hope in God, people, and last of all, he lost hope in love itself. That is why we were still visiting the dingy, smoke-stained shop after six years of very little apparent success. God kept bringing us back. He put in us a persistent love and relentless burden for this wounded soul. That is why we spent many hours hearing the same criticisms over and over. The same problems, the same confusion.

Nearly every month, he would fluctuate between hope and despair, love and hate, new life in God, and sadness and sin. We never knew what the next visit would bring. We could be swelling with hope and filled with blessing, or torn with angry words and sickened with dread. But we kept going back, and slowly he emerged from the pit of despair, and slowly allowed himself to be wrapped in the wonderful love of God and the glorious message of His redeeming grace. It was amazing to see the change in his life and to hear his ever-growing confidence in the love of Christ.

Today Ken loves the Lord. He is learning to walk with God. He has seen the love of God. He has found hope in God. He has experienced the unconditional love of God. He is still growing, and we are excited to see what God has for him.

I’m so glad that God brought Ken into my life. God had a plan for Ken and I. God wanted to show Ken that He loved him and that He would be there for him even when Josh turned his back on Him. God also wanted me to carry a burden in my youth. He knew how easily I would be distracted with money and fun. He knew that I needed a burden to carry, a soul to care for. He wanted me to be able to see beneath the shell of a hard soul and see a hurting child within. He wanted to give me a burden too big for me to carry so that I would learn to lean on Him. And most of all, He wanted to equip me to serve Him in broader ways.

Fellow Christians, open your lives to the work of God. Find an opportunity to love a hurting soul. Search out someone who needs a friend and love them, and wait and see what God has in store for you. Love until it hurts so badly that you don’t know what to do, and then turn to Jesus, who is there to help you through. God may be waiting for you to make the first step before He will use you. Your life is before you. You can choose to live a comfortable, happy life, or you can open yourself up to be hurt and find that after years pass, your life is overflowing with meaning and purpose. Jesus opened Himself to the pain and anguish of this world, and only through that do we have hope. He is asking us to follow His example, to open ourselves to pain so that others can have hope. And as He was glorified, so will we be glorified, in some measure, someday, and we will never regret the pain that we faced.

“Ondoka dukani kwangu! Sitaki watu kama wewe karibu nami! Na usirudi tena!” Midomo yangu ilitetemeka nilipotazama machoni mwa mtu aliyekuwa mwenye hasira na kuongea kwa sauti. Nilitapika machozi yasiyotakikana, nikitambua kwamba tena, ilibidi nimwache mtu huyu niliyempenda. Usiku wote nilihisi kuwa tunakaribia kufika hapa, na nilijaribu kwa nguvu zote kutoiruhusu itokee. Kwa jaribio la mwisho, nilipiga sauti kwa udhaifu juu ya mkao wa mvutano, “Ken, hatutaki…” lakini tena, nilikatwa kwa sura ya ukatili. Mikono yangu ilidondoka na macho yakimwangalia chini, nikageuka kukimbia kutoka kwenye duka lake la nyumba ya kubadilishia dhahabu lililoachwa, sauti yake iliyokuwa ikiongezeka tena na tena ikifinya matumaini ya hupa.

Harufu ya moshi iliyobaki na mwangwi wa sauti yake ya hasira vilijiunga na mawazo yaliyochanganyikiwa ya akili yangu iliyokuwa imevurugika kihisia, nikiwa ninaenda polepole juu ya mtaa. “Unaonaje, Josh?” niliuliza rafiki yangu mwaminifu, mwenye ukimya.

“Sijui,” alijibu, na tukarudi katika huzuni tuliyokuwa nayo kwa matokeo ya kile tulichodhania kuwa somo la Biblia, tukikamata sababu kwa majibu mabaya. Tungeweza kufanya nini tofauti? Kwa nini hakuweza kukubali ukweli? Nini kilikuwa nyuma ya macho hayo yaliyochomoza, na ni kumbukumbu gani zilizohifadhiwa chini ya kofia yake iliyokuwa ikimfunika kichwa kila mara?

Ken alizaliwa kwenye shamba la nchi katika milima inayoinama ya Schuylkill, Pennsylvania, mahali pazuri kwa mvulana mdogo mwenye kutaka kujua na kuwa jasiri kuishi.

Ken alipokuwa na umri wa miaka minne, wazazi wake walitengana. Alikuwa amesikia wakipigana mara nyingi, lakini hakujua kuwa inawezekana Mama na Baba watenganishwe. Ilinyima moyo wake na kumchanganya roho yake isiyo na hatia. Hakujua jinsi ya kushughulikia msongo wa mawazo na mabadiliko yaliyorushwa kwenye maisha yake ya amani.

Hofu na mkanganyiko wa mama yake akibandikisha mali zao kwa haraka, wakimsogeza yeye na ndugu zake kwenye gari, na kuondoka, bado vimekwama kwenye akili yake. Kilikuwa hakina mantiki! Kwa nini hawawezi kurudi nyumbani? Katika chumba chake chenye unyevu katika nyumba yao ndogo ya kuthaminiwa, alilala akitazama dari yenye utelezi wa ukungu, akijiuliza bila kukoma kilichokwenda vibaya.

Ken mara moja alibadilika kwa makazifu na makazi mapya katika mji wa Pottsville akiwa na magari tu, watu, na barabara badala ya ng'ombe, vyura, na matope. Lakini hatima haikuacha usalama mdogo uliotolewa na mtindo wake mpya wa maisha. Mama yake hakuweza kumtunza yeye na ndugu zake ipasavyo, hivyo watoto waliwekwa katika nyumba tofauti za malezi. Hilo lilikuwa baya zaidi ya kuondoka kwa Baba! Mavazi aliyovaa ndiyo vitu vya pekee vilivyomfahamisha. Badala ya kumuelewa na kumpenda, kila familia mpya ilileta kelele zaidi, chuki, na kunyanyasa. Hofu, machozi, upweke, na maumivu vilimfuata.

Ken alidhani nyumbani kwa malezi ya pili aliyowekwa wangekuwa mahali salama na lenye upendo. Baba alikuwa mrefu na mwenye nguvu na alionekana mpole. Mama alikuwa na uzito, lakini tabasamu lake la kirafiki lilitoweka hofu zake. Lakini usiku wa kwanza, alipofikia chakula, kwa bahati mbaya alimwagwa kikombe cha maji. Alililia kwa sauti na kumwambia kwamba hakuwa na thamani, na alitamani wangemwacha wasimpate. Baba aliendelea kula kana kwamba hakusikia wala kujali. Kwa nini mwanaume huyo mwenye nguvu hakuizuia?

Usiku huo, Ken alimikwa kitandani pake kikubwa na cha kigeni, tayari akilia kwa upweke, aliposikia mama akilia kwa ghadhabu. Aliruka kutoka kitandani kwa kasi na, kwa miguu inayotetemeka, alikunyoka nyuma ya mlango kujificha. Alipanda ngazi akiwa akilia kwa hasira, na Ken alikuwa hakika alikuwa katika shida. Kwa faraja yake, aliendelea chini ya ukuta wa korido. Bado alikuwa na woga wa kutoka mahali alipojificha kwa hofu ya kupigwa. Alisafisha machozi yake na alianza kuimba kwa chini ya pumzi wimbo aliusikia shuleni siku ya Jumapili, “Yesu anawapenda watoto wadogo, watoto wote wa dunia.” Akasimama kufikiri, na kilio chake kilikoma. “Basi kwa nini niko hapa?” alijiuliza. “Nimefanya jambo baya? Mungu lazima asipende watoto wadogo. Wimbo huo si wa kweli! Ikiwa Mungu ananipenda ningekua hapa!” Kwa hitimisho hilo, alilia kwa nguvu na akapata tamaa kwa Mungu. Aliamka asubuhi iliyoifu, bado amejificha nyuma ya mlango.

Giza lilikuwa limeanguka kwa muda mrefu, na familia yangu yote ilikuwa ikilala kwa amani kwenye nyumba yetu ya zamani ya shamba. Nililia hadi nilipolala, nikiomba kwa roho ya Ken, nikiomba kwa sababu sikuwa najua la kufanya, nikiomba kwa sababu rafiki yangu, mtu niliyekuwa natamani kumwona akiupata utulivu kwa Mungu, alinipinga.

Ken aliendelea kuuliza maswali. “Mungu anawezaje kuwa mwema na kuruhusu mabaya mengi? Mungu angewezaje kumsumbua mtoto?” Nilisikiliza alipoongea tena yale yale niliyoyasikia mara nyingi, akiniongezea nafasi hakuna ya kuongea.

Tena, ilikuwa wakati wa kuondoka, na nilifurahi kufanya hivyo. Aliendelea kuzungumza tulipokuwa tukitembea nje ya mlango. Tena, rafiki yangu na mimi tulitembea mtaa —wote tulioshindwa, tumechoka, na tukitamani tusirudi tena.

Ken alikuwa na umri wa miaka 13, na maisha yake hayakuwa bora kuliko ilivyokuwa alipoanza kuwekwa kwenye mfumo wa malezi. Maisha yake yalikuwa kwenye vurugu. Alikuwa analia mara kwa mara na kudharaulika nyumbani. Ken alikuwa amechanika kwa kulia. Hakuna aliyemjali, na hakukuwa na mtu atakayemsaidia kugawana tatizo lake. Ndipo alipoja na mpango wake mwenye busara. Rafiki yake wa shule alikuwa hippie, na wazazi wake walikuwa wanasafiri sana. Walikuwa wanaitwa Wageri. Aliisikia kuwa walikuwa wakienda California. Hivyo, Ken aliwaambia kuhusu maisha yake mabaya na kuwauliza kama wangeweza kumchukua. Walifurahi kusaidia.

Siku hiyo yenye msisimko, alifanya tu alivyokuwa akifanya kawaida. Alitoka kwenda shule na badala yake akaenda California. Hakujali kuacha vitu vyake vyote nyuma—hakuwa na mengi hata hivyo. Wazazi wake wa malezi hawakujali hata kwamba alikuwa ameondoka.

California, Ken aliishi ufukweni na kufanya kazi kwa wavuvi, na kwa yeyote aliyemhitaji msaada. Daima alikuwa na chakula cha kutosha na kitu cha kufanya. Alikuwa na wenzao wa ufukweni, lakini bado alikuwa peke yake ndani. Moyo wake bado ulikuwa tupu. Alitamani upendo.

Ken aliishi ufukweni kwa mwaka mmoja na nusu kisha akapiga msafara kwa usingizi hadi Arizona. Huko alipata makazi katika kambi ya wasio na makazi na akapata kazi. Alifanikiwa na hivi karibuni alikuwa peke yake, lakini utafutaji wake wa upendo ulimpeleka kwenye njia mbaya. Ken alitaka sana kuolewa na mke mwenye upendo na kuwa na familia, lakini msichana aliyekuwa ameoa hakumwona kwa sababu ya upendo. Alikuwa ameumizwa, na roho ya Ken mwenye majeraha ilivutiwa kwake. Wakaolewa na kila kitu kilikuwa sawa kwa miaka michache hadi alipogundua kuwa mkewe alikuwa akiwaona wanaume wengine. Moyo wake ulivunjika, na ulimwengu wake ukageuka. Ken alitaka sana kumweka watoto waliokuwa wametoka kwao katika usalama, hivyo alijaribu kwa nguvu kutegemeana. Hakutaka kuwapelekea watoto maisha aliyoyapata. Lakini baada ya miaka nane ya magumu, walitengana kwa ndoa.

Ken aliendelea na kujaribu kupona kutokana na uharibifu wa talaka. Utafutaji wake wa upendo ulimletea huzuni na maumivu zaidi. Kwa kuwa Ken alikuwa ameumizwa na haifurahi, alipata kuridhika katika kuwafanya wengine wafurahie. Alitumia pesa zake zote kwao, na alipokuwa hana chochote tena cha kuwapa, walienda.

Sasa Ken anakaa kwenye duka lake la kubadilishia dhahabu, peke yake, amejeruhiwa, msikitiko, na kujificha. Alichojifunza kupitia maisha yake ya huzuni ni kwamba hakuna aliyemjali. Kila mara alipojitolea kwa upendo, alikuwa kujeruhiwa. Chini kabisa moyoni, alihisi sana kwamba Mungu hakujali. Alipoteza matumaini kwa Mungu, watu, na mwishowe, alipoteza matumaini kwa upendo mwenyewe. Ndio sababu bado tulikuwa tukitembelea duka lile lenye mng'ao wa moshi baada ya miaka sita ya mafanikio machache yaliyoonekana. Mungu aliendelea kuturejea. Alitupatia mapenzi yasiyotokomea na mzigo usioacha kwa nafsi hii iliyokuwa imejeruhiwa. Ndio sababu tulitumia saa nyingi kusikiliza tu ukosoaji ule mara kwa mara. Matatizo yale yale, mkanganyiko ule ule.

Kila mwezi karibu, angependa kubadilika kati ya matumaini na kukata tamaa, upendo na chuki, uhai mpya kwa Mungu, na huzuni na dhambi. Hatukuwahi kujua ziara ijayo italeta nini. Tunaweza kujazwa na matumaini na kubeba neema, au tukatwamka kwa maneno ya ghadhabu na kuhisi hofu kabisa. Lakini tuliendelea kurudi, na polepole alitoka kwenye shimo la kukata tamaa, na polepole akajiruhusu kufunikwa na upendo wa ajabu wa Mungu na ujumbe wa utukufu wa neema yake ya ukombozi. Ilikuwa ajabu kuona mabadiliko katika maisha yake na kusikia kujiamini kwake kukizidi katika upendo wa Kristo.

Leo Ken anampenda Bwana. Anajifunza kutembea na Mungu. Ameona upendo wa Mungu. Ameipata tumaini kwa Mungu. Ameweza kuhisi upendo usio na masharti wa Mungu. Bado anastawi, na tunafurahi kuona kile Mungu ana kwake.

Ninafurahi sana kwamba Mungu alimleta Ken katika maisha yangu. Mungu alikuwa na mpango wa Ken na mimi. Mungu alipenda kumwonyesha Ken kwamba Yeye alimpenda na kwamba atakuwa naye hata wakati Josh aligeuka naye. Mungu pia alitaka niwe na mzigo wakati wa ujana wangu. Alijua jinsi nilivyokuwa ninaweza kufurahi kwa urahisi na pesa na burudani. Alijua kwamba nilihitaji mzigo wa kubeba, nafsi ya kumjali. Alitaka niweze kuona chini ya ganda la nafsi ngumu na kuona mtoto aliyejeruhiwa ndani. Alitaka kunipa mzigo ambao ungekuwa mkubwa mno kwa mimi kubeba ili nijifunze kutegemea Yeye. Na zaidi ya yote, alitaka kuinifuata ili nimtumikie Yeye kwa njia pana zaidi.

Wakristo wenzangu, fungulieni maisha yenu kwa kazi ya Mungu. Tafuteni fursa ya kupenda nafsi iliyojeruhiwa. Tafuteni mtu anayeahitaji rafiki na mwapende, kisha ngoja muone kile Mungu amekuwekea. Pende hadi itakavyokuumiza sana kiasi kwamba hutajua la kufanya, kisha geuka kwa Yesu, ambaye yupo hapo kukusaidia kupita hayo. Mungu anaweza kuwa anasubiri wewe kuchukua hatua ya kwanza kabla Yeye akutumie. Maisha yako yako mbele yako. Unaweza kuchagua kuishi maisha ya starehe na furaha, au unaweza kujifungua ili kujeruhiwa na kugundua kwamba baada ya miaka kupita, maisha yako yatakuwa yamejaa maana na kusudi. The winter of 1882 unfolded in the small southern town of Tuscumbia, Alabama. A happy, normal two-year-old girl fell desperately ill with a strange fever. The fever came and went, came and went, and came again. The family doctor feared the child would die of the strain, but the child was strong and one day the fever finally left for good. The following day the mother waved a hand past her daughter's face, but the child did not blink. Subsequent efforts wrought no results and a new day dawned upon the family with a blind daughter.

As the child gained strength enough to resume play, the great dinner bell released its peal to all around, but Helen did not respond. Other noises produced similar results and the Keller family came to the stark realization that life would never be the same again. Most of us may never face the grim circumstances that Helen Keller's family did, but each of us will certainly endure hardships tailored specifically by our God.

The human mind is an amazing and intricate creation. Though many have sought to understand it, its operational ability remains incomprehensible to mankind. It is no small wonder that a portion of the keenest insight into the health of the mind is revealed in God's Word. “For God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind.” (2 Timothy 1:7)

Fear is the ominous adversary to a sound mind. It towers over the soul and taunts the saint with its menacing derision. Fear can take a sunny meadow and turn it into a lonely wilderness. It can render a grand wedding celebration as dark as a cave, and turn a banquet fit for a king into a nauseating affair. It is the most powerful and devastating tool in the devil's employment. Despite many bold claims, none are exempt from its wielding. “A dreadful sound is in his ears: in prosperity the destroyer shall come upon him. He believeth not that he shall return out of darkness, and he is waited for of the sword.” (Job 15:21, 22) It is fear that stands to attack and quench all the prosperity of the soul. If we are to resist it in these days, we he must rise with all diligence in defiant warfare.

We do not need to look very far to behold the disarmament and weakening of man's mind. Medication for the mind ranks among the leading prescriptions consumed in America today. This is no pointed accusation at any individuals who may find themselves in need of medical assistance to control their mind. But it takes no scholar to look at obesity and consider the diet, to see rebellious teens and connect it to the infrastructure of the home, or to see men's hearts (minds) failing them and believe that fear is at the root. While some may totally master their diet, few can claim to be accomplished parents. Fewer yet are those who are not, at times, accosted by fear. Though pride and sense may keep the outward man in check, and remaining perfectly calm, the inward man, at least subconsciously, must deal with the strain. Americans love to claim the motto, "No fear!" but our medication consumption tells a different story. Paul claimed no exemption, for he was “troubled on every side; without were fightings, within were fears.” (2 Corinthians 7:5)

What do we fear? Loss, pain, and humility. No one likes to lose something that we have fought to obtain. No one enjoys pain. No one loves to be humiliated. Still, we do not need to read far in the Scriptures to realize that these are often the avenues that God uses to further urge His servants down the path into His likeness. There is no insurance on earth that can secure the vibrancy of youth, the love of a family, or the respect of friends. The things that supply us with earth's greatest vanguard are all vulnerable to the risks of loss. Therefore, we fear. Though we lie in bed until the dawn of the morning, we can in no wise increase our stature nor alleviate the loss that God has laid upon our lives. This anxiety only furthers our grief and adds fuel to our fears.

“Be careful for nothing; but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God. And the peace of God, which passeth all understanding, shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus.” (Philippians 4:6 7) Herein is the keeping of our hearts and minds: prayer, peace, and thanksgiving.

Like a skillful artisan we must carefully weave these two scriptures together on the loom of life for there seems to be a direct correlation between the fruitful - power, love and sound mind, to the “rootful”- prayer, peace, and thankfulness. There will be no conquering of our fears without these things, and every society that is anemic to these ingredients will certainly be handicapped.

Prayer Begets Power

In our weakened condition we cannot apprehend prayer as we ought. It is then we must rely on those who can or perhaps the Spirit, which maketh intercession for us with groanings which cannot be uttered. Communing with the Omnipotent Head of the universe is a tremendously bold task. Many will administer prayer as merely a formal task, seeking to be perfectly reverent in it. This is not communing as with a friend, nor is it bold. It is more apt to fall under the description of fear. The remedial therapy for fear is in pouring out all our anxiety, bitterness, and complaint onto our God. The saints of yesteryear had been known to vehemently pour out their accusations and the bitterness of their soul unto God.

“Then Job answered and said, Even to day is my complaint bitter: my stroke is heavier than my groaning. Oh that I knew where I might find him! That I might come even to his seat! I would order my cause before him, and fill my mouth with arguments. I would know the words which he would answer me, and understand what he would say unto me. Will he plead against me with his great power? No; but he would put strength in me.” (Job 23:1-6)

  • David —“I poured out my complaint before him; I shewed before him my trouble.” (Psalm 142:2)
  • Hannah —“For out of the abundance of my complaint and grief have I spoken hitherto.” (1 Samuel 1:16)
  • Jeremiah —“He hath filled me with bitterness, he hath made me drunken with wormwood.”
    (Lamentations 3:15)
  • Naomi —“Call me Mara: for the Almighty hath dealt very bitterly with me.” (Ruth 1:20)
  • Hezekiah —“He will cut me off with pining sickness: from day even to night wilt thou make an end of me.” (Isaiah 38:12)
  • Jesus — “My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?” (Matthew 27:46)

All these spewed forth bold accusations and complaints against God in fervent prayer and none of them offended Him. On the contrary, God had not given them the spirit of fear but of power, and they serve as our examples. It was faithless Ahab who was told to ask of God a sign in the heavens or earth. In his pious reply he refused to "tempt" God. This lack of boldness and abundance of fear is more tempting to God than the abundance of bitterness in our complaint for “there is no fear in love; but perfect love casteth out fear: because fear hath torment. He that feareth is not made perfect in love.” (1 John 4:18)

Peace Begets Love

We are all at rest with the things we love. "Great peace have they which love thy law: and nothing shall offend them.” (Psalm 119:165) A sparkling young child who is at peace with his father worships the man and strives to imitate him. Through the lad's tender eyes, his father's character is unflawed. His skill is unmatched. Even the brand of vehicle he drives is the best, and he emulates his every action. Even though every father knows the limitations of his son's expectations, we all bask in the seasonal loyalty. It is knowledge and fear that undermines this loyal love. An abusive father will destroy such childhood esteem and fear will be its replacement. It was through base fear that the evil servant buried his talent and did not trade with it. In his eyes his master was austere and to be feared. But God has not given us the spirit of fear but of love.

“We love him, because he first loved us. If a man say, I love God, and hateth his brother, he is a liar: for he that loveth not his brother whom he hath seen, how can he love God whom he hath not seen?” (1 John 4:19, 20) The soul who is affected by this love cannot but imitate it. He is at great peace with his Father’s love and the eyes through which he views his Father's character can only enlist replication. However dire the circumstances we may find ourselves in, this spirit of love and peace will carry us through whatever opposition we may meet with on life's pathway. Jacob made nothing of the hard service he was to endure for Rachel; the spirit of love to God will set us above the fear of man, and all the hurt that a man can do us.

Thankfulness Begets a Sound Mind

We do not need to study happy souls long to find buried within the bedrock of each one, a foundation of gratitude. The spirit of a sound mind, or quietness of mind, is a peaceable enjoyment of life. We are oftentimes discouraged in our way when the features of our environment do not measure not up to our own fancy and imagination. A mere sober, solid, thinking mind would obviate and defuse such fruitless notions, yet we are all tempted to entertain formidable ingratitude. It takes no brainpower to expose things we disdain, for Satan is certain to magnify and outline every unsatisfactory detail we encounter. We each may think ourselves into a deep cave, but we must thank ourselves out.

Fear of losing our health, wealth, reputation, and happiness is the biggest hindrance to securing it. To focus on our pain is to invite more. To be constantly analyzing our life to see if we are being fulfilled is a sure avenue to ingratitude. The world is constantly asking, "Are we having fun yet?" The answer is, "No". To these souls, life will never be adequate, and they must wander forth seeking the bigger fulfillment that the last one did not secure. It is the fear that we are not receiving our fair allotment in life that breeds discontentment. It is discontentment that produces more fear, and the downward spiral progresses. Such was the consternation of the soul who asked Christ to speak to his brother to divide the inheritance with him. This may be logical thinking, but it is not conducive to a sound and peaceable mind. This offended soul has no root in himself and will forever be wronged in some fashion and spend his days in search of a savior to come and fix the other party. “... neither fear ye their fear, nor be afraid. Sanctify the LORD of hosts himself; and let him be your fear, and let him be your dread.” (Isaiah 8:12, 13)

There is no earthly level of attainment or perfect environment that will promote a sound mind. It can only be secured through prayer, peace, and thankfulness. This may take some reprogramming of our minds to reach into the subconscious recesses, but we must soberly gird up the loins of our minds and exercise them if we ever hope to obtain “the grace that is to be brought unto you at the revelation of Jesus Christ;” (1 Peter 1:13)

“And the peace of God,
which passeth all understanding,
shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus.
Finally, brethren, whatsoever things are true,
whatsoever things are honest, whatsoever things are just,
whatsoever things are pure, whatsoever things are lovely,
whatsoever things are of good report;
if there be any virtue, and if there be any praise,
think on these things.

— Philippians 4:7, 8

1882 年的冬天在阿拉巴马州南部的小镇塔斯卡比亚展开。一个快乐、正常的两岁小女孩患上了一种奇怪的发烧，病情危急。热病时来时去，断断续续，最后又复发。家里的医生担心孩子会因为折磨而死去，但孩子身体结实，终于有一天热病彻底离开了。第二天，母亲在女儿脸前挥手，但孩子没有眨眼。之后的努力也无济于事，新的一天来临时，家庭发现女儿已成盲人。

当孩子恢复到足以继续玩耍的力气时，巨大的晚餐钟向四周敲响，但海伦没有作出反应。其他声音也产生类似的结果，凯勒一家逐渐认识到生活再也不会像从前那样了。我们大多数人可能永远不会面临海伦·凯勒一家所遭遇的严峻处境，但我们每个人肯定会忍受上帝为我们量身定制的苦难。

人的心智是一个奇妙而精密的创造。尽管许多人试图理解它，但其运作能力仍为人所难以穷尽。并不奇怪，上帝的话语中展露出对心智健康最深刻的洞见之一。“For God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind.” (2 Timothy 1:7)

恐惧是对清醒心智的可怕敌手。它高压于灵魂之上，用威胁与嘲弄戏弄圣徒。恐惧可以把一片阳光明媚的草地变成孤独的荒野。它能使盛大的婚礼庆典变得像洞穴一样阴暗，把适合君王的宴席变成令人作呕的场面。它是魔鬼所用的最强大、最具毁灭性的工具。尽管有许多大胆的宣称，但没有人能完全免于其摆布。“A dreadful sound is in his ears: in prosperity the destroyer shall come upon him. He believeth not that he shall return out of darkness, and he is waited for of the sword.” (Job 15:21, 22) 正是恐惧站在那儿攻击并熄灭灵魂的一切繁荣。如果我们要在这些日子抵抗它，就必须以全部的勤勉起来进行反抗性的争战。

我们不需走很远就能看到人心的解除武装与衰弱。心智用药如今位居美国常用处方之首。这并非对任何可能需要医学帮助以控制心智的个人发出指责。但不需学者也能看见肥胖便想到饮食，看到叛逆青少年便联想到家庭结构，或看到人的心（心智）失常便相信恐惧是根源。尽管有些人可能完全掌控了他们的饮食，很少有人能声称自己是称职的家长。更少有人能说他们从未在某些时候遭受恐惧的侵袭。尽管自尊与理智可能在外表上使人保持镇定，但内里的那个人，至少在潜意识层面，必须与压力搏斗。美国人喜欢宣称格言，“No fear!”，但我们的药物消费讲述了不同的故事。保罗并不自我豁免，因为他也曾“troubled on every side; without were fightings, within were fears.” (2 Corinthians 7:5)

我们害怕什么？失去、痛苦和屈辱。没有人喜欢失去自己为之奋斗所得之物。没有人喜欢痛苦。没有人喜欢受辱。然而，我们不需要在圣经中读得很远就会意识到，这些常常是上帝用来推动祂的仆人走向与祂相似之路的途径。世上没有保险能保障青春的朝气、家庭的爱或朋友的尊重。那些为我们供应世上最大防线的事物，都容易遭受失去的风险。因此，我们会害怕。尽管我们躺在床上直到拂晓，我们无论如何也无法增加自身的地位，也无法减轻上帝加在我们身上的失落。这种焦虑只会加重我们的悲伤，并为我们的恐惧添薪加炭。

“Be careful for nothing; but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God. And the peace of God, which passeth all understanding, shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus.” (Philippians 4:6 7) 在此乃是保守我们心与意的要道：祷告、平安与感谢。

像一位娴熟的工匠，我们必须在生命的织机上细心地将这两段经文并织在一起，因为看似“有果实”的——能力、爱与清醒心智，与“有根基”的——祷告、平安与感恩之间存在直接的关联。没有这些事就无法征服我们的恐惧，任何缺乏这些成分的社会肯定会受制约。

祷告生出能力

在我们虚弱的状态下，我们无法如应有那样把握祷告。在那时我们必须依靠能祷告的人，或许还有那位“the Spirit, which maketh intercession for us with groanings which cannot be uttered.” 与全能宇宙之头相交是一项极其大胆的任务。许多人把祷告仅仅当作一项形式性的事务，力求在其中保持完美的敬虔。这既不是与朋友般的交通，也不是大胆。这更容易落入“害怕”的范畴。医治恐惧的疗法在于把我们所有的焦虑、苦涩与抱怨都倾倒到我们的神面前。昔日的圣徒素来以猛烈地向神倾诉指控与心中苦楚而著称。

“Then Job answered and said, Even to day is my complaint bitter: my stroke is heavier than my groaning. Oh that I knew where I might find him! That I might come even to his seat! I would order my cause before him, and fill my mouth with arguments. I would know the words which he would answer me, and understand what he would say unto me. Will he plead against me with his great power? No; but he would put strength in me.” (Job 23:1-6)

  • 大卫 —“I poured out my complaint before him; I shewed before him my trouble.” (Psalm 142:2)
  • 哈拿 —“For out of the abundance of my complaint and grief have I spoken hitherto.” (1 Samuel 1:16)
  • 耶利米 —“He hath filled me with bitterness, he hath made me drunken with wormwood.”
    (Lamentations 3:15)
  • 拿俄米 —“Call me Mara: for the Almighty hath dealt very bitterly with me.” (Ruth 1:20)
  • 希西家 —“He will cut me off with pining sickness: from day even to night wilt thou make an end of me.” (Isaiah 38:12)
  • 耶稣 — “My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?” (Matthew 27:46)

所有这些人都在热切的祷告中向神大胆地倾诉指控与抱怨，而这些并没有得罪祂。相反，上帝没有赐给他们惧怕的心，反而赐给他们能力，他们成为我们的榜样。正是无信的亚哈被告知要向神求一个天上或地下的兆头。在他虔诚的回答里，他拒绝去“tempt”神。这种缺乏大胆和充满恐惧，较之我们抱怨中的满怀苦涩更令神试探。因为“there is no fear in love; but perfect love casteth out fear: because fear hath torment. He that feareth is not made perfect in love.” (1 John 4:18)

平安生出爱

我们与所爱之物同处便得安息。“Great peace have they which love thy law: and nothing shall offend them.” (Psalm 119:165) 一个与父亲和睦相处的天真孩童崇拜那人并努力效法他。透过孩子温柔的目光，他父亲的品格是无可指摘的。他的技能无与伦比。就连他所开的车也是最好的，他效仿父亲的一举一动。尽管每位父亲都知道儿子期望的局限，我们都沉浸在那季节性的忠诚中。正是知识和惧怕破坏了这种忠爱。虐待的父亲会摧毁这样的童年尊崇，而惧怕将取而代之。正是通过低劣的惧怕，那恶仆埋藏了他的才干而不去经商。在他眼中，他的主人严厉且应当被惧怕。但神并没有赐给我们惧怕的心，乃是赐给我们爱的心。

“We love him, because he first loved us. If a man say, I love God, and hateth his brother, he is a liar: for he that loveth not his brother whom he hath seen, how can he love God whom he hath not seen?” (1 John 4:19, 20) 被这爱影响的灵魂不得不去模仿它。他在父的爱里极得平安，他透过父的性情所看的目光只能招来模仿。不论我们身处何等凶险境地，这种爱与平安的心灵将使我们穿越人生路上所遇到的一切抵挡。雅各对为拉结所当受的辛苦并不在意；对上帝的爱之心将使我们高过对人的惧怕，以及人能对我们施加的一切伤害。

感恩生出清醒的心智

我们不必长时间研究快乐的灵魂就能发现，在每一个快乐灵魂的基岩之下都埋藏着一座感恩的根基。清醒心智的灵，或心智的宁静，是对生命的平和享受。当我们的环境特征达不到我们自己的喜好与想象时，我们常常在路上灰心丧志。仅有一颗清醒、稳重的头脑就能排除并瓦解这些徒劳的念头，然而我们都易受试探去培养强烈的不感恩。揭露我们所轻蔑之物并不需要多少脑力，因为撒但必然放大并描绘出我们遇见的每一个不满意的细节。我们每个人都可能把自己想象进一个深洞，但我们必须靠感恩把自己带出。

对失去健康、财富、名誉与快乐的恐惧，是保障这些事物的最大阻碍。专注于我们的痛苦就是招来更多的痛苦。不断地分析我们的生活以查看我们是否得到满足，是走向忘恩的必经之路。世人不断地问：“Are we having fun yet?” 答案是，“No”。对这些人来说，生命永远不够，他们必须继续漂泊，寻找上一个未能满足他们的更大满足。正是对未能在生命中得到公平份额的恐惧滋生了不满。不满又产生更多的恐惧，下滑的螺旋便持续发展。这正是那心怀忧惧之人的苦恼，他求基督对他兄弟说话，让其与他分割基业。这或许是合乎逻辑的思维，但它不利于清醒与平和的心。这受冒犯的灵在自己里面没有根，并将永远以某种方式受委屈，终日寻求一位要来为他修补他人过错的救主。“... neither fear ye their fear, nor be afraid. Sanctify the LORD of hosts himself; and let him be your fear, and let him be your dread.” (Isaiah 8:12, 13)

世上没有任何水平的成就或完美环境能促成清醒的心智。它只能通过祷告、平安与感恩来获得。这或许需要我们对心智作一些重新编程，以触及潜意识的深处，但我们必须清醒地束起心智的腰并锻炼它们，若我们仍抱希望得着“the grace that is to be brought unto you at the revelation of Jesus Christ;” (1 Peter 1:13)

“And the peace of God,
which passeth all understanding,
shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus.
Finally, brethren, whatsoever things are true,
whatsoever things are honest, whatsoever things are just,
whatsoever things are pure, whatsoever things are lovely,
whatsoever things are of good report;
if there be any virtue, and if there be any praise,

The winter of 1882 unfolded in the small southern town of Tuscumbia, Alabama. A happy, normal two-year-old girl fell desperately ill with a strange fever. The fever came and went, came and went, and came again. The family doctor feared the child would die of the strain, but the child was strong and one day the fever finally left for good. The following day the mother waved a hand past her daughter's face, but the child did not blink. Subsequent efforts wrought no results and a new day dawned upon the family with a blind daughter.

As the child gained strength enough to resume play, the great dinner bell released its peal to all around, but Helen did not respond. Other noises produced similar results and the Keller family came to the stark realization that life would never be the same again. Most of us may never face the grim circumstances that Helen Keller's family did, but each of us will certainly endure hardships tailored specifically by our God.

The human mind is an amazing and intricate creation. Though many have sought to understand it, its operational ability remains incomprehensible to mankind. It is no small wonder that a portion of the keenest insight into the health of the mind is revealed in God's Word. “For God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind.” (2 Timothy 1:7)

Fear is the ominous adversary to a sound mind. It towers over the soul and taunts the saint with its menacing derision. Fear can take a sunny meadow and turn it into a lonely wilderness. It can render a grand wedding celebration as dark as a cave, and turn a banquet fit for a king into a nauseating affair. It is the most powerful and devastating tool in the devil's employment. Despite many bold claims, none are exempt from its wielding. “A dreadful sound is in his ears: in prosperity the destroyer shall come upon him. He believeth not that he shall return out of darkness, and he is waited for of the sword.” (Job 15:21, 22) It is fear that stands to attack and quench all the prosperity of the soul. If we are to resist it in these days, we he must rise with all diligence in defiant warfare.

We do not need to look very far to behold the disarmament and weakening of man's mind. Medication for the mind ranks among the leading prescriptions consumed in America today. This is no pointed accusation at any individuals who may find themselves in need of medical assistance to control their mind. But it takes no scholar to look at obesity and consider the diet, to see rebellious teens and connect it to the infrastructure of the home, or to see men's hearts (minds) failing them and believe that fear is at the root. While some may totally master their diet, few can claim to be accomplished parents. Fewer yet are those who are not, at times, accosted by fear. Though pride and sense may keep the outward man in check, and remaining perfectly calm, the inward man, at least subconsciously, must deal with the strain. Americans love to claim the motto, "No fear!" but our medication consumption tells a different story. Paul claimed no exemption, for he was “troubled on every side; without were fightings, within were fears.” (2 Corinthians 7:5)

What do we fear? Loss, pain, and humility. No one likes to lose something that we have fought to obtain. No one enjoys pain. No one loves to be humiliated. Still, we do not need to read far in the Scriptures to realize that these are often the avenues that God uses to further urge His servants down the path into His likeness. There is no insurance on earth that can secure the vibrancy of youth, the love of a family, or the respect of friends. The things that supply us with earth's greatest vanguard are all vulnerable to the risks of loss. Therefore, we fear. Though we lie in bed until the dawn of the morning, we can in no wise increase our stature nor alleviate the loss that God has laid upon our lives. This anxiety only furthers our grief and adds fuel to our fears.

“Be careful for nothing; but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God. And the peace of God, which passeth all understanding, shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus.” (Philippians 4:6 7) Herein is the keeping of our hearts and minds: prayer, peace, and thanksgiving.

Like a skillful artisan we must carefully weave these two scriptures together on the loom of life for there seems to be a direct correlation between the fruitful - power, love and sound mind, to the “rootful”- prayer, peace, and thankfulness. There will be no conquering of our fears without these things, and every society that is anemic to these ingredients will certainly be handicapped.

Prayer Begets Power

In our weakened condition we cannot apprehend prayer as we ought. It is then we must rely on those who can or perhaps the Spirit, which maketh intercession for us with groanings which cannot be uttered. Communing with the Omnipotent Head of the universe is a tremendously bold task. Many will administer prayer as merely a formal task, seeking to be perfectly reverent in it. This is not communing as with a friend, nor is it bold. It is more apt to fall under the description of fear. The remedial therapy for fear is in pouring out all our anxiety, bitterness, and complaint onto our God. The saints of yesteryear had been known to vehemently pour out their accusations and the bitterness of their soul unto God.

“Then Job answered and said, Even to day is my complaint bitter: my stroke is heavier than my groaning. Oh that I knew where I might find him! That I might come even to his seat! I would order my cause before him, and fill my mouth with arguments. I would know the words which he would answer me, and understand what he would say unto me. Will he plead against me with his great power? No; but he would put strength in me.” (Job 23:1-6)

  • David —“I poured out my complaint before him; I shewed before him my trouble.” (Psalm 142:2)
  • Hannah —“For out of the abundance of my complaint and grief have I spoken hitherto.” (1 Samuel 1:16)
  • Jeremiah —“He hath filled me with bitterness, he hath made me drunken with wormwood.”
    (Lamentations 3:15)
  • Naomi —“Call me Mara: for the Almighty hath dealt very bitterly with me.” (Ruth 1:20)
  • Hezekiah —“He will cut me off with pining sickness: from day even to night wilt thou make an end of me.” (Isaiah 38:12)
  • Jesus — “My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?” (Matthew 27:46)

All these spewed forth bold accusations and complaints against God in fervent prayer and none of them offended Him. On the contrary, God had not given them the spirit of fear but of power, and they serve as our examples. It was faithless Ahab who was told to ask of God a sign in the heavens or earth. In his pious reply he refused to "tempt" God. This lack of boldness and abundance of fear is more tempting to God than the abundance of bitterness in our complaint for “there is no fear in love; but perfect love casteth out fear: because fear hath torment. He that feareth is not made perfect in love.” (1 John 4:18)

Peace Begets Love

We are all at rest with the things we love. "Great peace have they which love thy law: and nothing shall offend them.” (Psalm 119:165) A sparkling young child who is at peace with his father worships the man and strives to imitate him. Through the lad's tender eyes, his father's character is unflawed. His skill is unmatched. Even the brand of vehicle he drives is the best, and he emulates his every action. Even though every father knows the limitations of his son's expectations, we all bask in the seasonal loyalty. It is knowledge and fear that undermines this loyal love. An abusive father will destroy such childhood esteem and fear will be its replacement. It was through base fear that the evil servant buried his talent and did not trade with it. In his eyes his master was austere and to be feared. But God has not given us the spirit of fear but of love.

“We love him, because he first loved us. If a man say, I love God, and hateth his brother, he is a liar: for he that loveth not his brother whom he hath seen, how can he love God whom he hath not seen?” (1 John 4:19, 20) The soul who is affected by this love cannot but imitate it. He is at great peace with his Father’s love and the eyes through which he views his Father's character can only enlist replication. However dire the circumstances we may find ourselves in, this spirit of love and peace will carry us through whatever opposition we may meet with on life's pathway. Jacob made nothing of the hard service he was to endure for Rachel; the spirit of love to God will set us above the fear of man, and all the hurt that a man can do us.

Thankfulness Begets a Sound Mind

We do not need to study happy souls long to find buried within the bedrock of each one, a foundation of gratitude. The spirit of a sound mind, or quietness of mind, is a peaceable enjoyment of life. We are oftentimes discouraged in our way when the features of our environment do not measure not up to our own fancy and imagination. A mere sober, solid, thinking mind would obviate and defuse such fruitless notions, yet we are all tempted to entertain formidable ingratitude. It takes no brainpower to expose things we disdain, for Satan is certain to magnify and outline every unsatisfactory detail we encounter. We each may think ourselves into a deep cave, but we must thank ourselves out.

Fear of losing our health, wealth, reputation, and happiness is the biggest hindrance to securing it. To focus on our pain is to invite more. To be constantly analyzing our life to see if we are being fulfilled is a sure avenue to ingratitude. The world is constantly asking, "Are we having fun yet?" The answer is, "No". To these souls, life will never be adequate, and they must wander forth seeking the bigger fulfillment that the last one did not secure. It is the fear that we are not receiving our fair allotment in life that breeds discontentment. It is discontentment that produces more fear, and the downward spiral progresses. Such was the consternation of the soul who asked Christ to speak to his brother to divide the inheritance with him. This may be logical thinking, but it is not conducive to a sound and peaceable mind. This offended soul has no root in himself and will forever be wronged in some fashion and spend his days in search of a savior to come and fix the other party. “... neither fear ye their fear, nor be afraid. Sanctify the LORD of hosts himself; and let him be your fear, and let him be your dread.” (Isaiah 8:12, 13)

There is no earthly level of attainment or perfect environment that will promote a sound mind. It can only be secured through prayer, peace, and thankfulness. This may take some reprogramming of our minds to reach into the subconscious recesses, but we must soberly gird up the loins of our minds and exercise them if we ever hope to obtain “the grace that is to be brought unto you at the revelation of Jesus Christ;” (1 Peter 1:13)

“And the peace of God,
which passeth all understanding,
shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus.
Finally, brethren, whatsoever things are true,
whatsoever things are honest, whatsoever things are just,
whatsoever things are pure, whatsoever things are lovely,
whatsoever things are of good report;
if there be any virtue, and if there be any praise,
think on these things.

— Philippians 4:7, 8
